Commentary on the interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra. This is a Book which We have sent down to you, that you might bring mankind out of darkness into light, by the permission of their Lord, to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾ (14:1).

Abu Ja'far al-Tabari said: The explanation of the meaning of His words "Alif-Lam-Ra" has already been given earlier, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary. [See what preceded: vol. 1, pp. 205–224.]

* *

As for His words ﴿A Book which We have sent down to you﴾, their meaning is: This is a Book which We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, meaning the Qur'an. ﴿That you might bring mankind out of darkness into light﴾ means: that you may guide them by it from the darkness of error and disbelief to the light of faith and its radiance, and make clear to those in ignorance and blindness the paths of right guidance and direction. [See the lexicographical references for the words of this verse in the earlier indexes.]

His words ﴿by the permission of their Lord﴾ mean: by the enabling of their Lord for them in this, and His kindness toward them. [See the explanation of "permission" (al-idhn) earlier, p. 476, note 3, and the references there.] ﴿To the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾ means: to the straight path of God, which is His religion that He has approved and prescribed for His creation. [See the explanation of "the path" (al-sirat) earlier, vol. 12, p. 556, note 3, and the references there.

And the explanation of "the Almighty" has been omitted here; see what preceded in vol. 15, p. 373, note 2, and the references there.]

* *

As for ﴿al-Hamid﴾, it is of the form "fa'il", derived from the form "maf'ul" and changed into "fa'il"; its meaning is: the one praised for His bounties. [See the explanation of "al-Hamid" earlier, vol. 5, p. 570; vol. 9, p. 296; vol. 15, p. 400.]

* *

God, exalted is His remembrance, attributed the bringing of people out of darkness into light, by the permission of their Lord who enabled them for that, to His Prophet ﷺ, who is the guide of His creation and the one who grants success to whomever among them He loves for faith, since it is from him that they are called to it and informed of what benefits and harms them therein. Thereby, the soundness of the view of the people of affirmation (ahl al-ithbat), who attribute the actions of servants to them as acquisition (kasb), and to God, may His praise be exalted, as origination and governance, is made clear; and the corruption of the view of the people of predestination (ahl al-qadar), who deny that God has any part in that, is shown. [Ahl al-ithbat are the People of the Sunnah who affirm the divine attributes. Ahl al-qadar are the Mu'tazila and those who deny predestination.]

* *

Those of the exegetes said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

2055) Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿to bring mankind out of darkness into light﴾: i.e., from error to guidance.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 2:

The explanation of His, may His remembrance be exalted, words ﴿Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed regarding the recitation of this.

The majority of the reciters of Medina and Syria recited it: "Allahu alladhi lahu ma fi as-samawat" with the word "Allah" in the nominative, as a beginning (mubtada'), and made His words ﴿alladhi lahu ma fi as-samawat﴾ its predicate (khabar).

* *

The majority of the reciters of Iraq, Kufa and Basra recited: ﴿Allahi alladhi﴾ with "Allah" in the genitive, following what comes after it ﴿al-'Azizi al-Hamidi﴾, and both are genitive.

* *

The grammarians differed in its interpretation when it was recited in this way.

It is related from Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' that he used to recite it in the genitive, and he would say: its meaning is: "by the permission of their Lord, to the path of [Allah] the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, He to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens." [[I added what is between the brackets because it is required for the sense of the speech; otherwise the meaning would not stand as "the postponed which means the preposed," as will come, but would be redundant and extended, which is invalid. It is an omission due to the haste of the copyist and a slip of the pen.]] He would say: it is of the postponed (al-mu'akhkhar) which means the preposed (al-taqdim), and he illustrates it with the saying of the speaker: "I passed by the handsome 'Abd Allah," where the phrase that is placed in the position of the noun is the epithet (na't), and then the noun is placed in the position of the epithet, so its case-ending follows the case-ending of the epithet that was placed in the position of the noun, as one of the poets said:

"Had I been possessed of a bow and a shizib, I would not have feared the assaults of the wicked wolf." [[The metre escaped my memory. "Shizib" and "shizba" (with a fatha and then a sukun) are names for the bow, referring to one that is neither new nor worn, as if its branch had wilted, i.e., dried up. "Shadda" (with a fatha on the shin) means an attack; one says "he charged at the enemy," i.e., attacked.]]

* *

As for al-Kisa'i, it is related from him that he said: whoever read it in the genitive intended to make it one speech, and made the genitive follow the genitive, and it was with the genitive that he recited.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known recitations, each of which has been recited by leading reciters, and their meaning is one; so whichever one the reciter reads, he is correct.

It is also possible that the one who read it in the nominative intended the meaning of the one who read it in the genitive, in following the speech of one part by another, but he put it in the nominative because it is separated from the verse before it, as His, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties﴾ to the end of the verse, then He said: ﴿The repentant, the worshippers﴾ [Surah at-Tawbah: 111, 112]. [[See what Abu Ja'far said about the verse, previously 14:500, note no. 2.]]

* *

The meaning of His words ﴿Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ is: Allah, who owns all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth.

He says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: We have sent down to you this Book so that you may call My servants to the worship of One who has this description, and abandon the worship of whoever does not own for them or for himself any harm or benefit, of the deities and idols. Then He, may His remembrance be exalted, threatened whoever disbelieved in Him and did not respond to the call of His Messenger to what he called them to, of sincere monotheism toward Him, saying: ﴿And woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment﴾. He says: it is the valley that flows with the pus of the people of Hell, for whoever denies His oneness and worships another alongside Him, from the severe punishment of Allah. [[See the explanation of "woe" (al-waylu) previously, 2:267-269, 237.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 3:

The interpretation of the words of the Mighty and Majestic One: ﴿Those who prefer the worldly life over the Hereafter, and bar (people) from the way of Allah, and seek to make it crooked. Those are in far-off error.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His majesty be exalted, ﴿Those who prefer the worldly life over the Hereafter﴾, He means: those who choose the worldly life, its enjoyments, and acts of disobedience to Allah therein, over obedience to Allah and the deeds beneficial in the Hereafter that bring them closer to His pleasure [[See the explanation of "istihbab" (preferring) above, 14:175.]] = ﴿and bar (people) from the way of Allah﴾, meaning: they prevent those who wish to believe in Allah and follow His Messenger in what he brought from Allah, from believing in Him and following him [[See the explanation of "sadd" (barring) above, p. 467, note 2, and the references there.

= And the explanation of "sabil" (way) in the linguistic indexes above.]] = ﴿and seek to make it crooked﴾, meaning: they seek to distort the way of Allah = which is His religion with which He sent His Messenger = ﴿crooked﴾: distortion and alteration through lies and falsehood. [[See the explanation of "ibtigha'" (seeking) above, 15:285, note 2, and the references there.

= And the explanation of "awaj" (crookedness) above, 15:285, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

"Al-'iwaj" with a kasra on the ʿayn and a fatha on the waw is used for religion, land, and everything that is not upright. As for everything that is upright, such as a wall, a spear, or a tooth, it is said "'awaj" with a fatha on both the ʿayn and the waw. [[For another explanation of "awaj," see above, 12:448. See also Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubaydah, 1:335, where there is an error.]]

* *

The Mighty One says: ﴿Those are in far-off error﴾, meaning these disbelievers who prefer the worldly life over the Hereafter. He says: they are far away from the truth, taking a path other than guidance, and deviating from the straight way. [[See the explanation of "dalal" (error) above in the linguistic indexes.]]

* *

The scholars of Arabic have differed concerning the reason for the use of "ʿala" (over) in His words ﴿over the Hereafter﴾. Some grammarians of Basra said: the verb is connected with "ʿala," as it is said "darabuhu fi al-sayf" (they struck him with the sword), meaning "bi al-sayf," because all these particles may be connected with the verb and omitted, as in the Arabs' saying "nazaltu Zaydan" and "marartu Zaydan," meaning "marartu bihi" and "nazaltu ʿalayhi."

* *

Others said: it was introduced because the verb carries the meaning of another verb [[His words "yu'addi ʿan ma'nahu min al-af'al," i.e., it implies the meaning of another verb.]]. In His words ﴿they prefer the worldly life﴾ the meaning is "they prefer the worldly life over the Hereafter," and therefore "ʿala" was introduced.

I have explained this and its parallels in other places in this book, sufficiently to avoid repetition. [[See "Discussions of grammar and Arabic and other matters," above in the parts of this book.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 4:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people, to make [the message] clear for them. Then Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Exalted is He, says: And We did not send to any nation of the nations, O Muhammad, before you and before your people, a messenger except in the language of the nation to which We sent him, and their tongue. ﴿To make [it] clear for them﴾ means: to make them understand what Allah sent him with of His command and prohibition, so that the proof of Allah is established against them. Then guidance and misguidance are in the hand of Allah: He forsakes from accepting what His messenger brought from Him whomever He wills of them, and grants success in accepting it to whomever He wills. Therefore "fa-yudilla" is in the nominative, because it is intended as a new clause and not as a conjunction with what precedes it, as it was said: ﴿That We may make clear to you, and We cause to remain in the wombs what We will﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 5]. ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾ [[See the explanation of "al-'Aziz" above, about five hundred and eleven, footnote 4, and the references there.]] who is not prevented from what He wills of misguidance or guidance for whomever He wills it for. ﴿The Wise﴾, in His granting success to faith to whomever He grants it to, and His guidance of whomever He guides to Himself, and His leaving astray of whomever He leaves astray from Himself, and in other of His arrangements. [[See the explanation of "al-Hakim" above in the language indexes.]]

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil said things like what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

20560 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people﴾, meaning in the tongue of his people, whatever it was. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿To make [it] clear for them﴾ [what was sent to them], so that He establishes the proof thereby. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Then Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 5:

The interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs, [saying], "Bring your people out from darknesses into the light and remind them of the days of Allah. Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We certainly sent Moses with Our proofs and evidences before you, O Muhammad, just as We sent you to your people with the like of such proofs and evidences. [See the explanation of "ayah" (sign) in what preceded in the indices of language (ayy).] As follows:

20561 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih =H [This is the first time the symbol (H) is used in this manuscript. It is a convention of the hadith scholars and others, meaning: transfer of the chain (tahwil al-isnad), i.e., narrating the report with another chain before completing the statement.] And al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan al-Ashyab related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, from Abu Najih, from Mujahid =H [This is the first time the symbol (H) is used in this manuscript. It is a convention of the hadith scholars and others, meaning: transfer of the chain (tahwil al-isnad), i.e., narrating the report with another chain before completing the statement.] And al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Shababa related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs﴾ he said: with the clear proofs.

20562 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs﴾ he said: the nine signs, the flood and what accompanied it.

20563 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿We sent Moses with Our signs﴾ he said: the nine clear signs.

20564 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Bring your people out from the darknesses into the light﴾, as We sent down this Book to you, O Muhammad, to bring people out from darknesses into the light by the permission of their Lord. By His words (... bring your people out from the darknesses into the light) is meant: call them, [In the printed edition: "i.e., call them", a mistake in transmission; the intended reading is: "call them", so that they come out from misguidance into guidance, by omission and abbreviation.] from misguidance to guidance, and from disbelief to faith, as follows:

20565 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs, [saying] bring your people out from the darknesses into the light﴾ he says: from misguidance to guidance.

20566 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Hisham related to us, from Amr, from Sa'id, from Qatada, the like of it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And remind them of the days of Allah﴾, He, exalted and majestic, says: Admonish them with what preceded of blessings bestowed upon them in the days that passed, so the mention of "the days" suffices for the mention of the blessings intended, because they were days known to them, in which Allah bestowed great blessings upon them: He rescued them in them from the family of Pharaoh after they had been in the humiliating torment, drowned their enemy Pharaoh and his people, and made them inheritors of their land, their homes and their wealth.

* *

Some of the people of the Arabic language said: its meaning is: frighten them with what befell 'Ad and Thamud and their like of punishment, and with pardon for others. He said: and in meaning it is like your saying: "Take them with severity and gentleness."

* *

Others among them said: We have found evidence for naming blessings "days" in their speech. Then he cited for that the verse of Amr ibn Kulthum:

"And days for us, bright and long, when we disobeyed the king in them, refusing to submit."

[From his famous outstanding ode, see Sharh al-Qasa'id al-Sab' of Ibn al-Anbari: 388.]

He said: So perhaps he only called them "bright and long" for their bestowing benefits upon people in them. He said: So this is evidence for the one who said: ﴿And remind them of the days of Allah﴾ meaning the blessings of Allah. Then he said: It may also be that calling them "bright" refers to their superiority over the king and their refusal of him, so their days are bright for them and long against their enemies. [This is undoubtedly the statement of Abu 'Ubayda, in my opinion; Ibn al-Anbari quoted it verbatim from him in Sharh al-Sab' al-Tiwal: 389, from the beginning of the page to the seventh line, with variation in the order of statements. It is also undoubtedly from his book "Majaz al-Qur'an", though I did not find it in the printed edition 1: 335, in the interpretation of this surah, nor anywhere other than this place. I almost assert that the copy of Majaz al-Qur'an has lost something at the beginning of the interpretation of "Surat Ibrahim", as indicated by the comments of its editor, my virtuous brother Professor Muhammad Fu'ad Sezgin. What al-Tabari transmitted is unattributed, while what Ibn al-Anbari transmitted attributed to Abu 'Ubayda should be placed in this location of the book. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. See what will come: 535, note 4.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The one who said this, that this verse is evidence that "days" means blessings, has no valid argument. For Amr ibn Kulthum only described the days as "bright" because of his tribe's honour in them and their refusal to submit to the king in obedience, and that is like people's saying: "Such-and-such never had a white day," meaning by it: he never had a day remembered for good. As for his describing them as long, they are only described as long in a time of hardship, as al-Nabigha said:

"Leave me to a concern, O Umayma, weary, and to a night I endure, slow in its stars."

[His Diwan: 42, the opening of the Nabigha's ode, praising Amr ibn al-Harith al-A'raj when he fled to Syria from al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir; the verse will come in the interpretation after 14:15 / 23:106 (Bulaq).]

So Amr only described them as long because of the severity of their hardship upon the enemies of his people. There is no basis for that other than what I have said.

* *

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

20568 - Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Habib ibn al-Shahid related to me, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Ubayd al-Mukattib, from Mujahid: ﴿And remind them of the days of Allah﴾ he said: with the blessings of Allah. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful﴾. He says: Indeed in the days that passed, with My blessings upon them, meaning upon the people of Moses, are ﴿signs﴾, meaning: lessons and admonitions. [See the explanation of "ayah" in what preceded in the indices of language (ayy).] ﴿For everyone patient and grateful﴾: he says: for everyone who is patient in obedience to Allah and grateful to Him for the blessings He has bestowed upon him. [See the explanation of "patience" in what preceded, 13: 35, note 4, and the references there.

And the explanation of "gratitude" in what preceded, 3: 212, 213.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 6:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And [remember] when Moses said to his people, "Remember the favour of God upon you when He saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who inflicted upon you the worst torment, slaughtering your sons and sparing your women. And in that was a great trial from your Lord."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And remember, O Muhammad, when Moses son of 'Imran said to his people, the Children of Israel: ﴿Remember the favour of God upon you﴾, which He bestowed upon you, ﴿when He saved you from the people of Pharaoh﴾, meaning: when He saved you from the people of Pharaoh's religion and obedience to him [[See the explanation of "al-inja'" (deliverance) in what has preceded: 15:53, 194, 195.]]; ﴿who inflicted upon you the worst torment﴾, meaning: who made you taste the most severe torment [[See the explanation of "al-sawm" (inflicting) in what has preceded: 2:40/13, 85; then Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubaydah, 1:335. And the explanation of "su' al-'adhab" (the worst torment) in what has preceded: 2:40/13:85.]], ﴿and slaughtered your sons﴾, together with making you taste the most severe torment, [they slaughtered] your sons. [[From "together with making you taste..." is omitted in the printed edition, and "[they slaughtered]" between brackets is omitted in the printed edition.]]

* *

The conjunction "and" (wa) has been placed in this position because His words ﴿and slaughtered your sons﴾ are intended to inform that the people of Pharaoh tortured the Children of Israel with kinds of torment other than slaughter, and also with slaughter. In another place in the Qur'an, however, it came without the "and": ﴿who inflicted upon you the worst torment, slaughtering your sons﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 49] in one place, and in another place ﴿killing your sons﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 141]. The "and" was not inserted in the places where it was not, because His words ﴿slaughtering﴾ and His words ﴿killing﴾ are intended to specify the characteristics of the torment they were inflicting upon them. The same applies to every sentence whose elaboration is intended: without the "and" when it is elaboration, and when it is intended to be joined to what precedes it by something other than it and not as elaboration, then with the "and." [[In the printed edition: "fa-al-waw" (then the "and"); the manuscript's reading has not been correctly transcribed.]]

* *

20582. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Ibn 'Uyaynah, regarding His words ﴿And [remember] when Moses said to his people, "Remember the favour of God upon you"﴾: the bounties of God upon you and His days. [[Report 20582: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr ibn 'Isa al-Humaydi, mentioned before under numbers 9914 and 11622. I have extended the discussion about his lineage in Jamharat Ansab Quraysh by al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar, 1:449, note 1. To this may be added: al-Intiqa' by Ibn 'Abd al-Barr, p. 104, and the beginning of Musnad al-Humaydi, which was recently printed in India.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿and spare your women﴾, it means: they let your women live, leaving off killing them; and that sparing of theirs was for them [[See the explanation of "al-istihya'" (sparing) in what has preceded: 2:41-48 / 13:41, 85.]]. The meaning is: they leave them alive, and "al-hayah" (life) here is leaving off, and from it comes the report narrated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said:

"Kill the elders of the polytheists, and spare their youths (shurkh)," [[This report was related by Ahmad in his Musnad in two places, 5:12, 20, in the Musnad of Samurah ibn Jundab, through the route of Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-Hajjaj, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Samurah. Then through the route of Hushaym, from Hajjaj ibn Arta'ah, from Qatadah, and in this second one he said: "and spare their youths (istabqu shurkahum)."

Abu Dawud related it in his Sunan, 3:73, through the route of Sa'id ibn Mansur, from Hushaym, from Hajjaj.

al-Tirmidhi related it in the chapter on campaigns (abwab al-siyar), "Chapter on what has come concerning submitting to judgement," through the route of Abu al-Walid al-Dimashqi, from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah. He said: "This is a good, strange hadith, and al-Hajjaj ibn Arta'ah related it from Qatadah in similar form." In it: "and spare" (wa-istahyu). Then he said: "al-shurkh: the boys who have not grown up (lam yunbitu)."

'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad said (Musnad 5:12): "I asked my father about the explanation of this hadith: 'Kill the elders of the polytheists?' He said: It means: the elder is hardly ever Muslim, whereas the youth, i.e., he becomes Muslim; it is as if he is closer to Islam than the elder. He said: al-shurkh, the youths."]] meaning: spare them, so do not kill them.

* *

﴿And in that was a great trial from your Lord﴾: He, exalted is He, says: And in what the people of Pharaoh did to you of kinds of torment, there was a great trial for you from your Lord, meaning a test and examination for you from your Lord, which is great. [[See the explanation of "al-bala'" (trial) in what has preceded: 15, 250, note 4, and the references there.]] "Al-bala'" in this place may also mean a blessing (ni'mah), and it may mean the trial which befalls people through hardships. [[In the printed edition: "And its meaning may be the trial which may befall people in hardships and other things." He added to the sentence whatever his whim wished and other things; he erred, may God forgive him.]]

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And [remember] when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you; but if you are ungrateful, indeed My punishment is severe﴾ (14:7).

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, says: Remember also when your Lord made it known to you (ta'dhdhana rabbukum).

* *

"Ta'adhdhana" is of the form "tafa''ala" from "adhana." The Arabs sometimes use the form "tafa''ala" in place of "af'ala," as they say "awda'tuhu" and "tawa''adtuhu," with the same meaning. "Adhana" means "a'lama" (to inform). [[See the explanation of "adhana" in what has preceded, 13:204, and then the explanation of "al-idhn" in the indices of language earlier. Then see Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:345.]] As al-Harith ibn Hilliza said:

*Asma' has announced to us her parting, / Many a dweller whom lingering wearies him.*
[[The opening of his well-known long ode; see Sharh al-Qasa'id al-sab' of Ibn al-Anbari: 433.]]

By his words "adhanatna" (announced to us), he means "a'lamatna" (informed us).

* *

It is related from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he used to recite: ﴿Wa-idh taadhdhana rabbukum﴾ as "wa-idh qala rabbukum" (and when your Lord said):

20583 - al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from him.
[[Report 20583: "al-Harith" is Al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah, named after his grandfather; he is Al-Harith ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Usamah al-Tamimi, a teacher of al-Tabari, trustworthy, mentioned several times before, the last at no. 14333.

"'Abd al-'Aziz" is 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Aban al-Umawi, a wicked liar who fabricated hadith, mentioned many times before, the last at no. 14333.]]

20584 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And when your Lord proclaimed﴾, "and when your Lord said," that is the "ta'adhdhun" (proclamation).

* *

As for His words: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾, He means: If you are grateful to your Lord, by obeying Him in what He commanded you and forbade you, I will surely increase you in His favours toward you and His blessings upon you, beyond what He has already given you of deliverance from the people of Pharaoh and rescue from their torment.

* *

Another view has been stated on this, namely what was narrated:

20585 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: I heard 'Ali ibn Salih say, regarding the words of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾, he said: "That is, of My obedience."

20586 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: I heard 'Ali ibn Salih, and he mentioned something similar.

20587 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾, he said: "Of My obedience."

20588 - al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Mughul narrated to us, from Aban ibn Abi 'Ayyash, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾, he said: "Of My obedience."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: There is no intelligible sense in this view, because no mention of obedience has preceded in this context, so that it could be said: "If you thank Me for it, I will increase you in it." Rather, the mention preceding this verse was a report of Allah's favour upon the people of Musa, through His words: ﴿And when Musa said to his people: Remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾; then He informed them that if they thanked Him for this favour, He would increase them. So the sound meaning of the statement is that He would increase them from His favours, not from something whose mention has not preceded, namely "obedience," unless it is meant: "If you are grateful and obey Me by being thankful, I will increase you in the means of gratitude that help you to it," in which case that would be a valid reading.

* *

As for His words: ﴿But if you are ungrateful, indeed My punishment is severe﴾, He means: And if you, O people, are ungrateful for Allah's favour, denying it by abandoning thanks for it and opposing His command and prohibition, and committing His disobediences, [then] ﴿indeed My punishment is severe﴾: I will punish you as I punish whoever among My creatures disbelieves in Me.

* *

Some of the Basran grammarians said, regarding the meaning of His words: ﴿And when your Lord proclaimed﴾, "ta'adhdhana rabbukum," that "idh" (when) is among the superfluous particles. [[This is Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:345.]] We have already demonstrated the invalidity of that view earlier. [[See what preceded, 1:439–444; and add to the references on p. 439, note 1, that this statement of Abu 'Ubaydah is in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:36, 37.]]

**The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And Moses said, "If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on earth entirely, then indeed Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy."﴾ (14:8)**

Abu Ja'far said: His, the Exalted's, saying means: Moses said to his people, "If you disbelieve, O people, and deny the blessing of Allah that He has bestowed upon you, you [and those who are on earth entirely will do the same as your deeds]," meaning that whoever is on earth entirely will act as you act. ﴿Then indeed Allah is Free of need﴾ from you and from them, from all of His creation, having no need for your thanks for His blessings from all of you [[See the explanation of "al-Ghani" (the Free of need) above, 15:145, note 2, and the references there.]] ﴿Praiseworthy﴾, meaning One who is praised by His creation for what He has bestowed upon them [[See the explanation of "al-Hamid" (the Praiseworthy) above, shortly before, 512, note 1, and the references there.]], as related:

20589. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hashim related to us, saying: Sayf informed us, from Abu Rawq, from Abu Ayyub, from Ali: regarding ﴿Then indeed Allah is Free of need﴾, he said: "Free of need of His creation," and ﴿Praiseworthy﴾, he said: "One who is praised by them" [[In Asas al-Balagha: "Istahmada Allah ila khalqihi, bi-ihsanihi ilayhim, wa-in'amihi 'alayhim" (He was praised by Allah's creation for His goodness toward them and His bounty upon them). The verb "istahmada" was previously mentioned in another report, no. 8349, in volume 7, page 470, and it is something that should be noted in the major lexicons such as Lisan al-Arab, Taj al-Arus, and similar works.]]

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) on the words of Allah Most High: **﴿Has there not come to you the report of those before you, the people of Noah, ʿAad, and Thamud, and those after them, whom none knows but Allah? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they put their hands to their mouths and said: "We disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and we are truly in grave doubt about that to which you call us."﴾ (14:9)**

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, is reporting what Musa said to his people: "O my people, **﴿has there not come to you the report of those before you﴾**," meaning the news of the nations that passed away before you, **﴿the people of Noah, ʿAad and Thamud﴾**. The people of Noah is a clarifying apposition (tabyin) for "those," and ʿAad is conjoined to "the people of Noah" [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "and the people of ʿAad, so he clarified with them 'those'," which is meaningless; the copyist erred. His meaning is that "the people of Noah" is a substitute (badal) for "those," and "tabyin" is the substitution. Al-Akhfash mentioned this (Hamʿ al-Hawamiʿ 2:125). It is also called tafsir (explanation), as I mentioned in volume 12:7, note 1, and it is also called takrir (repetition) (Hamʿ al-Hawamiʿ 2:125).]]. **﴿And those after them﴾** means after the people of Noah, ʿAad and Thamud. **﴿Whom none knows but Allah﴾** means: none can count their number or know their extent except Allah, as follows:

20590. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymun, regarding **﴿and ʿAad and Thamud and those after them, whom none knows but Allah﴾**, he said: "The genealogists have lied." [[The reports 20590–20593 were cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 4:71, who also attributed them to ʿUbayd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim. The chain of this report is sound.]]

20591. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Israʾil narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymun, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, with the like of that.

20592. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababa narrated to us, saying: Israʾil informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymun, who said: Ibn Masʿud told us that he used to recite it: "waʿadan wa-Thamuda wal-ladhina min baʿdihim la yaʿlamuhum illa Allah," and then he would say: "The genealogists have lied."

20593. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymun, from ʿAbd Allah, the like of that. [[Note on 20593: "Ibn al-Muthanna" is Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-ʿAnazi, the memorizer known as al-Zaman, Tabari's teacher, from whom Tabari narrated countless reports; he has been mentioned many times (see 2734, 2740, 5440, 10314). "ʿIsa ibn Jaʿfar" here is an undoubted error; the correct reading is "Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Hudhali," who is Ghundar. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated from him in many places in the tafsir, too numerous to count. Consider the chains already mentioned, for example: 35, 101, 194, 208, 419 in the first volume of the tafsir, and in the eighth volume: 8761, 8810, 8863, 8973, where "al-Muthanna" appears and the correct form is "Ibn al-Muthanna." There are many other examples.]]

* *

As for His words, **﴿Their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾**, He means: these nations were visited by their messengers, whom Allah sent to them, calling them to devote worship sincerely to Him. **"With clear proofs"** means with arguments and evidences for the truth of what they called them to, in the form of miracles. [[See the explanation of "clear proofs" (al-bayyinat) in volume 13:14, note 2, and the references there. In the printed edition it reads: "meaning with evident arguments and manifest proofs of the truth of what they called them to, miracles," which adds a great deal of worthless padding; it seems he did not understand Abu Ja'far's text, so he tried to clarify it with what is both bad and burdensome.]]

* *

As for His words, **﴿so they put their hands to their mouths﴾**, the people of interpretation (ta'wil) differed about its meaning. Some of them said: its meaning is that they bit their fingers in rage at the messengers' call to what the messengers called them to.

Those who said this:

20594. Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbd Allah: **﴿so they put their hands to their mouths﴾**, he said: "They bit them in rage."

20595. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbd Allah, regarding His words **﴿so they put their hands to their mouths﴾**, he said: "In rage," and he did thus, and bit his hand.

20596. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nuʿaym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbd Allah: **﴿so they put their hands to their mouths﴾**, he said: "They bit them." [[Reports 20594–20596: the report of "Sufyan al-Thawri, from Abu Ishaq" was cited by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2:351 via ʿAbd al-Razzaq; here it is number 20595. Its wording in al-Mustadrak is:

"ʿAbd Allah said: thus, and he put his hand in his mouth and bit his hand, and said: They bit their fingers in rage."

Al-Hakim said: "This is a sound hadith with the addition, according to the conditions of the two shaykhs (Bukhari and Muslim)," and al-Dhahabi agreed.

al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 4:72, and attributed it also to ʿAbd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Abu ʿUbayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani. al-Haythami cited it in Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid 7:43 and said: "al-Tabarani narrated it from his shaykh, ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Saʿid ibn Abi Maryam, who is weak." Neither he nor al-Suyuti mentioned the hadith with al-Hakim's addition.

The report of Sufyan al-Thawri and Israʾil will come under number 20603.]]

20597. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Rajaʾ al-Basri narrated to us, saying: Israʾil narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbd Allah, regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: **﴿so they put their hands to their mouths﴾**, he said: "They bit their fingers." [[Report 20597: "Israʾil" is Israʾil ibn Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq al-Sabiʿi, who narrated from his grandfather; he has been mentioned countless times. "ʿAbd Allah ibn Rajaʾ ibn ʿAmr al-Ghadani al-Basri" is trustworthy, and his reports from Israʾil were good; his biography was given at 2814, 2939, 16973. This report was narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak via ʿUbayd Allah ibn Musa from Israʾil, and he said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two shaykhs, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed. It will come via Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri from Israʾil and Sufyan together under number 20603. See the takhrij of the preceding reports.]]

20598. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbd Allah: **﴿so they put their hands to their mouths﴾**, he said: "They bit the tips of their fingers." [[Report 20598: this is a third route for the report of Abu al-Ahwas from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud: "Sharik, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbd Allah." See the preceding reports.]]

20599. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Hubayra, from ʿAbd Allah, that he said regarding this verse: **﴿so they put their hands to their mouths﴾**, he said: "That he puts his finger in his mouth."

20600. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, both saying: Abu Qatan narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Hubayra, from ʿAbd Allah, regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: **﴿so they put their hands to their mouths﴾**, and Shuʿba placed the tips of his left fingers on his mouth.

20601. al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn ʿAbbad narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq informed us, from Hubayra, who said: ʿAbd Allah said **﴿so they put their hands to their mouths﴾**, he said: "Thus," [[i.e., he gestured. The meaning of "qala" (he said) in this sense has been explained many times before.]] and he inserted his fingers into his mouth.

20602. al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAffan narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq said: Informed us from Hubayra, from ʿAbd Allah, that he said about this verse **﴿so they put their hands to their mouths﴾**, he said: Abu ʿAli said: ʿAffan showed us, inserting the tips of the fingers of his open palm into his mouth, and he mentioned that Shuʿba had shown him thus. [[Reports 20599–20602: these three are another route for the report of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, from the hadith of Hubayra from him. "Abu Qatan" is ʿAmr ibn al-Haytham ibn Qatan al-Zubayri, Abu Qatan al-Basri, trustworthy, in the fourth tabaqa of Shuʿba's students, mentioned at 18674, 20091, 20420. "Yahya ibn ʿAbbad al-Duba'i," Abu ʿAbbad, was one of Ahmad's shaykhs; and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah al-Zaʿfarani is trustworthy, but weak. Mentioned at 20010, 20091. "Hubayra ibn Maryam al-Shabbami" is a trustworthy Successor who narrated only from Abu Ishaq al-Sabiʿi, mentioned at 3001, 5468.]]

20603. Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan and Israʾil narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbd Allah: **﴿so they put their hands to their mouths﴾**, he said: "They bit their fingertips." Sufyan said: "They bit in rage." [[Report 20603: see the commentary on the preceding reports.]]

20604. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words **﴿so they put their hands to their mouths﴾**, and then recited: "They bite their fingertips at you out of rage" (Surat Aal ʿImran: 119), and said: "This is it: **﴿they put their hands to their mouths﴾**." He said: "They inserted their fingers into their mouths." And he said: "When a person is enraged, he bites his hand." [[In the printed edition: "and he said: the meaning of: they put their hands to their mouths," which tampers with the wording and gravely misrepresents it.]]

* *

Others said: rather, the meaning is that when they heard the Book of Allah they were astonished by it, and placed their hands over their mouths.

Those who said this:

20605. Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: **﴿so they put their hands to their mouths﴾**, he said: "When they heard the Book of Allah, they were amazed, and they returned their hands to their mouths."

* *

Others said: rather, the meaning is that they denied them with their mouths.

Those who said this:

20606. Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid. = And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: **﴿so they put their hands to their mouths﴾**, he said: "They returned their words to them and denied them."

20607. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababa narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of that.

20608. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of that.

20609. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words **﴿Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, so they put their hands to their mouths﴾**, he said: "Their people denied their messengers and rejected what they brought of clear proofs, and rejected them with their mouths, and said: 'We are truly in doubt about that to which you call us, grave doubt.'"

20610. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, regarding His words **﴿so they put their hands to their mouths﴾**, he said: "They rejected what the messengers brought."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It seems that Mujahid directed His words **﴿so they put their hands to their mouths﴾** toward the meaning: "they rejected the favors (ayadi) of Allah, which, had they accepted them, would have been favors and blessings for them, but they did not accept them." He directed His words **﴿to their mouths﴾** toward the meaning "with their mouths," meaning with their tongues, which are in their mouths. [[See what was mentioned before: 515, note 6.]]

* *

It has been reported from some Arabs by hearing: "Allah admit you with the Garden (bil-jannah)," meaning: into the Garden. And he recited this verse [[I do not know its composer. The one who recited it is al-Farra', as in Lisan al-ʿArab (fya).]]:

"And I am averse to her (fiha) from Luqayt and his kin...
but as for Sinbis, I am not averse (to her)."

[[Lisan al-ʿArab (fya). It will come in the tafsir 17:105 (Bulaq). Al-Farra' recited it in Lisan al-ʿArab thus: "And I am averse to her from ʿUbayd and his kin, but as for Sinbis, I am not averse to her."]]

He means: "and I am averse by her (wa-arghab bi-ha)," meaning: by a daughter of his, [[In the printed edition: "He means: 'and I am averse in her,' meaning 'I am averse by her from Luqayt'," which misread the manuscript, since the manuscript has "and I am averse in her" rather than "and I am averse by her," and because "bint" was written with an unpointed open ta, which he misread, altered, and misled. There is no power or strength except through Allah.]] "from Luqayt, and I am not averse by her from my tribe."

* *

Others said: rather, the meaning is that they used to place their hands over the mouths of the messengers, rejecting their words and denying them.

* *

Others said: this is a figure of speech (mathal), and what is meant is that they refrained from what they were commanded to say of the truth, [[In Abu ʿUbayda's Majaz al-Qur'an the word is "bi-qawlihi" (with his saying), rather than "bi-qabulihi" (with his acceptance), so I adopted it. I did not adopt what is in the manuscript and printed edition, nor what agreed with them in Fath al-Bari (8:285), because Abu Ja'far's statement afterward: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has told us that they said: ..." is evidence of its correctness.]] and did not believe in it or submit to it. And he said: It is said of a man who holds back from answering and does not respond: "He put his hand in his mouth." And some of them mentioned that the Arabs say: "I spoke to so-and-so about a need, and he put his hand in his mouth," when he falls silent and does not answer. [[This is the statement of Abu ʿUbayda in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:336, but in the printed Majaz it is very abbreviated, and this part of the Majaz seems disordered and has gaps, as I explained at p. 519, note 2.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This also is a statement without merit, because Allah, Mighty is His remembrance, has told us that they said: "We disbelieve in that with which you were sent," so they had answered with denial.

* *

Abu Ja'far said:

The most likely of these statements to be correct in the interpretation of this verse, in my view, is the statement we mentioned from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud: that they put their hands to their mouths and bit them in rage at the messengers, just as Allah, Majestic and Mighty, described their brothers among the hypocrites, saying: **﴿And when they are alone, they bite the tips of their fingers at you out of rage﴾** (Surat Aal ʿImran: 119). This is the well-known expression and the understood meaning of "returning the hand to the mouth."

* *

As for His words **﴿and they said: "We disbelieve in that with which you were sent"﴾**, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: and they said to their messengers: "We disbelieve in that with which He who sent you sent you, namely the call to abandon the worship of idols and images," **﴿and we are truly in doubt﴾** about the reality of what you call us to, namely the monotheism of Allah, **﴿grave (murib)﴾**, meaning: that doubt makes us uneasy, that is, it compels us to unease and suspicion regarding it.

* *

This is derived from: "arab al-rajul" (the man became suspicious), when he committed something causing suspicion, "yurib irabah" (he causes suspicion). [[See the explanation of "rayb" (doubt) in the lexical indexes earlier (r-y-b), and the explanation of "irabah" earlier at 15:370, 493.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 10:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Their messengers said: "Is there any doubt about God, the Originator of the heavens and the earth? He calls you that He may forgive you of your sins and defer you until a specified term." They said: "You are only human beings like us. You want to turn us away from what our fathers used to worship, so bring us a clear authority."﴾ (14:10)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the messengers of the nations to whom their messengers came said: ﴿Is there any doubt about God?﴾ [[In the manuscript: "Is there any doubt about the people?" which is an error on his part.]] That is, that He is the one who deserves from you, O people, divinity and worship to the exclusion of all His creation. ﴿Doubt﴾ — and His words: ﴿the Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ mean: the Creator of the heavens and the earth. [[See the explanation of "fatara" in what has preceded: 287, footnote 2, and the references there.]] ﴿He calls you that He may forgive you of your sins﴾ means: He calls you to His monotheism and obedience. ﴿That He may forgive you of your sins﴾ means: He will conceal for you some of your sins by pardoning them, so He will not punish you for them. [[See the explanation of "al-maghfirah" in what has preceded in the language indices (gh-f-r), then see Abu 'Ubaydah's Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 336, on the explanation of the addition of "min" in the verse.]] ﴿And defer you﴾ means: He will extend your lifespans, so He will not punish you immediately and destroy you, but will defer you until the time He has written in the Umm al-Kitab, at which He will take you, which is the term He has named for you. [[See the explanation of "al-ajal" in what has preceded: 476, footnote 4, and the references there. And the explanation of "musamma" in what has preceded: 326, footnote 1, and the references there.]] Then the nations said to them: ﴿You are only﴾ — O people — ﴿human beings like us,﴾ in form and appearance, and you are not angels. [[See the explanation of "bashar" in what has preceded, vol. 15: 295, footnote 2, and the references there.]] And you intend by this statement of yours, which you say to us, ﴿to turn us away from what our fathers used to worship﴾ — that is, you only intend by your words to turn us away from worshipping the idols that our fathers used to worship. [[See the explanation of "al-sadd" in what has preceded: 515, footnote 2, and the references there.]] ﴿So bring us a clear authority﴾ — that is, bring us a proof for what you say that makes clear to us its reality and its soundness, so that we may know that you are right in what you say. [[See the explanation of "al-sultan" in what has preceded: 106, footnote 1, and the references there. And the explanation of "mubin" in what has preceded in the language indices (b-y-n).]]

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari), Jami' al-Bayan, on Surah 14, verse 11:

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of the words of the Exalted, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿Their messengers said to them: "We are only mortals like you, but Allah bestows His favour upon whom He wills of His servants. It was not for us to bring you any authority except by Allah's leave. And upon Allah let the believers rely."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: The peoples to whom the messengers came said to their messengers: [[In the printed edition: "قال الأمم التي أتتهم الرسل لرسلهم"، وهو لا يفهم، وفي المخطوطة: "قالت الأمم التي أتتهم الرسل رسلهم"، وصوابها "للأمم"، و"رسلهم" فاعل "قالت". Translation: In the printed edition it reads "qal al-umam allati atathum al-rusul li-rusulihim," which is not understood; in the manuscript it reads "qalat al-umam allati atathum al-rusul rusulahum," and its correct form is "lil-umam," with "rusulahum" as the subject of "qalat."]] ﴿We are only mortals like you﴾, meaning: You have spoken truly in what you said, that you are only mortals like us. We are indeed only mortals of the children of Adam, human beings like you. [[See the explanation of "al-bashar" above, shortly before: 537, note 5.]] = ﴿But Allah bestows His favour upon whom He wills of His servants﴾, meaning: But Allah graces with His bounty whom He wills of His creation, guiding him and granting him success in the truth, and preferring him over many of His creatures. = ﴿It was not for us to bring you any authority﴾, meaning: It was not for us to bring you a proof and evidence for what we call you to. = ﴿except by Allah's leave﴾, meaning: except by Allah's command to us to do so. [[See the explanation of "al-idhn" above: 526, note 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾, meaning: And in Allah let those who believe in Him and obey Him place their trust, for we trust in Him and rely upon Him. [[See the explanation of "al-tawakkul" above: 166, note 2, and the references there.]]

20610 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿So bring us a clear authority﴾, he said: "The clear authority" is the proof and the evidence. And regarding His words ﴿for which He has sent down no authority﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 151 / Surah al-A'raf: 7 / Surah al-Hajj: 71], he said: a clear sign and proof.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verses 12–14:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted be His remembrance: ﴿And why should we not put our trust in Allah, when He has guided us to our ways? We will surely endure patiently whatever harm you inflict upon us. And upon Allah let those who trust rely.﴾ (12)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted be His remembrance, says, reporting the saying of the messengers to their peoples: ﴿And why should we not put our trust in Allah﴾, that is, trust in Him and in His sufficiency and His defending you against us? ﴿And He has guided us to our ways﴾, meaning: He has made clear to us the path of salvation from His punishment, and has shown us [[See the explanation of "guidance" (hudā) in the earlier indexes of language (h-d-y), and the explanation of "way" (sabīl) in the indexes (s-b-l).]] ﴿And we will surely endure patiently whatever harm you inflict upon us﴾, for God's sake and for what we meet from you of hardship because of our calling you to what we call you to, [[See the explanation of "harm" (adhā) above, vol. 14, p. 324, note 1, and the references there.]] namely, disavowal of idols and images and sincere worship of Him. ﴿And upon Allah let those who trust rely﴾, meaning: upon Allah let those rely who are confident in Him from among His creatures; as for those who are disbelievers in Him, their guardian is Satan.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted be His remembrance: ﴿And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, "We will surely expel you from our land, or you must return to our religion." So their Lord revealed to them, "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers, and We will surely settle you in the land after them. That is for whoever fears My standing [before Me] and fears My threat."﴾ (13–14)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted be His remembrance, says: And those who disbelieved in Allah said to their messengers, whom they had been sent to, when they called them to the oneness of Allah and sincere worship of Him, and to forsaking the worship of gods and idols, ﴿"We will surely expel you from our land"﴾, meaning: from our country, so that we drive you out of it; ﴿"or you must return to our religion"﴾, meaning: unless you return to our religion, which we follow, of worshipping idols. [[See the explanation of "religion" (millah) above, vol. 1, p. 101, note 1, and the references there; and see Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubaydah, vol. 1, p. 336.]]

* *

The lam was introduced into His saying ﴿"you must return" (la-ta'uddunna)﴾, and it has the sense of a condition, as if it were the answer to an oath; the meaning of the speech is: "We will surely expel you from our land, or you will return to our religion."[[In the printed edition: "aw ta'udun", and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

* *

The meaning of "or" (aw) here is the meaning of "except" (illa) or the meaning of "until" (hatta), as one says in speech: "I will surely strike you, or you confess to me." Among the Arabs, some make what follows "or" in such a position a conjunction of what came before it: if what came before it is jussive, they make it jussive, and if it is accusative, they make it accusative, and if it has a lam, they make it have a lam, since "or" is a conjunctive particle. Others put the verb after "or" in the accusative in every case, so that by its accusative it is known to be cut off from what precedes it, as Imru' al-Qays said:

My companion wept when he saw the road before him, and was certain that we would be overtaken at Caesar's;
So I said to him: "Do not let your eye weep; we only seek a kingdom, or die and be excused."[[From his famous ode, which he composed on a journey to Caesar seeking his aid after the killing of his father. His companion whom he mentioned is 'Amr ibn Qami'ah al-Yashkuri, whom he took with him to Caesar. "Al-Darb" is the pass between Tarsus and the land of the Romans.]]

So he put "die and be excused" in the accusative, while he made "seek" nominative, because he intended the meaning: "except that we die," or "until we die." From the same usage is the saying of another:

I cannot be weaned from her love, or love would do to me other than what it has done.[[The verse is by al-Ahwas ibn Muhammad al-Ansari, though it is sometimes attributed to Majnun. Al-Aghani 4:299; Diwan Majnun: 200. Our teacher Adil Sulayman traced the verses of al-Ahwas in what he collected of his poetry, which has not yet been published.]]

As for His saying ﴿"So their Lord revealed to them, 'We will surely destroy the wrongdoers'"﴾, the wrongdoers are those who wronged themselves, [[See the explanation of "revealed" (awḥā) above, vol. 6, p. 405; vol. 9, p. 399; vol. 11, pp. 217, 290, 371, 533.]] so they incurred for themselves God's punishment by their disbelief. It is also permissible that they were called "wrongdoers" for worshipping what it is not permitted to worship, such as idols and gods, [[See the explanation of "wrong" (ẓulm) above, vol. 1, pp. 523–524; vol. 2, pp. 369, 519; vol. 4, p. 584; vol. 5, p. 384, and elsewhere in the indexes of language.]] so that by placing worship in other than its proper place, which is wrongdoing, they were named thus.[[In the printed edition: "sammū bi-dhālika ẓālimīn" (they were named thereby "wrongdoers"), adding what has no substance, since it did not conform to the wording of Abu Ja'far, so it obscured it for him.]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿"and We will surely settle you in the land after them"﴾, this is a promise from God to whichever of His prophets He promised victory over the disbelievers among their people. It means: when the peoples of the messengers persisted in disbelief and threatened their messengers with harming them, God revealed to them the destruction of those among their peoples who disbelieved in them, and promised them victory. All of this was from God as a warning and threat to the polytheists of the people of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) for their disbelief in him, their audacity toward his messenger, and as a confirmation for Muhammad (ﷺ), and a command to him to be patient over what he met of harm from his people's polytheists, just as those before him among the steadfast messengers were patient, and as making known that the outcome for whoever disbelieves in Him is destruction, and that their outcome for the one who is victorious over them is victory; this is the custom of God concerning those who passed away before.

* *

Narrated to us by Bishr, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿"and We will surely settle you in the land after them"﴾: He said: He promised them victory in this world, and Paradise in the Hereafter.

* *

As for His saying ﴿"That is for whoever fears My standing [before Me] and fears My threat"﴾, He, may His praise be exalted, says: Thus is My action toward whoever fears His standing before Me, and fears My threat, so he obeys Me and fears Me, and avoids My wrath: I will help him against whoever intends him harm and seeks to bring him hardship from My enemies; I will destroy his enemy, disgrace him, and make him inherit their land and their dwellings.

* *

And His saying ﴿"for whoever fears My standing [before Me]"﴾ has the meaning I have stated: that it is for whoever fears standing before Me, where I will set him there for reckoning, [[See Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubaydah, vol. 1, p. 337.]] as He said: ﴿"And you make your provision that you deny [it]"﴾ [Surah al-Waqi'ah: 82], meaning: "And you make My provision to you that you deny." This is because the Arabs attribute their actions to themselves and to what they act upon, saying: "I was delighted by your seeing, and by my seeing you," and so likewise is this.

Al-Aghani 4:299; Diwan Majnun: 200. Our teacher Adil Sulayman traced the verses of al-Ahwas in what he collected of his poetry, which has not yet been published.]]

As for His saying ﴿"So their Lord revealed to them, 'We will surely destroy the wrongdoers'"﴾, the wrongdoers are those who wronged themselves, [[See the explanation of "revealed" (awḥā) above, vol. 6, p. 405; vol. 9, p. 399; vol. 11, pp. 217, 290, 371, 533.]] so they incurred for themselves God's punishment by their disbelief. It is also permissible that they were called "wrongdoers" for worshipping what it is not permitted to worship, such as idols and gods, [[See the explanation of "wrong" (ẓulm) above, vol. 1, pp. 523–524; vol. 2, pp. 369, 519; vol. 4, p. 584; vol. 5, p. 384, and elsewhere in the indexes of language.]] so that by placing worship in other than its proper place, which is wrongdoing, they were named thus.[[In the printed edition: "sammū bi-dhālika ẓālimīn" (they were named thereby "wrongdoers"), adding what has no substance, since it did not conform to the wording of Abu Ja'far, so it obscured it for him.]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿"and We will surely settle you in the land after them"﴾, this is a promise from God to whichever of His prophets He promised victory over the disbelievers among their people. It means: when the peoples of the messengers persisted in disbelief and threatened their messengers with harming them, God revealed to them the destruction of those among their peoples who disbelieved in them, and promised them victory. All of this was from God as a warning and threat to the polytheists of the people of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) for their disbelief in him, their audacity toward his messenger, and as a confirmation for Muhammad (ﷺ), and a command to him to be patient over what he met of harm from his people's polytheists, just as those before him among the steadfast messengers were patient, and as making known that the outcome for whoever disbelieves in Him is destruction, and that their outcome for the one who is victorious over them is victory; this is the custom of God concerning those who passed away before.

* *

Narrated to us by Bishr, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿"and We will surely settle you in the land after them"﴾: He said: He promised them victory in this world, and Paradise in the Hereafter.

* *

As for His saying ﴿"That is for whoever fears My standing [before Me] and fears My threat"﴾, He, may His praise be exalted, says: Thus is My action toward whoever fears His standing before Me, and fears My threat, so he obeys Me and fears Me, and avoids My wrath: I will help him against whoever intends him harm and seeks to bring him hardship from My enemies; I will destroy his enemy, disgrace him, and make him inherit their land and their dwellings.

* *

And His saying ﴿"for whoever fears My standing [before Me]"﴾ has the meaning I have stated: that it is for whoever fears standing before Me, where I will set him there for reckoning, [[See Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubaydah, vol. 1, p. 337.]] as He said: ﴿"And you make your provision that you deny [it]"﴾ [Surah al-Waqi'ah: 82], meaning: "And you make My provision to you that you deny." This is because the Arabs attribute their actions to themselves and to what they act upon, saying: "I was delighted by your seeing, and by my seeing you," and so likewise is this.

**The interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And they sought victory, and every obstinate tyrant was lost.﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the messengers sought victory over their peoples, meaning they asked God for help against them [[See the explanation of "al-istiftah" (seeking victory or opening) in what has preceded: 2:254 / 10:405, 406, and Majaz al-Quran (Abu 'Ubaydah's Quranic metaphors) 1:337.]] = ﴿and every obstinate tyrant was lost﴾. He says: every arrogant, oppressive person who deviated from acknowledging the Oneness of God and sincerely worshipping Him perished.

* *

"Al-'anid," "al-'athid," and "al-'anud" have the same meaning. [[See the explanation of "'anid" in what has preceded: 15:366, 367, and Majaz al-Quran 1:337.]]

* *

From "al-jabbar" one says: he is a jabbar, clearly displaying al-jabbariyyah, al-jabriyyah, al-jabarut, and al-jabarut. [[See the explanation of "jabbar" in what has preceded: 10, 172 / 11:470 / 15:366.

Note: in the printed edition, the text reads: "he is a jabbar, clearly displaying al-jabbariyyah, al-jabarutiyyah, al-jabarut, and al-jabarut." It added in the language something not supported by the text, namely "al-jabarutiyyah," and omitted one of the five forms, "al-jabarut." In the manuscript, in place of the second "al-jabriyyah," there is "al-jabr nabbih," undotted and badly written.]]

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things in agreement with what we have said on this.

Ibn Zayd used to say, regarding the meaning of His words: ﴿And they sought victory﴾, something contrary to the view of these people, and he would say: rather, it was the nations who sought victory, and they were answered.

He said: so the seeking victory was punishment. He said: it was said to them: "Indeed, for this there is a term!" when they asked God to send it down upon them, so He said: ﴿Rather, We delay them until a day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾. [[This is a derivation from a verse of Surat Ibrahim: 42.]] And they said: "We do not want to be delayed until the Day of Resurrection": ﴿Our Lord, hasten for us our share (qittana) of punishment﴾ ﴿before the Day of Reckoning﴾ [Surat Sad: 16]. And he recited: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment, and had there not been a term appointed, the punishment would have come upon them﴾, until he reached: ﴿And from beneath their feet, and it will be said: Taste what you used to do﴾ [Surat al-'Ankabut: 53–55].

**Commentary of al-Ṭabarī (Jāmiʿ al-Bayān) on Sūrah 14, verses 16–17 (part 1 of 2)**

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿Before him is Hell, and he will be given to drink festering water (ṣadīd)﴾ (16), ﴿which he will sip, but will scarcely be able to swallow. Death will come at him from every place, yet he will not die; and before him is a severe punishment﴾ (17).**

Abū Jaʿfar (al-Ṭabarī) said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿min warāʾihi﴾ means "in front of every tyrant," ﴿jahannam﴾ means "Hell," which they will approach (yaridūnahā).

* * *

In this context, *warāʾ* means "in front of," as one says: "Indeed death is *min warāʾika*," meaning "in front of you." It is also as the poet said:
[[This is Jarīr.]]
*"Do you threaten me in front of the Banū Riyāḥ? You have lied; your hands will fall short of reaching me."* [[The verse, its takhrīj and its explanation are mentioned earlier: p. 399, note 3. Then see Majāz al-Qurʾān by Abū ʿUbayda, 1:337.]]
He means: "in front of the Banū Riyāḥ," before them and facing them.

* * *

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: By His words ﴿min warāʾihi﴾ He means "in front of him," because it is behind what he is in. As one says to you, "All of this is *min warāʾika*," meaning it will come upon you, and it is behind what you are in, because what you are in had already happened before, and it is behind it. And He said: ﴿Behind them was a king who seized every boat by force﴾ [Sūrat al-Kahf: 79], in this sense, meaning that what was behind them was in front of them.

* * *

Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: This is most permissible regarding times, because time passes over you, so it becomes behind you once you have passed it. Likewise ﴿there was behind them a king﴾, because they pass it, so it becomes behind them.

* * *

Some of them used to say: It is among the words with opposite meanings (*ḥurūf al-aḍdād*), meaning *warāʾ* can be both "in front" and "behind."

* * *

His words ﴿and he will be given to drink of festering water﴾ mean: he will be given to drink of water. Then He clarified that water, exalted is His praise, and what it is, saying: it is *ṣadīd*. Therefore *al-ṣadīd* was made to agree in its case-ending (iʿrāb) with *al-māʾ*, because it is a clarification (*bayān*) of it. [[*Al-bayān* is ʿaṭf al-bayān (explicative apposition), which the Kufans call *al-tarjama*, as mentioned earlier. See the index of terms.]]

* * *

*Al-ṣadīd* is pus and blood.

* * *

And the people of interpretation (*ahl al-taʾwīl*) explained it likewise.

His words ﴿which he will sip (yatajarraʿuhu)﴾ mean: he will sip it slowly (yataḥassāh). ﴿But will scarcely be able to swallow (yusīghuhu)﴾ means: he will scarcely be able to gulp it down, because of its extreme repulsiveness, though he is made to swallow it because of severe thirst.

* * *

The Arabs use "*lā yakād*" (scarcely/hardly) both for what has been done and for what has not been done. As for what has been done, this is an example, because Allah, exalted is His praise, made that a drink for them. As for what has not been done, in which *kāda* (to nearly do) is used, His words are: until ﴿when he extends his hand, he can hardly see it﴾ [Sūrat al-Nūr: 40], so he does not see it. [[For the explanation of *kāda* see earlier: 2:218–219; 13:131.]]

* * *

In line with what we have said, that the meaning of His words ﴿and scarcely able to swallow it﴾ is that he does swallow it, a report came from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Mention of the narration to that effect:

20631 – Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Ibrāhīm Abū Isḥāq al-Ṭāliqānī narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us, from Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr, from Abū Umāma, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His words ﴿and he will be given to drink of festering water, which he will sip﴾: "When he drinks it, it cuts up his intestines until it comes out from his posterior." Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿and they will be given boiling water, which cuts their intestines to pieces﴾ [Sūrat Muḥammad: 15], and He says: ﴿And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten metal that scalds the faces; what a wretched drink﴾ [Sūrat al-Kahf: 29]. [[The two reports, 20631 and 20632: Ibrāhīm, Abū Isḥāq al-Ṭāliqānī, is Ibrāhīm ibn Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā al-Ṭāliqānī al-Bannānī, sometimes called Ibrāhīm ibn ʿĪsā after his grandfather. He was a client of the Banānah clan, trustworthy (thiqa), one of Aḥmad's teachers, who heard from Ibn al-Mubārak and Baqiyya. Al-Ṭāliqān (with the lām unvocalized, though it may be vocalized with a fatḥa) is a town in Khurasan. He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 1/1/273, Ibn Abī Ḥātim in two places 1/1/86, 119, and Tārīkh Baghdād 6:24.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak is one of the great imams, and has been mentioned many times.
Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr ibn Harim al-Sakkasikī is trustworthy, reliable and dependable; he has been mentioned several times, including 7009, 12194, 12807, 13108.
ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr, in diminutive form, is so here and in Aḥmad's Musnad and in Tirmidhī's Sunan. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr appears in al-Ḥākim's al-Mustadrak and Abū Nuʿaym's Ḥilyat al-Awliyāʾ. In Ibn Kathīr, quoting the Musnad, it is "ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bishr," which is a misreading.
This report through Ibn al-Mubārak from Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr was narrated by Aḥmad in his Musnad from ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak (Musnad 5:265).
Tirmidhī narrated it from Suwayd ibn Naṣr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak (in the chapter on what has come concerning the description of the drink of the people of the Fire).
Abū Nuʿaym narrated it in Ḥilya 8:182 through several chains: Nuʿaym ibn Ḥammād from Ibn al-Mubārak; Muʿādh ibn Asad from Ibn al-Mubārak; Yaḥyā al-Ḥimmānī from him; and Muḥammad ibn Muqātil from him: four chains.
Al-Ḥākim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2:31 through ʿAbdān, who is ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Jabala, from Ibn al-Mubārak, and said: "This is a sound hadith according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabī agreed with him.
There is a discussion about ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr. Tirmidhī said, after mentioning the report: "This is a strange (gharīb) hadith. Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl said thus: 'from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr,' and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr is not known except in this hadith. Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr, the Companion of the Prophet (ﷺ), other than this hadith. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr had a brother who heard from the Prophet (ﷺ), and his sister heard from the Prophet (ﷺ). And ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr, from whom Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr narrated the hadith of Abū Umāma, is the brother of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr."
I say: I did not find what Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Bukhārī said in his al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr.
As for Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilya, he said: "Ṣafwān alone narrated it from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr. It was said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bishr, who is al-Yaḥṣubī al-Ḥimṣī, with the kunya Abū Saʿīd. Baqiyya ibn al-Walīd narrated it from Ṣafwān similarly. Ṣafwān narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr al-Māzinī, who had companionship (ṣuḥba), and from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bishr, and for this reason it was confused for some people. This one is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr."
Al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar said in al-Tahdhīb, and quoted what Tirmidhī said: "Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr, also said ʿAbd Allāh, narrated from Abū Umāma, and from him Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr narrated. Al-Ṭabarānī said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr al-Yaḥṣubī, from Abū Umāma, and he narrated this hadith to him, and another hadith through Baqiyya from Ṣafwān, and Allah knows best. Abū Mūsā al-Madīnī mentioned in Dhayl al-Ṣaḥāba: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr, the brother of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr, as said by al-Salmānī." What al-Ḥāfiẓ quoted from Ibn Abī Ḥātim is found in al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl 2/2/308.
But it is strange that the imam and hafiẓ Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Bukhārī did not include a biography of ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr in his al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr or al-Ṣaghīr, despite what Tirmidhī quoted from him, which gives the impression that it is in one of them. What is in it is: "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr al-Sulamī, then al-Māzinī, from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)" (al-Kabīr 3/1/14). Then he mentioned "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr," who is not al-Māzinī, al-Jubrānī; this one narrates from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr al-Māzinī, the Companion, and from Abū Umāma al-Bāhilī. (Also biographed in al-Tahdhīb.)
The reference that almost explicitly points to this report in the Book of al-Bukhārī is in the biography of "ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bashīr ibn Jarīr al-Bajalī," where he said: "from Abū Umāma, may Allah be pleased with him, from Ibn al-Mubārak, from Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr, al-Shāmī." I do not know how this is, because Ibn Abī Ḥātim gave a biography of "ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr" in al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl 2/2/308, number 1467, then the next, number 1468, he said: "ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bashīr ibn Jarīr al-Bajalī (narrated from ...), from whom Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq narrated. I heard my father say that, and he says: he is unknown (majhūl)."
Likewise al-Dhahabī did in Mīzān al-iʿtidāl 2:164, and said: "ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr: Ḥimṣī, from Abū Umāma, and from him Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr alone; he is not known." It is said he is "ʿAbd Allāh the Companion," and it is also said he is "ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr al-Ḥabrānī, the Successor (tābiʿī), and this is more apparent." Then he mentioned after "ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bashīr al-Bajalī," and said: "There is obscurity in him; Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq narrated from him, and no one else."
It is almost clear that what occurred in al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr (3/1/374–375) is a mixing of two different biographies, and that the beginning of the biography of "ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr" has fallen out of the printed edition of al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr, and part of it has merged into another biography. And His saying: ﴿And death will come to him from every place, but he will not die﴾. 20634 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿He will gulp it down, but will hardly swallow it.
