And His saying: ﴿And behind him is a severe punishment﴾, meaning: and beyond what he is in of punishment, i.e., before him and in front of him [[See the explanation of "wara'" (behind/beyond) in what has passed: 546, 475, note 1.]] ﴿a severe punishment﴾. [[See the explanation of "al-ghaliz" (severe) in what has passed: 7:341 / 14:360, 576 / 15:366.]]

**Commentary of al-Ṭabarī (Jāmiʿ al-Bayān) on Sūrah 14, verses 16–17 (part 1 of 2)**

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿Before him is Hell, and he will be given to drink festering water (ṣadīd)﴾ (16), ﴿which he will sip, but will scarcely be able to swallow. Death will come at him from every place, yet he will not die; and before him is a severe punishment﴾ (17).**

Abū Jaʿfar (al-Ṭabarī) said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿min warāʾihi﴾ means "in front of every tyrant," ﴿jahannam﴾ means "Hell," which they will approach (yaridūnahā).

* * *

In this context, *warāʾ* means "in front of," as one says: "Indeed death is *min warāʾika*," meaning "in front of you." It is also as the poet said:
[[This is Jarīr.]]
*"Do you threaten me in front of the Banū Riyāḥ? You have lied; your hands will fall short of reaching me."* [[The verse, its takhrīj and its explanation are mentioned earlier: p. 399, note 3. Then see Majāz al-Qurʾān by Abū ʿUbayda, 1:337.]]
He means: "in front of the Banū Riyāḥ," before them and facing them.

* * *

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: By His words ﴿min warāʾihi﴾ He means "in front of him," because it is behind what he is in. As one says to you, "All of this is *min warāʾika*," meaning it will come upon you, and it is behind what you are in, because what you are in had already happened before, and it is behind it. And He said: ﴿Behind them was a king who seized every boat by force﴾ [Sūrat al-Kahf: 79], in this sense, meaning that what was behind them was in front of them.

* * *

Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: This is most permissible regarding times, because time passes over you, so it becomes behind you once you have passed it. Likewise ﴿there was behind them a king﴾, because they pass it, so it becomes behind them.

* * *

Some of them used to say: It is among the words with opposite meanings (*ḥurūf al-aḍdād*), meaning *warāʾ* can be both "in front" and "behind."

* * *

His words ﴿and he will be given to drink of festering water﴾ mean: he will be given to drink of water. Then He clarified that water, exalted is His praise, and what it is, saying: it is *ṣadīd*. Therefore *al-ṣadīd* was made to agree in its case-ending (iʿrāb) with *al-māʾ*, because it is a clarification (*bayān*) of it. [[*Al-bayān* is ʿaṭf al-bayān (explicative apposition), which the Kufans call *al-tarjama*, as mentioned earlier. See the index of terms.]]

* * *

*Al-ṣadīd* is pus and blood.

* * *

And the people of interpretation (*ahl al-taʾwīl*) explained it likewise.

Mention of those who said that:

20626 – Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us. And al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us. – And al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: Shabāba narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us – from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His words ﴿from festering water﴾, he said: pus and blood.

20627 – al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, the like of it.

20628 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, regarding His words ﴿and he will be given to drink of festering water﴾: *al-ṣadīd* is what flows from his flesh and skin. [[The report 20628: in the printed edition it reads "from his blood, flesh and skin," with an addition; I have kept what is in the manuscript, which agrees with what is in al-Durr al-Manthūr 4:74.]]

20629 – al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda, regarding His words ﴿and he will be given to drink of festering water﴾, he said: what flows from between his flesh and skin.

20630 – al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Isḥāq narrated to us, saying: Hishām narrated to us, from one he named, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, ﴿and he will be given to drink of festering water﴾, he said: By *al-ṣadīd* is meant what comes out of the inside of the disbeliever, mixed with pus and blood.

* * *

His words ﴿which he will sip (yatajarraʿuhu)﴾ mean: he will sip it slowly (yataḥassāh). ﴿But will scarcely be able to swallow (yusīghuhu)﴾ means: he will scarcely be able to gulp it down, because of its extreme repulsiveness, though he is made to swallow it because of severe thirst.

* * *

The Arabs use "*lā yakād*" (scarcely/hardly) both for what has been done and for what has not been done. As for what has been done, this is an example, because Allah, exalted is His praise, made that a drink for them. As for what has not been done, in which *kāda* (to nearly do) is used, His words are: until ﴿when he extends his hand, he can hardly see it﴾ [Sūrat al-Nūr: 40], so he does not see it. [[For the explanation of *kāda* see earlier: 2:218–219; 13:131.]]

* * *

In line with what we have said, that the meaning of His words ﴿and scarcely able to swallow it﴾ is that he does swallow it, a report came from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Mention of the narration to that effect:

20631 – Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Ibrāhīm Abū Isḥāq al-Ṭāliqānī narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us, from Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr, from Abū Umāma, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His words ﴿and he will be given to drink of festering water, which he will sip﴾: "When he drinks it, it cuts up his intestines until it comes out from his posterior." Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿and they will be given boiling water, which cuts their intestines to pieces﴾ [Sūrat Muḥammad: 15], and He says: ﴿And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten metal that scalds the faces; what a wretched drink﴾ [Sūrat al-Kahf: 29]. [[The two reports, 20631 and 20632: Ibrāhīm, Abū Isḥāq al-Ṭāliqānī, is Ibrāhīm ibn Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā al-Ṭāliqānī al-Bannānī, sometimes called Ibrāhīm ibn ʿĪsā after his grandfather. He was a client of the Banānah clan, trustworthy (thiqa), one of Aḥmad's teachers, who heard from Ibn al-Mubārak and Baqiyya. Al-Ṭāliqān (with the lām unvocalized, though it may be vocalized with a fatḥa) is a town in Khurasan. He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 1/1/273, Ibn Abī Ḥātim in two places 1/1/86, 119, and Tārīkh Baghdād 6:24.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak is one of the great imams, and has been mentioned many times.
Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr ibn Harim al-Sakkasikī is trustworthy, reliable and dependable; he has been mentioned several times, including 7009, 12194, 12807, 13108.
ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr, in diminutive form, is so here and in Aḥmad's Musnad and in Tirmidhī's Sunan. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr appears in al-Ḥākim's al-Mustadrak and Abū Nuʿaym's Ḥilyat al-Awliyāʾ. In Ibn Kathīr, quoting the Musnad, it is "ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bishr," which is a misreading.
This report through Ibn al-Mubārak from Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr was narrated by Aḥmad in his Musnad from ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak (Musnad 5:265).
Tirmidhī narrated it from Suwayd ibn Naṣr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak (in the chapter on what has come concerning the description of the drink of the people of the Fire).
Abū Nuʿaym narrated it in Ḥilya 8:182 through several chains: Nuʿaym ibn Ḥammād from Ibn al-Mubārak; Muʿādh ibn Asad from Ibn al-Mubārak; Yaḥyā al-Ḥimmānī from him; and Muḥammad ibn Muqātil from him: four chains.
Al-Ḥākim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2:31 through ʿAbdān, who is ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Jabala, from Ibn al-Mubārak, and said: "This is a sound hadith according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabī agreed with him.
There is a discussion about ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr. Tirmidhī said, after mentioning the report: "This is a strange (gharīb) hadith. Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl said thus: 'from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr,' and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr is not known except in this hadith. Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr, the Companion of the Prophet (ﷺ), other than this hadith. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr had a brother who heard from the Prophet (ﷺ), and his sister heard from the Prophet (ﷺ). And ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr, from whom Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr narrated the hadith of Abū Umāma, is the brother of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr."
I say: I did not find what Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Bukhārī said in his al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr.
As for Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilya, he said: "Ṣafwān alone narrated it from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr. It was said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bishr, who is al-Yaḥṣubī al-Ḥimṣī, with the kunya Abū Saʿīd. Baqiyya ibn al-Walīd narrated it from Ṣafwān similarly. Ṣafwān narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr al-Māzinī, who had companionship (ṣuḥba), and from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bishr, and for this reason it was confused for some people. This one is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr."
Al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar said in al-Tahdhīb, and quoted what Tirmidhī said: "Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr, also said ʿAbd Allāh, narrated from Abū Umāma, and from him Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr narrated. Al-Ṭabarānī said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr al-Yaḥṣubī, from Abū Umāma, and he narrated this hadith to him, and another hadith through Baqiyya from Ṣafwān, and Allah knows best. Abū Mūsā al-Madīnī mentioned in Dhayl al-Ṣaḥāba: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr, the brother of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr, as said by al-Salmānī." What al-Ḥāfiẓ quoted from Ibn Abī Ḥātim is found in al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl 2/2/308.
But it is strange that the imam and hafiẓ Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Bukhārī did not include a biography of ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr in his al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr or al-Ṣaghīr, despite what Tirmidhī quoted from him, which gives the impression that it is in one of them. What is in it is: "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr al-Sulamī, then al-Māzinī, from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)" (al-Kabīr 3/1/14). Then he mentioned "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr," who is not al-Māzinī, al-Jubrānī; this one narrates from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bisr al-Māzinī, the Companion, and from Abū Umāma al-Bāhilī. (Also biographed in al-Tahdhīb.)
The reference that almost explicitly points to this report in the Book of al-Bukhārī is in the biography of "ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bashīr ibn Jarīr al-Bajalī," where he said: "from Abū Umāma, may Allah be pleased with him, from Ibn al-Mubārak, from Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr, al-Shāmī." I do not know how this is, because Ibn Abī Ḥātim gave a biography of "ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr" in al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl 2/2/308, number 1467, then the next, number 1468, he said: "ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bashīr ibn Jarīr al-Bajalī (narrated from ...), from whom Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq narrated. I heard my father say that, and he says: he is unknown (majhūl)."
Likewise al-Dhahabī did in Mīzān al-iʿtidāl 2:164, and said: "ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr: Ḥimṣī, from Abū Umāma, and from him Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr alone; he is not known." It is said he is "ʿAbd Allāh the Companion," and it is also said he is "ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr al-Ḥabrānī, the Successor (tābiʿī), and this is more apparent." Then he mentioned after "ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bashīr al-Bajalī," and said: "There is obscurity in him; Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq narrated from him, and no one else."
It is almost clear that what occurred in al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr (3/1/374–375) is a mixing of two different biographies, and that the beginning of the biography of "ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Bisr" has fallen out of the printed edition of al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr, and part of it has merged into another biography. What supports this is that Ibn Abī Ḥātim, who mentioned both biographies, did not address this in his book Bayān Khaṭaʾ Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Bukhārī fī Tārīkhihi; had such a thing been in the original of al-Bukhārī's Tārīkh, it would not have escaped Ibn Abī Ḥātim. So what Tirmidhī quoted from al-Bukhārī's al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr is what has dropped from the printed edition.]]

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) on the words of the Exalted, ﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes which the wind blows hard upon on a stormy day. They have no power over anything of what they have earned. That is the far-straying error.﴾ (14:18)

Abu Ja'far said: The grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyya, the scholars of Arabic grammar) differed concerning the element that makes "mathal" (likeness) nominative (raf').

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is as if he said: "And among what We relate to you is the likeness of those who disbelieve," and then he went on explaining, as in His words ﴿The likeness of Paradise﴾ (13:35). This is common.

* *

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The likeness belongs to the deeds, but the Arabs put the nouns first because they are more definite, and then they bring the predicate concerning which they inform, along with its companion. The meaning of the speech is: "The likeness of the deeds of those who disbelieve in their Lord is like ashes," as it was said: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, their faces blackened﴾ (39:60). The meaning of the speech is: "And on the Day of Resurrection you will see the faces of those who lied about God blackened." He said: If "al-a'mal" (the deeds) were put in the genitive, it would be permissible, as in His words ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it﴾ (2:217), and His words ﴿The likeness of Paradise which the God-fearing have been promised: rivers flow beneath it﴾ (13:35). He said: "Tajri" (flows) is in the position of the predicate, as if he said: "that it flows," and "that such-and-such should be," and if he introduced "an" (that), it would be permissible. He said: From this is the saying of the poet:

"Leave me alone, for your command will not be obeyed,
and you will not find me to be one whose forbearance is wasted."

He said: "Forbearance" is put in the accusative by "alfaytu" (I found), through repetition (al-takrir). He said: If it were in the nominative, it would be correct. He said: This is a likeness that God struck for the deeds of the disbelievers. He said: The likeness of the deeds of those who disbelieved, on the Day of Resurrection, which they used to do in the world, claiming that they intended God by them, is the likeness of ashes upon which the wind blew on a day of stormy wind, so it scattered it and carried it away. Likewise the deeds of those who disbelieve in Him on the Day of Resurrection: they will find nothing of them that benefits them with God, so that it rescues them from His punishment, because they did not do them purely for God, but associated with them idols and images.

God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿That is the far-straying error﴾, meaning: their deeds which they used to do in the world, in which they associated partners with God, are deeds done without guidance and rectitude, but rather in deviation from guidance, far away, and in a severe path not straight.

* *

It was said: ﴿On a stormy day﴾: so the day is described as stormy, and that belongs to the attribute of the wind, because the wind is in it, as one says "a cold day" and "a hot day," because cold and heat occur in it. (See the explanation of "stormy" in what has preceded, 15:51.) As the poet said:

"Two cloudy days and a sunny day..."

He described the two days as cloudy, and clouds only occur in them. It is also possible that what is meant is: "on a stormy day of wind," and "the wind" was omitted because it had been mentioned before. This would be like the saying of the poet:

"When there comes a day dark in its sun, eclipsing..."

He means: "eclipsing the sun." It was also said: It is an adjective of "the wind" alone, but since it came after "the day," it took its i'rab (grammatical case). That is because the Arabs make the genitive follow the genitive in adjectives, as the poet said:

"She shows you a face of a noble lineage, unblemished,
smooth, with no mole or scar upon it."

Here "ghayr" (unblemished) is in the genitive by following the case of "al-wajh" (the face), though it is actually an adjective of "al-sunna" (the lineage/the sheen). The meaning is: "the sheen of a face unblemished." Similarly they said: "This is the hole of a ruined lizard."

* *

Those who interpreted the Qur'an said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

20636 - Al-Qasim told us, al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words ﴿like ashes which the wind blows hard upon﴾: He said: The wind carried it away on a stormy day.

20637 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, my father told me, my paternal uncle told me, my father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes which the wind blows hard upon on a stormy day﴾: He says: Those who disbelieved in their Lord and worshipped other than Him, their deeds on the Day of Resurrection are like ashes which the wind blows hard upon on a stormy day. They have no power over any of their deeds that benefits them, just as ashes cannot be controlled when sent off by a stormy wind.

* *

As for His words ﴿That is the far-straying error﴾, meaning: the clear error, far from the path of truth.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 14, verses 19–20:

Regarding the interpretation of His words, may He be mighty and remembered: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth? If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation.﴾ (19) ﴿And that is not difficult for Allah.﴾ (20)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may He be mighty and remembered, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Have you not seen, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart" [see the explanation of "ru'ya" (seeing) earlier, vol. 5, p. 485, note 1, and the references there], so that you know that Allah brought the heavens and the earth into being in truth, alone in their creation, without any helper or assistant? ﴿If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation﴾: that is, the One who alone created that and brought it into being, without any helper or partner, if He wills to take you away and cause you to perish, He takes you away and destroys you [see the explanation of "idhhab" (taking away) earlier, vol. 14, p. 161, note 1, and the references there], and brings in place of you another creation other than you, renewing their creation. ﴿And that is not difficult for Allah﴾: that is, taking you away, destroying you, and bringing into being a creation other than you in your place is not impossible or unattainable for Allah, because He is capable of whatever He wills. [see the explanation of "'aziz" (mighty) earlier, p. 511, note 4, and the references there]

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His words: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah created (khalaqa)﴾.

The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufans, recited it as ﴿khalaqa﴾ in the form "fa'ala".

* *

The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it as "khaliq", in the form "fa'il".

* *

Both are well-transmitted readings, each recited by leading readers, and their meanings are close. Whichever of the two a reader recites, he is correct.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 21:**

The interpretation of His, may His remembrance be exalted, words: ﴿They will come forth before God, all of them, and the weak will say to those who were arrogant: "Indeed, we were your followers, so can you avail us anything against the punishment of God?" They will say: "Had God guided us, we would have guided you. It is all the same for us whether we lament or endure patiently; for us there is no escape."﴾ (14:21)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His saying ﴿And they will come forth before God, all of them﴾, He means that those who disbelieved in Him will appear on the Day of Resurrection from their graves, and they will be brought out into the open (al-baraz) from the earth [[See the explanation of "baraza" in what has preceded: 5:354 / 7:324 / 8:562.]]. ﴿All of them﴾ means all of them [[See the explanation of "al-jami'" in what has preceded: 15:212.]]. ﴿Then the weak will say to those who were arrogant﴾ means: the followers among them will say to the leaders, those who were arrogant in the world toward sincerely worshipping God and following the messengers sent to them [[See the explanation of "al-du'afa'" (the weak) in what has preceded: 14:419, note 2, and the references there. And the explanation of "al-istikbar" (arrogance) in what has preceded: 15:155, note 2, and the references there.]]. ﴿Indeed, we were your followers﴾, in the world.

* *

"Al-tabac" is the plural of "tabi'" (follower), just as "al-ghayab" is the plural of "ghai'b" (absent).

* *

What they meant by their saying ﴿Indeed, we were your followers﴾ is that they used to follow them in the world, obeying what they commanded them to do, such as worshipping idols and disbelieving in God, and refraining from what they forbade them, namely following the messengers of God. ﴿So can you avail us anything against the punishment of God?﴾ They mean: can you ward off from us today anything of the punishment of God? [[See the explanation of "al-ighna'" (averting, availing) in what has preceded: p. 166, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

Ibn Juraij used to say something similar to this:

20638. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His saying ﴿and the weak will say﴾: "The followers." ﴿To those who were arrogant﴾: "To the leaders."

* *

As for His saying ﴿Had God guided us, we would have guided you﴾: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The leaders, who were upon disbelief in God, will say to their followers: ﴿Had God guided us﴾, meaning: had God made clear to us something by which we could ward off His punishment from ourselves today; ﴿we would have guided you﴾, meaning: we would have made it clear to you so that you could ward off the punishment from yourselves. But we have lamented the punishment, and our lamenting it has not benefited us, nor has our patience under it [[See the explanation of "al-huda" (guidance) in the indices of language in what has preceded, under the root (h-d-y).]]. ﴿It is all the same for us whether we lament or endure patiently; for us there is no escape.﴾ They mean: they have no place to which they can turn aside (yarughun) and escape from it. [[In the printed edition: "mizag," "yazughun," and "zaagh," all with a zay, but what is in the manuscript is purely correct.]]

* *

It is said of this: "hasa 'an kadha" (he escaped from such-and-such) when he turned away from it, "yahisu haysan, wahuyusan, wahayasanan."[[See the explanation of "al-hays" in what has preceded: 9:226.]]

* *

20639. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Abi Layla, of the tribe of Banu 'Amir, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say: "It has reached me, or it was mentioned to me, that the people of the Fire said to one another: 'O people, the punishment and affliction that has befallen you is what you see. So come, let us endure patiently, for perhaps patience will benefit us, just as the people of the world endured patiently in obedience to God and patience benefited them when they were patient.'" He said: "So they agreed upon patience. They were patient, and their patience lasted long. Then they lamented, and they called out: ﴿It is all the same for us whether we lament or endure patiently; for us there is no escape﴾," meaning: no place of deliverance. [[The report 20639: "al-Hakam" is "al-Hakam al-Makki," a teacher of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, whose status Imam al-Bukhari hesitated over. Ibn Abi Hatim said: he is unknown (majhul). Al-Bukhari said: "al-Hakam al-Makki, from Umar ibn Abi Layla; Ibn al-Mubarak and Muhammad ibn Muqatil heard from him. Marwan, that is Ibn Mu'awiya, narrated from al-Hakam ibn Abi Khalid, client of the Banu Fazara, from Umar ibn Abi Layla. Al-Hasan ibn Ali said, and from al-Hakam ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Hasan, from Jabir, regarding Paradise, so I do not know whether this is from that." It seems this refers to this very report.

It is mentioned in the biography of "al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr al-Fazari": "Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Marwan narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Abi Khalid, client of the Banu Fazara, from Umar ibn Abi Layla al-Numayri..." and he said the same as he said in the biography of "al-Hakam al-Makki." Then he gave a biography of "al-Hakam ibn Abi Khalid" and did not mention anything of this in it.

As for Ibn Abi Hatim, he limited himself to the biography of "al-Hakam al-Makki" and did not mention "al-Hakam ibn Abi Khalid" in it.

Ibn Hajar said in al-Tahdhib: "Ibn Abi Khaythama said: I heard Yahya ibn Ma'in say: 'Marwan ibn Mu'awiya used to change the names, confusing the people; he would say: "al-Hakam ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us," when in fact it was al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr.'"

See what I have mentioned in al-Bukhari's al-Kabir 1/2/336, 339, 342; Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/131; Mizan al-I'tidal 1:273; Lisan al-Mizan 2:341; and Tahdhib al-Tahdhib.

As for "Umar ibn Abi Layla": al-Bukhari said in al-Kabir 3/2/190: "al-Hakam al-Makki narrated from him, and some of them said: 'Umar ibn Abi Layla, brother of the Banu Amir, heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b, his saying.'" Al-Bukhari added, in the biography of "al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr," the nisba "al-Numayri," as mentioned shortly before. Ibn Abi Hatim said the same in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil 3/1/131, and he added from his father, who said: "I heard him say: he is unknown (majhul)." In Mizan al-I'tidal 2:268 he said: "I say: Ibn Abi Fudayk and al-Waqidi narrated from him." Ibn Hajar added in Lisan al-Mizan 4:224: "Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat."

In the printed edition it was "Amr ibn Abi Layla," which differs from what is confirmed in the manuscript, which is correct.

As for "Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi," he is a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i), from whom the compilers of the six books related; he has passed many times, too many to count.

This report is unsound (talif), because of what you know about "al-Hakam al-Makki" and his unknown status. If he is "al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr al-Fazari," then he is abandoned (matruk), as has passed many times before.]]

20640. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿It is all the same for us whether we lament or endure patiently; for us there is no escape﴾: "The people of the Fire said to one another: 'Come, for the people of Paradise attained Paradise only through their weeping and their humble supplication to God. So come, let us weep and humbly supplicate to God!' So they wept, and when they saw that this did not benefit them, they said: 'Come, for the people of Paradise attained Paradise only through patience. Come, let us be patient!' So they were patient with a patience the like of which had never been seen, but it did not benefit them. At that point they said: ﴿It is all the same for us whether we lament or endure patiently; for us there is no escape﴾."

[[The copyist played with the wording, making it: "So the people of Paradise did not attain Paradise except through patience," changing "fa-innama" to "fa-ma," then adding "illa"! Marvel at what he did.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 22:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And Satan will say, when the matter has been decided: "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I broke my promise to you. I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I disbelieve in your associating me with Allah before this." Indeed, for the wrongdoers there is a painful punishment.﴾ (14:22)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And Iblis said [See the explanation of "Satan" above, 1:111-112, 12:51]. ﴿When the matter has been decided﴾, meaning when the people of Paradise had been admitted to Paradise and the people of the Fire to the Fire, and each group had settled in its abode [See the explanation of "decided" above, p. 107, note 2, and the references there], that Allah promised you, O followers, the Fire, and I promised you victory, but I broke my promise to you, while Allah fulfilled His promise to you. ﴿I had no authority over you﴾, meaning: I had no proof against you regarding what I promised you of victory, by which my words would be validated [See the explanation of "authority" above, p. 537, note 7, and the references there]. ﴿Except that I called you﴾. This is a disconnected exception from the preceding statement, as one says: "I did not strike him except that he is a fool," meaning: but I ﴿called you, and you responded to me.﴾ He means: I called you to obey me and disobey Allah, and you responded to my call. ﴿So do not blame me﴾ for your response to me, ﴿and blame yourselves﴾ for it. ﴿I cannot help you﴾, he means: I cannot relieve you. ﴿Nor can you help me﴾, nor can you relieve me from the punishment of Allah, nor save me from it. ﴿Indeed, I disbelieve in your associating me with Allah before this﴾, he means: I denied that I should be a partner of Allah in what you associated me with in your worship of me. ﴿Before this﴾, in this world. ﴿Indeed, for the wrongdoers there is a painful punishment﴾, he means: indeed, for those who disbelieve in Allah there is a punishment that is "painful," meaning causing pain from Allah [See the explanation of "association" and "painful" above, in the language indexes under the roots (sh-r-k) and (a-l-m)].

* *

It is said: "I aṣrakhtu al-rajul" (I shouted for the man to help him) when I came to his aid with "iṣrākh," and "qad ṣaraka al-ṣārikh, yaṣruku, and yaṣraku" (the one crying out cried out), which is rare, and it is "al-ṣarīkh" and "al-ṣurākh" (the cry for help). ["Yaṣraku" with a fatha on the ra', as it is vocalized in the manuscript. I have not found anyone among the lexicographers who stated the present tense of "ṣaraka" with a fatha on the ra', so this is an addition.]

* *

Those who engaged in ta'wil (interpretation) said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

20641. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Amir, regarding this verse: ﴿I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I disbelieve in your associating me with Allah before this﴾. He said: Two orators will stand on the Day of Resurrection: Iblis and 'Isa ibn Maryam. As for Iblis, he will stand among his party and say this statement. As for 'Isa, peace be upon him, he will say: ﴿I said to them only what You commanded me: "Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." And I was a witness over them as long as I remained among them. But when You caused me to die, You were the Watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 117].

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Two orators will stand on the Day of Resurrection, one of them 'Isa and the other Iblis. As for Iblis, he will stand among his party and say: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth﴾, and Dawud recited until he reached: ﴿because you associated me with Allah before this﴾. I do not know whether he completed the verse or not. As for 'Isa, peace be upon him, it will be said to him: ﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?"﴾ And he recited until he reached: ﴿Indeed, You are the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 116-118].

20643. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Asim narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Amir, who said: Two orators will stand on the Day of Resurrection before the people. Allah, may He be exalted, will say: ﴿O 'Isa son of Maryam, did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah"?﴾ up to His words ﴿This is a day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 116-119]. He said: Then Iblis will stand and say: ﴿I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me﴾, meaning: I cannot relieve you, nor can you relieve me.

20644. al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us, saying: Khalid narrated to me, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, regarding His words: ﴿I cannot help you, nor can you help me﴾. He said: Two orators will stand on the Day of Resurrection. As for Iblis, he will say this, and as for 'Isa, he will say: ﴿I said to them only what You commanded me.﴾

20645. al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Rushdin ibn Sa'd, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad informed me, from Dukhayn al-Hajri, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who mentioned the hadith, saying: 'Isa will say: "That is the unlettered Prophet." They will come to me, and Allah will permit me to stand. I will rise from my seat with the best scent anyone has ever smelled, until I come to my Lord and He grants me intercession and makes for me a light upon light, from the hair of my head to the nail of my foot. Then the disbelievers will say: "The believers have found someone to intercede for them, so stand up and intercede for us, for indeed you misled us." He will stand and rise from his seat with the foulest odor anyone has ever smelled, then Hell will groan [In the printed edition: "Their wailing will increase," which differs from what the manuscript agrees upon, and al-Durr al-Manthur and Ibn Kathir. This is what I have confirmed; but I am uncertain of the word, and I think it is "yuqaṭṭim li-jahannam," from their saying "qaṭṭama al-shārib," when he tasted the drink and disliked it, and made a face, and frowned]. At that point he will say: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I broke my promise to you﴾, up to the end of the verse.

[Report 20645: "Rushdin ibn Sa'd al-Misri" was a righteous man, whom the heedlessness of the righteous overtook, so he confused the hadith, and he did not care from whom he narrated. He is weak and abandoned, and he has disconnected and unfamiliar reports. He has been mentioned several times, the last of which is number 17729.

And "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad ibn An'am al-Sha'bani al-Ifriqi" was a righteous man, but he was weak in hadith, even though some deemed him trustworthy. Abu al-Hasan ibn al-Qattan said: He was among the people of knowledge and asceticism, with no disagreement among people about that. Some people deem him trustworthy and shield him from the lowest level of rejecting narrations. The truth about him is that he is weak, because of his frequent narration of unfamiliar reports, a matter that affects the righteous. He has also been mentioned several times, the last of which is number 14337.

And "Dukhayn al-Hajri" is "Dukhayn ibn 'Amir al-Hajri," "Abu Layla al-Misri." He narrated from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad narrated from him. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/234, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/442.

This report is weak in its chain of narration and cannot be relied upon. al-Suyuti recorded it in al-Durr al-Manthur 4:74, and added its attribution to Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn 'Asakir, and said: They recorded it with a weak chain. Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 4:557 transmitted it from Ibn Abi Hatim.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verses 23–25 (part 1 of 3):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds will be admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever by the permission of their Lord. Their greeting therein will be, "Peace." (23) Have you not considered how Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree, whose root is firmly fixed and whose branches are in the sky (24), giving its fruit at every season by the permission of its Lord. And Allah presents examples for the people that they may remember.﴾ (25)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "And admit those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger, acknowledging the oneness of Allah and the message of His messengers, and that what they brought is the truth from Allah." ﴿And did righteous deeds﴾: meaning they acted in obedience to Allah, so they complied with the command of Allah and His prohibition. ﴿Gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾: orchards beneath which rivers flow. ﴿Abiding therein﴾: meaning remaining therein forever [[The phrase "meaning remaining therein forever" is omitted from the printed edition.]]. ﴿By the permission of their Lord﴾: meaning, "They enter it by the command of Allah to them to enter." ﴿Their greeting therein will be, "Peace"﴾ [[See the explanation of the words of this verse in the earlier language indexes under (amn), (salah), (jann), (nahr), (khald), (adhn). And see the explanation of "greeting" (tahiyyah) earlier, 8:586.]]. This, if Allah wills, is as follows:

20657: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: regarding His saying, ﴿their greeting therein will be "Peace"﴾, he said: "The angels will greet them with peace in Paradise."

* * *

And His saying: ﴿Have you not considered how Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree﴾. He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Have you not seen, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart [[See the explanation of "seeing" (al-ru'yah) earlier, 556, note 2, and the references there.]], so that you know how Allah has set forth an example and made a comparison?" ﴿A good word﴾: by "good" He means faith in Him, exalted is His praise, [[See the explanation of "good" (al-tayyib) earlier, 13:165, note 3, and the references there.]] like a tree good in its fruit. The mention of "fruit" is omitted, being sufficient through the listeners' knowledge, by the mention of "tree." And His saying: ﴿Its root is firm and its branch is in the sky﴾: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: The root of this tree is firm in the earth, and "its branch," which is its highest part, is "in the sky," meaning it rises high toward the sky. And His saying: ﴿It gives its produce at every season by the permission of its Lord﴾: meaning it yields what is eaten of its fruit at every season by the command of its Lord [[See the explanation of "eating" (al-akl) earlier, 472, note 3, and the references there. And the explanation of "permission" (al-idhn) in the language indexes earlier under (adhn).]]. ﴿And Allah presents examples for the people﴾: meaning, Allah sets forth examples for the people and makes comparisons for them [[See the explanation of "set forth an example" (darb mathal) earlier, 1:403.]]. ﴿That they may remember﴾: meaning, that they may remember the proof of Allah against them, so that they may take heed from it, be admonished, and desist from their unbelief in Him toward faith [[See the explanation of "remembrance" (al-tadhakkur) earlier in the language indexes under (dhakr). And see the discussion of "la'alla" (perhaps/that) in the Arabic linguistic discussions.]].

* * *

The interpreters have differed regarding the meaning of "the good word."

Some of them said: It refers to the faith of the believer.

Those who said this:

20658: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿A good word﴾: the testimony that there is no god but Allah. ﴿Like a good tree﴾: this refers to the believer. ﴿Its root is firm﴾: meaning, "There is no god but Allah," firmly established in the heart of the believer. ﴿And its branch is in the sky﴾: meaning, the deed of the believer is raised by it to the sky.

20659: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding ﴿a good word﴾, he said: This is the parable of faith. So faith is the good tree, and its root is the firm one which does not cease, which is sincerity to Allah. And its branch is in the sky: its branch is the fear of Allah.

20670: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Mujahid said: ﴿Have you not considered how Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree﴾, he said: "like a palm tree." Ibn Juraij said: Others said: "The good word," its root is firm: it has a root in the heart. ﴿And its branch is in the sky﴾: it ascends and is not veiled until it reaches Allah.

* * *

Others said: Rather, it refers to the believer himself.

Those who said this:

20671: Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Have you not considered how Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree, its root is firm and its branch is in the sky, giving its produce at every season by the permission of its Lord﴾. He means by the good tree the believer, by its firm root in the earth, and by its branch in the sky. The believer works on the earth and speaks, and his deed and his words reach the sky while he is on the earth.

20672: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated to us, from Atiyyah al-Awfi, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree﴾, he said: That is the parable of the believer, from whom there continually issues good speech and righteous deed that ascends to Him.

20673: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: "Its root is firm in the earth," and thus he used to recite it. He said: That is the believer, whose parable was set forth. He said: The sincerity to Allah alone and worship of Him without partner. He said: ﴿Its root is firm﴾: he said: the root of his deed is firm in the earth. ﴿And its branch in the sky﴾: he said: his remembrance is in the sky.

* * *

They differed regarding this "tree" which was made a parable for the good word.

Some of them said: It is the palm tree.

Those who said this:

20674: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik on this phrase: ﴿like a good tree﴾, he said: It is the palm tree.

20675: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abu Qatan narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, from Anas, the like of it.

20676: Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: ﴿A good word like a good tree﴾, he said: the palm. [[The reports 20674–20676: this report is authentic in its chain, through its three routes, stopping at Anas (mawquf).]] See the commentary on the following reports.

20677: Ya'qub and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to me, both saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Shu'ayb narrated to us, who said: I went out with Abu al-Aliyah, wishing to visit Anas ibn Malik. He said: We came to him, and he called for us a bunch (qinw) with dates on it [[Qinw, with kasra and sukun, plural aqna' and qinwan, is the stalk of the palm with what is on it of ripe dates, namely the cluster (kubasah).]], and said: Eat from this tree about which Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree, its root firm and its branch in the sky﴾. Al-Hasan said in his narration: "on a platter" (bi-qina')[[Al-qina', with kasra, and al-qinʿ, with kasra and sukun, is the tray on which food is eaten, or in which fruit is eaten, and it is said to be specifically for ripe dates. Al-busr, with damma and sukun, is the date before it ripens, which has not yet changed color or matured; when it ripens it is rutab, ripe dates.]].

20678: Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, saying: Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab informed us, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was brought a platter of unripe dates [[See the note above on qina' and busr.]], and he said: ﴿Like a good word like a good tree﴾, and said: it is the palm tree.

20679: Sawwar ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was brought a platter with unripe dates, and he said: ﴿Like a good word like a good tree﴾, and said: "It is the palm tree." Shu'ayb said: I informed Abu al-Aliyah of this, and he said: "Thus they used to say."

20680: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab, who said: We were with Anas, and we were brought a tray, or platter, with ripe dates on it. He said: Eat, O Abu al-Aliyah, for this is from the tree which Allah, mighty and majestic, mentioned in His Book: ﴿Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree, whose root is firm﴾.

20681: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Mahdi ibn Maymun narrated to us, from Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab, who said: Abu al-Aliyah used to visit me. He came to me one day at my house after I had prayed the dawn prayer, and I went with him to Anas ibn Malik. We entered with him to Anas ibn Malik, and a tray with ripe dates was brought. Anas said to Abu al-Aliyah: "Eat, O Abu al-Aliyah, for this is from the tree which Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿Have you not seen how Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree, whose root is firm﴾." He said: Thus Anas recited it on that day. [[The reports 20677–20681: the hadith of Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab from Anas is transmitted here through five routes: two routes raised to the Prophet (ﷺ), from Hammad ibn Salamah from Shu'ayb (20678, 20679); then from Hammad from Shu'ayb again, stopping at Anas (20680); and then two routes stopping at Anas, from Ibn Ulayyah from Shu'ayb and from Mahdi ibn Maymun from Shu'ayb (20677, 20681).

As for the raised version, al-Hakim recorded it in al-Mustadrak 2:352 and said: "This is a sound hadith according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it." Al-Tirmidhi recorded it in his commentary on this surah at length, through the route of Abu al-Walid, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Shu'ayb; then he said: "Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab narrated to us, from his father, from Anas ibn Malik, similar in meaning, but he did not raise it, and he did not mention the saying of Abu al-Aliyah" (20679). "This is more authentic than the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah. Many have related the like of it stopping at Anas, and we know of no one who raised it except Hammad ibn Salamah. Ma'mar, Hammad ibn Zayd, and others related it without raising it. Ahmad ibn Abdah al-Dabbi narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab, from Anas ibn Malik, similar to the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab, and he did not raise it."

Al-Suyuti recorded the raised version in al-Durr al-Manthur 4:76, adding its attribution to al-Nasa'i, al-Bazzar, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, and Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his commentary 4:561.]]

20682: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Talq narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Murrah, from Abdullah, the like of it. [[The report 20682: "Talq" is Talq ibn Ghannam ibn Talq al-Nakha'i, mentioned earlier as 20000, from whom Abu Kurayb narrated. "Shurayk" is Shurayk ibn Abdullah al-Nakha'i, the judge, from whom Talq narrated, mentioned many times before. Before this report in the manuscript there is a sign like this: ".. ", indicating doubt, and it is correct, for the report of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud has not been mentioned before, so he says: "the like of it." It has been transmitted by Ibn Kathir in his commentary 4:559, who said: "Thus al-Suddi narrated it from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: 'It is the palm tree.'" Likewise al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 4:76. I fear that a report containing the exact words of Ibn Mas'ud has dropped out before this report.]]

20683: Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Jami' ibn Abi Rashid, from Murrah ibn Sharahil al-Hamdani, from Masruq: ﴿like a good tree﴾, he said: the palm tree.

20684: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa = and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us [narrated to us, saying: Warqa' = both, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿like a good tree﴾, he said: like a palm tree.

20685: [Al-Hasan] narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us = and Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us = both, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it. [[What is between the parentheses, from the middle of the preceding report to this point, is omitted from the printed edition.]]

20686: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Murrah, from Abdullah, the like of it.

20687: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Mu'alla ibn Asad narrated to us, saying: Khalid narrated to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Ikrimah regarding His saying: ﴿like a good tree﴾, he said: It is the palm tree; there is always benefit in it.

20688: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra' narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: ﴿like a good tree﴾, he said: Allah set forth the parable of the believer as the parable of the palm tree = ﴿it gives its produce at every season﴾.

20689: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿like a good word like a good tree﴾, we used to be told that it is the palm tree.

20690: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿like a good tree﴾, he said: They claim it is the palm tree.

20691: Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿it gives its produce at every season﴾, he said: It is the palm tree.

20692: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ubayd narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and its branch is in the sky﴾, he said: the palms. [[In the printed edition: "the palm tree."]]

20693: Al-Hasan [[In the printed edition: "narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan," adding what has no place.]] narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us, saying: Khalid narrated to us, from al-Shaybani, from Ikrimah: ﴿it gives its produce at every season﴾, he said: It is the palm tree.

20694: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab said, from Anas ibn Malik: "The good tree" is the palm tree.

Others said: Rather, it is a tree in Paradise.

Those who said this:

20695: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Affan narrated to us, saying: Abu Kudaynah narrated to us, saying: Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree, its root firm and its branch in the sky, giving its produce at every season by the permission of its Lord﴾, he said: It is a tree in Paradise. [[Report 20695: "Abu Kudaynah" is Yahya ibn al-Muhallab al-Bajali, trustworthy, who sometimes erred, and whose report is considered; his biography has been mentioned before at 4193, 5994, 9745. "Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan al-Janbi" is weak, of poor memory, who transmits alone from his father what has no basis, so he sometimes raised the mursal reports and traced back the mawquf ones; mentioned at 9745, 10682, 16679. His father "Abu Zabyan," whose name is "Husayn ibn Jundub al-Janbi," is trustworthy; the majority related from him; mentioned at 9745, 10683, 16679.]]

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the two opinions regarding this is the view of the one who said: it is "the palm tree," because the report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is sound, namely:

20696: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated it to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: I accompanied Ibn Umar to Medina, and I did not hear him narrate from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) except one hadith. He said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ), and a heart of palm was brought, and he said: "Among the trees there is a tree whose likeness is that of a Muslim man." I wished to say, "It is the palm tree," but I was the youngest of the people, so I remained silent. [The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is the palm tree."] [[Report 20696: its chain is sound. Ahmad recorded it in his Musnad, no. 4599, and Ahmad also recorded it through Shurayk, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Mujahid, in a longer and shorter form (5647, 5955). Al-Bukhari recorded it in his Sahih (al-Fath 1:151), and Muslim in his Sahih (17:152), through three routes: through Ayyub, from Abu al-Khalil al-Dab'i, from Mujahid; through Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid; and through Ibn Numayr, from his father, from Sayf, from Mujahid.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verses 23–25 (part 2 of 3):

The note at the head of the report was the letter (ṭ) in the manuscript, indicating the omission in it, which I have supplied from Musnad Aḥmad and placed between brackets.]]
20697: Al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, saying: Sulaymān informed us, from Yūsuf ibn Sarj, from a man, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you know what the good tree is?" Ibn ʿUmar said: "I wanted to say, 'It is the date palm,' but my position among ʿUmar prevented me. They said, 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'It is the date palm.'" [[The report: 20697 – "Sulaymān" is Sulaymān ibn Ṭarkhān al-Taymī, who has passed many times. "Yūsuf ibn Sarj," with a jīm, is so stated by ʿAbd al-Ghanī in al-Mu'talif wa'l-Mukhtalif (p. 69), and by al-Dhahabī in al-Mushtabih (p. 356). He transmitted a mursal report, and Sulaymān al-Taymī narrated from him. He is biographed in al-Kabīr of al-Bukhārī (4/2/373) and Ibn Abī Ḥātim (4/2/223), and it seems they both pointed to this report.
In the printed edition here it reads "Sarḥ" with a ḥāʾ, and likewise in the manuscript, though it sometimes omits some diacritical dots.]]
20698: Al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥammād narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār narrated to us, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said one day to his companions: "Is there a tree among the trees that does not shed its leaves, like the believer?" He said: The people began to think of the trees of the desert, and it came into my heart that it was the date palm, but I felt shy, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It is the date palm." [[The report: 20698 – "ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz" is ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Salama al-Mājishūn, one of the leading scholars, from whom the whole group narrated. He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr (3/2/12), and Ibn Abī Ḥātim (2/2/386).
This report was narrated by Aḥmad in his Musnad (6052), by way of ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Mājishūn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār, in full. It was also narrated by way of Mālik, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār, in full (5274). Al-Bukhārī narrated it in his Ṣaḥīḥ by this route (al-Fatḥ 1:203), and by way of Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār (al-Fatḥ 1:133–134), and by way of Sulaymān ibn Bilāl, from ʿAbd Allāh (al-Fatḥ 1:136). Muslim narrated it in his Ṣaḥīḥ (17:153) by way of Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar, from ʿAbd Allāh.
See the commentary on the following report.]]
20699: Al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muslim al-Qasmalī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār narrated to us, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Among the trees there is a tree whose leaves do not fall, and it is like the believer; so tell me what it is?" Then he mentioned something similar. [[The report: 20699 – "ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muslim al-Qasmalī" is trustworthy in hadith, reliable, biographed in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr (3/2/28), and Ibn Abī Ḥātim (2/2/394). This is another route for the earlier report.]]
20700: Al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAlī narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿd narrated to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allāh narrated to us, saying: Nāfiʿ narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Tell me of a tree like the Muslim man, which yields its fruit every season, whose leaves do not fall?" He said: It came into my mind that it was the date palm, but I disliked speaking while Abū Bakr and ʿUmar were present. When they did not speak, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It is the date palm." [[The report: 20700 – "Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd ibn Farrūkh," al-Qaṭṭān, the memorizer, is trustworthy, and the whole group narrated from him; he has passed many times.
"ʿUbayd Allāh" is ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Ḥafs ibn ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, who has passed many times. This is a ṣaḥīḥ report narrated by al-Bukhārī in his Ṣaḥīḥ (al-Fatḥ 1:286) in full, by way of ʿUbayd ibn Ismāʿīl, from Abū Usāma, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar. Muslim narrated it in his Ṣaḥīḥ (17:155) from Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shayba, from Abū Usāma.
It will come by another route.]]
20701: Al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ narrated to us, saying: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ, something similar. [[The report: 20701 – "Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Dūlābī," the cloth merchant, whom the whole group narrated from; he has passed as no. 20514. "Ismāʿīl" is Ismāʿīl ibn Zakariyyā al-Khalqānī al-Asadī, whose epithet is "Shaqūṣā," whom the group narrated from. He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr (1/1/355), and Ibn Abī Ḥātim (1/1/170).]]
* *
The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wīl) differed regarding the meaning of "ḥīn" (a season, a period of time) which Allah, mighty and majestic, mentioned in this place, when He said: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: it yields its fruit every morning and evening.
Those who said that:
20702: Al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: Abū Muʿāwiya narrated to us, saying: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "ḥīn" may be morning and evening.
20703: Al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾, he said: morning and evening.
20704: Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, the like of it.
20705: Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from Sulaymān, from Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, with the like of it.
20706: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ṭalq narrated to us, from Zāʾida, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, the like of it.
20707: Al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAlī ibn al-Jaʿd narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾, he said: at dawn and evening.
20708: Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: Sharīk narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾, he said: at dawn and evening.
20709: Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾, he said: Allah is remembered at every hour of the night and the day.
20710: Al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAffān narrated to us, saying: Abū Kudayna narrated to us, saying: Qābūs narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾, he said: morning and evening.
20711: Al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Isḥāq narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mughrāʾ narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, regarding His words: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾, he said: The believer obeys Allah by night and day, and in every season.
20712: Al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Isḥāq narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Jaʿfar narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾, his deed ascends at the beginning of the day and its end.
20713: Al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾, he said: his deed ascends morning and evening.
20714: It was narrated to me from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: Ubayd ibn Sulaymān informed us, who said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His words: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾: "Its fruit comes out every season. This is like the believer who works every season, every hour of the day, and every hour of the night, and in winter and summer, in obedience to Allah."
* *
Others said: The meaning of that is: it yields its fruit every six months, from the time of its harvesting (ṣirām) to the time of its bearing (ḥaml). [["Ṣirām al-nakhl," with a kasra on the ṣād, is cutting and gathering the fruit from the palm.]]
Those who said that:
20715: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ṭāriq ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "ḥīn" is six months.
20716: Yaʿqūb narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, saying: Ayyūb informed us, saying: ʿIkrima said: I was asked about a man who swore that he would not do such and such until a ḥīn. So I said: Among the ḥīn is a ḥīn that can be attained, and among the ḥīn is a ḥīn that cannot be attained. The ḥīn that cannot be attained is His saying: ﴿And you will surely know its news after a while﴾ [Sūrat Ṣād: 88], and the ḥīn that can be attained is ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾. He said: That is from the time the palm is harvested to the time it puts forth its spathe (ṭalʿ), [["Aṭlaʿa al-nakhl," it brought out its spathe, i.e. its blossom sheath.]] and that is six months.
20717: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ibn al-Aṣbahānī, from ʿIkrima, who said: "al-ḥīn" is six months. [[The report: 20717 – "Sufyān" is al-Thawrī, who has passed many times. "Ibn al-Aṣbahānī" is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Aṣbahānī, whom the group narrated from. He narrated from Anas, Abū Ḥāzim, ʿIkrima and others. He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb. See no. 20725.]]
20718: Al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr narrated to us, saying: Khālid narrated to us, from al-Shaybānī, from ʿIkrima, regarding His words: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾, he said: It is the palm, and "ḥīn" is six months.
20719: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Kathīr ibn Hishām narrated to us, saying: Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: ʿIkrima narrated to us: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾, he said: It is what lies between the bearing of the palm and the time it is harvested (tujadd). [[The report: 20719 – "Kathīr ibn Hishām al-Kilābī," trustworthy and truthful, has passed as no. 12648. "Jaʿfar" is Jaʿfar ibn Burqān al-Kilābī, trustworthy, has passed as no. 4577.
In the printed edition it reads "ilā an tuḥraz" (until it is secured), and in the manuscript the same, undotted. I judged the correct reading to be "tujadd," from "jadda al-nakhl yajidduhu jadan, wa-jidādan," meaning to harvest it. "Ajadda al-nakhl" means it became time for it to be harvested.]]
20720: Al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Qabīṣa ibn ʿUqba narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, saying: ʿIkrima said: "al-ḥīn" is six months.
20721: Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: Qays narrated to us, from Ṭāriq ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he was asked about a man who swore he would not speak to his brother for a ḥīn. He said: "al-ḥīn" is six months. Then he mentioned the palm, that what lies between its bearing and its harvest is six months.
20722: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ṭāriq, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: ﴿It yields its fruit every season﴾, he said: six months.
20723: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, regarding His words: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾: "ḥīn" is what lies between seven and six, and it is eaten in winter and summer.
20724: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, who said: al-Ḥasan said: "What lies between six months and seven"; meaning "ḥīn."
20725: Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aṣbahānī, from ʿIkrima, who said: "al-ḥīn" is six months.
* *
Others said: Rather, "ḥīn" here is a year.
Those who said that:
20726: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Abū Mukayn, from ʿIkrima: that he vowed to cut off the hand of his slave, or to imprison him for a ḥīn. [[In the printed edition: "in nadhara," an error.]] He said: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz asked me, and I said: His hand is not to be cut off; let him imprison him for a year, and "ḥīn" is a year. Then he recited: ﴿They will imprison him until a ḥīn﴾ [Sūrat Yūsuf: 35], and he recited: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾. Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakīʿ narrated to us, and Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī added, from ʿIkrima, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: "al-ḥīn" has two kinds: a ḥīn that is known and a ḥīn that is not known. As for the ḥīn that is not known: ﴿And you will surely know its news after a while﴾ [Sūrat Ṣād: 88]; and as for the ḥīn that is known, His saying: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾.
20727: Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, who said: I asked Ḥammād and al-Ḥakam about a man who swore he would not speak to a man until a ḥīn. Both said: "al-ḥīn" is a year.
20728: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us, and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, and al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: Shabāba narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to me, and al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, his words: ﴿every season﴾, he said: every year. [[In the manuscript here there is a colophon, apparently the end of an earlier division from which our manuscript was copied, and this is its text:
"Followed, if Allah the Exalted wills, by: Yūnus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: (It yields its fruit every season), he said: every year.
May Allah bless our master Muḥammad and his family and companions and grant them peace."
And after it, at the beginning of the part: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. My Lord, make it easy." Abū Jaʿfar said: Yūnus narrated to me...]]
20729: Yūnus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿It yields its fruit every season﴾, he said: every year.
20730: Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: Sallām narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from a man among them [[In the printed edition: "from an unnamed man," which did not understand the manuscript's meaning. His words "a man among them" mean from the Thaqīf, the kinsmen of ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib.]], that he asked Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: I swore I would not speak to a man for a ḥīn? So Ibn ʿAbbās recited: ﴿It yields its fruit every season﴾, and "ḥīn" is a year.
20731: Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ghasīl narrated to us, from ʿIkrima, who said: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz sent for me and said: O client of Ibn ʿAbbās, I have sworn that I will not do such and such for a ḥīn; what is the ḥīn by which one is known? I said: Among the ḥīn is a ḥīn that is not attained, and among the ḥīn is a ḥīn that is attained. As for the ḥīn that is not attained, it is Allah's saying: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning?﴾ [Sūrat al-Insān: 1], and by Allah, he does not know how much time passed before he was created. As for the one that is attained, His saying: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾, which is what lies between one year and the coming year. He said: You are right, O client of Ibn ʿAbbās; how good is what you said. [[The report: 20731 – "Ibn Ghasīl" is the better form "Ibn al-Ghasīl," ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥanẓala al-Anṣārī, known as Ibn al-Ghasīl; his grandfather was Ḥanẓala ibn Abī ʿĀmir, "the washed of the angels." He has passed as nos. 5123 and 7777. In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "Ibn ʿUsayl," with an unpointed ʿayn.]]
20732: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, who said: A man came to Ibn ʿAbbās and said: I vowed that I would not speak to a man for a ḥīn? So Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿It yields its fruit every season﴾, and "ḥīn" is a year.
* *
Others said: Rather, "ḥīn" in this place is two months.
Those who said that:
20733: Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, saying: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Muslim al-Ṭāʾifī narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn Maysara, who said: A man came to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and said: I have sworn that I will not speak to so-and-so for a ḥīn? [He said: Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾.] [[What is between the brackets is in the printed edition and is missing from the manuscript; I did not delete it, since it fits well.]] He said: It is the palm; it yields its fruit only two months, so "ḥīn" is two months.

Abū Jaʿfar said: The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying of the one who said: by "ḥīn" in this place is meant morning and evening, and every hour. [[See the explanation of "ḥīn" above: 1:540/12:359/16:92–94.]] This is because Allah, mighty is His remembrance, made what this tree yields of fruit at every season a parable for the deed and speech of the believer. There is no doubt that a righteous deed and word of the believer is raised to Allah every day, not every year, or every six months, or every two months. If that is so, then there is no doubt that the parable does not contradict what it is a parable for in meaning. And if that is so, the soundness of what we have said becomes clear.

If someone says: Which palm yields fruit at every time, in summer and winter? It is said: As for winter, the spathe is from its produce; as for summer, there are the unripe dates, the semi-ripe dates, the ripe dates and the dried dates, and all of that is from its produce.
* *
As for His words: ﴿It yields its fruit﴾, it is as follows:
20734: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated this to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda: ﴿It yields its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord﴾, he said: its fruit is eaten in winter and summer.
20735: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda: ﴿It yields its fruit every season﴾, he said: it is eaten in winter and summer.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verses 23–25 (part 3 of 3):

20736 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas: ﴿It brings forth its fruit every season by the permission of its Lord﴾. "Its deed ascends, meaning the deed of the believer, from the beginning of the day and its end."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verses 23–25 (part 1 of 3):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds will be admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever by the permission of their Lord. Their greeting therein will be, "Peace." (23) Have you not considered how Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree, whose root is firmly fixed and whose branches are in the sky (24), giving its fruit at every season by the permission of its Lord. And Allah presents examples for the people that they may remember.﴾ (25)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "And admit those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger, acknowledging the oneness of Allah and the message of His messengers, and that what they brought is the truth from Allah." ﴿And did righteous deeds﴾: meaning they acted in obedience to Allah, so they complied with the command of Allah and His prohibition. ﴿Gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾: orchards beneath which rivers flow. ﴿Abiding therein﴾: meaning remaining therein forever [[The phrase "meaning remaining therein forever" is omitted from the printed edition.]]. ﴿By the permission of their Lord﴾: meaning, "They enter it by the command of Allah to them to enter." ﴿Their greeting therein will be, "Peace"﴾ [[See the explanation of the words of this verse in the earlier language indexes under (amn), (salah), (jann), (nahr), (khald), (adhn). And see the explanation of "greeting" (tahiyyah) earlier, 8:586.]]. This, if Allah wills, is as follows:

20657: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: regarding His saying, ﴿their greeting therein will be "Peace"﴾, he said: "The angels will greet them with peace in Paradise."

* * *

And His saying: ﴿Have you not considered how Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree﴾. He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Have you not seen, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart [[See the explanation of "seeing" (al-ru'yah) earlier, 556, note 2, and the references there.]], so that you know how Allah has set forth an example and made a comparison?" ﴿A good word﴾: by "good" He means faith in Him, exalted is His praise, [[See the explanation of "good" (al-tayyib) earlier, 13:165, note 3, and the references there.]] like a tree good in its fruit. The mention of "fruit" is omitted, being sufficient through the listeners' knowledge, by the mention of "tree." And His saying: ﴿Its root is firm and its branch is in the sky﴾: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: The root of this tree is firm in the earth, and "its branch," which is its highest part, is "in the sky," meaning it rises high toward the sky. And His saying: ﴿It gives its produce at every season by the permission of its Lord﴾: meaning it yields what is eaten of its fruit at every season by the command of its Lord [[See the explanation of "eating" (al-akl) earlier, 472, note 3, and the references there. And the explanation of "permission" (al-idhn) in the language indexes earlier under (adhn).]]. ﴿And Allah presents examples for the people﴾: meaning, Allah sets forth examples for the people and makes comparisons for them [[See the explanation of "set forth an example" (darb mathal) earlier, 1:403.]]. ﴿That they may remember﴾: meaning, that they may remember the proof of Allah against them, so that they may take heed from it, be admonished, and desist from their unbelief in Him toward faith [[See the explanation of "remembrance" (al-tadhakkur) earlier in the language indexes under (dhakr). And see the discussion of "la'alla" (perhaps/that) in the Arabic linguistic discussions.]].

* * *

The interpreters have differed regarding the meaning of "the good word."

Some of them said: It refers to the faith of the believer.

Those who said this:

20658: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿A good word﴾: the testimony that there is no god but Allah. ﴿Like a good tree﴾: this refers to the believer. ﴿Its root is firm﴾: meaning, "There is no god but Allah," firmly established in the heart of the believer. ﴿And its branch is in the sky﴾: meaning, the deed of the believer is raised by it to the sky.

20659: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding ﴿a good word﴾, he said: This is the parable of faith. So faith is the good tree, and its root is the firm one which does not cease, which is sincerity to Allah. And its branch is in the sky: its branch is the fear of Allah.

20670: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Mujahid said: ﴿Have you not considered how Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree﴾, he said: "like a palm tree." Ibn Juraij said: Others said: "The good word," its root is firm: it has a root in the heart. ﴿And its branch is in the sky﴾: it ascends and is not veiled until it reaches Allah.

* * *

Others said: Rather, it refers to the believer himself.

Those who said this:

20671: Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Have you not considered how Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree, its root is firm and its branch is in the sky, giving its produce at every season by the permission of its Lord﴾. He means by the good tree the believer, by its firm root in the earth, and by its branch in the sky. The believer works on the earth and speaks, and his deed and his words reach the sky while he is on the earth.
