His saying "the wind snatched his cloak" means: pulled his cloak from him. "Commanded" means: subjugated by God's command, not intending what it does. His saying "does not deserve it" means: it does not deserve the curse. One says: "He is worthy of that" and "worthy for that."]]

20753. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas: ﴿And the likeness of an evil word is like an evil tree﴾, he said: "This disbeliever has no deed on earth, nor any mention in heaven." ﴿uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability﴾: he said: "His deed does not ascend to heaven, nor does it stand on earth." It was asked: "Then where will their deeds be?" He said: "They will carry their burdens on their backs."

20754. Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Fudayl ibn Marzuq related to us, from 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi: ﴿And the likeness of an evil word is like an evil tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth﴾, he said: "It is the likeness of the disbeliever; no good word ascends for him, nor any righteous deed."

20755. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: ﴿And the likeness of an evil word﴾, which is *shirk*, ﴿is like an evil tree﴾, meaning the disbeliever. He said: ﴿uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability﴾: that is, *shirk* has no root, which the disbeliever can hold to, nor any proof; and God does not accept any deed along with *shirk*.

20756. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿And the likeness of an evil word is like an evil tree﴾, he said: "The likeness of the evil tree is the likeness of the disbeliever, whose speech and deed have no root and no branch, and whose speech and deed neither settle on the earth nor ascend to heaven."

20757. It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: God struck the likeness of the disbeliever: ﴿like an evil tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability﴾. That is: it has no root and no branch, and it has no fruit, and there is no benefit in it. Likewise, the disbeliever does no good, nor says any, and God has placed in him no blessing nor benefit.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 27 (part 1 of 3):

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, and Allah leads astray the wrongdoers, and Allah does what He wills﴾ (14:27).

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe﴾, He means: Allah confirms their deeds and their faith [[See the explanation of "al-tathbit" (keeping firm) above, vol. 15, p. 539, note 4, and the references there.]]. ﴿with the firm word﴾ means: with the true word, and it is, as has been said, the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.

* *

As for His words ﴿in the life of this world﴾, the people of ta'wil (interpretation, tafsir) differed about it. Some of them said: He means by it that Allah keeps them firm in their graves before the Hour rises.

Those who said this:

20758. Abu al-Sa'ib Salm ibn Junadah narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'd ibn Ubaydah, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, concerning His words ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world﴾, he said: The keeping firm in the life of this world is when the two angels come to him in the grave and say to him: "Who is your Lord?" He says: "My Lord is Allah." They say to him: "What is your religion?" He says: "My religion is Islam." They say to him: "Who is your Prophet?" He says: "My Prophet is Muhammad (ﷺ)." That is the keeping firm in the life of this world.

[[The report: 20758 is a hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib (may Allah be pleased with him), which Abu Ja'far transmitted by fourteen chains of narration (isnad) at this point. I wished to gather them and separate them, so that they may be easily reviewed, the discussion about them is not scattered, and their takhrij (tracing to sources) is easy and clear. The hadith from al-Bara' is transmitted by three routes:
1 - the route of Sa'd ibn Ubaydah, from al-Bara'.
2 - the route of Zadhan, from al-Bara'.
3 - the route of Khaythamah, from al-Bara'.
At the start of each route, I will mention its chains in detail, God willing. This is the place for the explanation of the first route: (1)
The route of Sa'd ibn Ubaydah from al-Bara'.
Abu Ja'far transmitted it by two routes:
1 - the route of al-A'mash, from Sa'd ibn Ubaydah.
2 - the route of 'Alqamah ibn Martad, from Sa'd ibn Ubaydah. (1) The route of al-A'mash, from Sa'd ibn Ubaydah.
1 - the route of Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, number 20758.
2 - the route of Jabir Nuh, from al-A'mash, number 20759.]]

20759. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'd ibn Ubaydah, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, with something similar to it in meaning. [[The report: 20759 - for the following chain, see the earlier note.]]

20760. 'Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-Naqid al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Alqamah ibn Martad, from Sa'd ibn Ubaydah, from al-Bara', who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned the believer and the disbeliever, and said: "When the believer is questioned in his grave, he says: 'My Lord is Allah.' That is His saying: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾." [[The route of Jabir ibn Nuh, from al-A'mash: Jabir ibn Nuh al-Hammani is weak in hadith; Ibn Ma'in said: his hadith is not worth anything.
So the report through this route is weak in its chain, and I have not found it except with Abu Ja'far, and the sound chain is the earlier one.]]

20761. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: 'Alqamah ibn Martad informed me, saying: I heard Sa'd ibn Ubaydah, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Muslim is questioned in the grave, he testifies that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." He said: "That is His saying: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾." [[The report: 20761 - this is a repetition of the earlier report.
Hisham ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-Bahili, Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi, whom the whole group (of canonical compilers) transmitted from; he has passed many times.
Al-Bukhari and Abu Dawud transmitted it through Abu al-Walid, from Shu'bah, as was mentioned in the takhrij of the previous one.
In the printed edition it read: "when he is questioned in the grave he testifies", as in the narration of al-Bukhari, and in the narration of Abu Dawud: "so he testified." I have kept what is in the manuscript, and both are correct.
In the manuscript here it read "Sa'id" in place of "Shu'bah", and that is a gross scribal error.]]

20762. Al-Husayn ibn Salamah ibn Abi Kabshah and Muhammad ibn Ma'mar al-Bahrani narrated to me (the wording is that of the hadith of Ibn Abi Kabshah) — they both said: Abu 'Amir 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn Rashid narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at a funeral, and he said: "O people, this community is tried in its graves. When the person is buried and his companions disperse from him, an angel comes to him with a mitraq (hammer) in his hand, and makes him sit up, and says: 'What do you say about this man?' If he was a believer, he says: 'I testify that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.' Then it is said to him: 'You have spoken the truth.' A door to the Fire is opened for him, and it is said: 'This was your place had you disbelieved in your Lord; but since you believed in Him, Allah has given you this in its place.' Then a door to the Garden is opened for him, and he wants to rise towards it, but it is said to him: 'Be still.' Then his grave is made spacious for him. As for the disbeliever or the hypocrite, it is said to him: 'What do you say about this man?' He says: 'I do not know!' It is said to him: 'You did not know, nor did you learn, nor were you guided!' Then a door to the Garden is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'This was your place had you believed in your Lord; but since you disbelieved, Allah has given you this in its place.' Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and then the angel batters him with the mitraq a blow which all of Allah's creation hears except the two weighty ones (jinn and humans)." One of his companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, none of us will have an angel standing over his head with a mitraq in his hand without being terrified at that moment!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, and Allah leads astray the wrongdoers, and Allah does what He wills﴾. [[The report: 20762 - Al-Husayn ibn Salamah ibn Isma'il ibn Yazid ibn Abi Kabshah al-Azdi al-Tahhan, a shaykh of al-Tabari, trustworthy, has passed at number 17608. In the printed edition and the manuscript it read "al-Hasan ibn Salamah", which is an error.
Muhammad ibn Ma'mar al-Bahrani, a shaykh of al-Tabari, trustworthy, whom the whole group transmitted from; he has passed many times, the last at number 16885.
'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr al-Qaysi and Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi, trustworthy, among the shaykhs of Ahmad; he has passed many times, the last at 17608.
'Abbad ibn Rashid al-Tamimi, trustworthy but not strong; al-Bukhari transmitted from him only in conjunction with others; he has passed many times, the last at 17608.
Dawud ibn Abi Hind, trustworthy; he has passed many times.
Abu Nadrah, al-Mundhir ibn Malik ibn Qut'ah al-'Abdi, a Successor (tabi'i), trustworthy, prolific in hadith; he has passed many times, the last at numbers 15797-15801.
This hadith is of sound chain. Ahmad transmitted it in his Musnad, 3:3, from Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi, with its chain. Al-Haythami traced it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 3:47 and said: "Ahmad and al-Bazzar transmitted it, and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih." Al-Suyuti traced it in al-Durr al-Manthur 4:80, and added its attribution to Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Dhikr al-Mawt, Ibn Abi 'Asim in al-Sunnah, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in 'Adhab al-Qabr, and said: "with a sound chain, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri." There is some variation in the wording of the report.
"Al-mitraq" is a word which the dictionaries have not mentioned, yet it is established in all the transmissions of this report, in the places I have noted, and it is correct in Arabic. Its like is "al-mitraq" with a kasrah and then a sukun, and it appeared in the report at number 2389. And "al-mitraqah" is the hammer of the blacksmith with which iron is beaten.
As for his words "la darayta wa la tadarrayta" (you did not know and you did not learn), this is how it is in the manuscript, so I have kept it that way. In the printed edition it read "la darayta wa la talayta" (you did not know nor did you recite), as in all the references mentioned above. What is in the manuscript is written clearly, and I do not find it plausible that the copyist altered "talayta" into "tadarrayta", given the fame of this report. If this wording is confirmed as the narration transmitted by Abu Ja'far, then "tafa''ala" is from "daraa", meaning you sought knowledge, just as you say "'alima"; the two are the same in meaning, and it is very good in meaning.
As for "la darayta wa la talayta", its meaning has been disputed. They said: it is from "talawta", meaning you did not recite nor study, from "tala yatlu", and he said it with a ya' so that it would correspond with the ya' in "daraayta". Yunus used to say: in the speech of the Arabs it is only: "wa la atlayta", meaning that your camels are not followed (by their young), i.e., they have no offspring following them. Others said: it is only "la darayta wa la itta-layta", in the form "ifta'alta" from "alawta", meaning you were able and could, as if he said: you did not know and were not able. Ibn al-Athir said: "The hadith scholars transmit this hadith as 'wa la talayta', but its correct form is 'wa la i'tatlayta'."
Al-Zamakhshari said in al-Fa'iq (under t-l-w): he mentioned the report, and said: "That is, nor did you follow the people by saying something that they say. It may also be from their saying: 'Fulan talaa talwa ghayri 'aqil', when he acted like the ignorant, meaning: you neither knew nor were ignorant, i.e., you were ruined and left out of both groups."
I think that what is in the tafsir, if its transmission is sound, is clearer in indicating the meaning than what they have stated. Moreover, in the transmission of the report in their collections there is an addition at this place: "He says: I do not know; I heard the people saying something." This is the narration of Ahmad.]]

20763. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Zadhan, from al-Bara', that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned the taking of the soul of the believer: "His soul is returned into his body, and two angels come to him and make him sit in his grave, and they say: 'Who is your Lord?' He says: 'My Lord is Allah.' They say: 'What is your religion?' He says: 'My religion is Islam.' They say to him: 'What is this man who was sent among you?' He says: 'He is the Messenger of Allah.' They say: 'How do you know?' He says: 'I read the Book of Allah, believed in it and affirmed it.' Then a caller from the heaven calls out: 'My servant has spoken the truth.'"
He said: That is the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾. [[The report: 20763 - this is the second route, as I mentioned in the note on number 20758.]]

20764. Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Minhal, from Zadhan, from al-Bara', from the Prophet (ﷺ), with something similar to it. [[The route of Zadhan, from al-Bara'.
Abu Ja'far transmitted it by two routes, in abridged form.
1 - the route of al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Zadhan.
2 - the route of Yunus ibn Khabbab, from al-Minhal, from Zadhan.
Then he transmitted from al-A'mash by five routes: from Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash, from al-A'mash: 20763; from Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash: 20764; from Jarir, from al-A'mash: 20765; from Ibn Numayr, from al-A'mash: 20766; and from Abu 'Awanah, from al-A'mash: 20780 and 20787.
Al-Minhal ibn 'Amr al-Asadi. People have spoken about him, and a group declared him trustworthy. My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, preferred his trustworthiness in the Musnad (7:14), and in al-Tabari (3:337). Abu al-Hasan ibn al-Qattan said: "Abu Muhammad ibn Hazm used to weaken al-Minhal and rejected the report of al-Bara' from his transmission," meaning this hadith; and al-Bukhari and Muslim did not include anything from him in their Sahih. Ibn Abi Khaythamah transmitted that al-Mughirah, the companion of Ibrahim (and he is al-Mughirah ibn Miqsam al-Dabbi), stood against Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad and said: "Are you not amazed at this foolish al-A'mash? I forbade him from transmitting from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr and from 'Abbayah, and he parted from me on condition that he would not do so, yet he transmits from them both. I beseech you by Allah, the Exalted: would the testimony of al-Minhal be accepted for two dirhams?" He said: "No, by Allah." This is among the harshest things said about him, but it is to be understood, God willing, as the statement of contemporaries, one of whom says about another.
Zadhan, Abu 'Abdullah or Abu 'Umar al-Kindi, al-Darir al-Bazzar, a trustworthy Successor; he has passed many times.
Abu 'Abdullah al-Hakim has extensively gathered the routes of this hadith in al-Mustadrak (1:37-40), and brought supporting reports conforming to the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim, by which he establishes the soundness of the report of al-Minhal from Zadhan.
Al-Hakim added the narration of Sufyan from al-A'mash (1:38), which is in the Musnad (4:297), and the narration of Shu'bah from al-A'mash (1:38); in the Musnad of Ahmad there is the narration of Za'idah from al-A'mash (4:288).
Abu Ja'far al-Tabari added the narration of Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash from al-A'mash in this chain, and previously in abridged form at number 14614. See the discussion of the following reports from this route and what was mentioned in the note on number 14614. Al-Haythami traced it in Majma' al-Zawa'id (3:49-51) and said: "It is in the Sahih and elsewhere, in abridged form. Ahmad transmitted it, and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]]

20765. Ibn Humayd and Ibn WakI' narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Zadhan, from al-Bara', from the Prophet (ﷺ), with something similar to it. [[The report: 20764 - from the route of Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash; transmitted by Ahmad in al-Musnad (4:287), al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (1:37), and Abu Dawud in his Sunan (4:330).]]

20766. Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, saying: al-Minhal ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Zadhan, from al-Bara', from the Prophet (ﷺ), with something similar to it. [[The report: 20766 - from the route of 'Abdullah ibn Numayr, from al-A'mash; transmitted by Ahmad in al-Musnad (4:288), Abu Dawud in his Sunan (4:331), and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (1:37).]]

20767. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Qays narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Khabbab, from al-Minhal, from Zadhan, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similar to it. [[The report: 20768 - this is the route of Yunus ibn Khabbab, from al-Minhal, as I mentioned in the note on number 20763. Abu Ja'far transmitted it through 'Amr ibn Qays, from Yunus: 20768. 20770 - Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, both saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Amr informed us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Indeed the deceased hears the sound of their sandals when they turn away from him, retreating. If he was a believer, prayer (salat) will be at his head, zakat at his right, fasting at his left, and the doing of good deeds, such as charity, kinship ties, kindness and goodness to people, at his feet. He will be approached from the direction of his head, and Prayer will say: 'There is no entrance from my side.' He will be approached from his right, and Zakat will say: 'There is no entrance from my side.' He will be approached from his left, and Fasting will say: 'There is no entrance from my side.' He will be approached from the direction of his feet, and the doing of good deeds (such as charity, kinship ties, goodness and kindness to people) will say: 'There is no entrance from my side.' Then it will be said to him: 'Sit up.' He sits up, the sun having been shaped before him as it draws near to setting. It will be said to him: 'Tell us about what we ask you.' He says: 'Let me pray first.' It will be said: 'You will indeed do so. But tell us about what we ask you.' He says: 'And what do you ask?' It will be said: 'What do you say about this man who was among you, and what do you testify concerning him?' He says: 'Muhammad?' It is said to him: 'Yes.' He says: 'I testify that he is the Messenger of God, and that he came with the clear proofs from God, and we affirmed him.' It will be said to him: 'Upon this you lived, upon this you died, and upon this you will be raised, if God wills.' Then his grave will be widened for him seventy cubits, and it will be illuminated for him. Then a door to Paradise will be opened for him, and it will be said to him: 'Look at what God has prepared for you therein.' He will increase in joy and delight. Then a door to the Fire will be opened for him, and it will be said to him: 'Look at what God has averted from you had you disobeyed Him!' He will increase in joy and delight. Then his soul (nasam) will be placed among the good souls (al-nasam al-tayyib), which are green birds suspended from the trees of Paradise. [[Report 20771: "Abu Qatan" is Amr ibn al-Haytham al-Zubaydi al-Qatʻi, trustworthy. He has passed many times, the last being no. 20599.
"Al-Mas'udi" is Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah al-Mas'udi. He was trustworthy, but became confused toward the end of his life; the narrations of the earlier transmitters from him are sound. He has passed many times, the last being no. 17982.
"Abd Allah ibn Mikhariq": his case is very problematic. al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir (3/1/208), and Ibn Abi Hatim in al-Jarh wa'l-Ta'dil (2/2/179). Both said, and the wording here is Ibn Abi Hatim's: "Abd Allah ibn Mikhariq ibn Sulaym al-Sulami, a Kufan. He narrated from his father Mikhariq. Narrating from him were Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah al-Mas'udi, Abu al-Amis Utbah ibn Abd Allah, and Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Ghaniyyah." Ibn Abi Hatim then reported from Yahya ibn Ma'in that he was asked about "Abd Allah ibn Mikhariq ibn Sulaym," and he said: "He is well known."
Al-Bukhari said in his biography: "Simak narrated from Qabus ibn Mikhariq al-Shaybani, and Sulayman al-Shaybani also narrated from Mikhariq ibn Sulaym al-Shaybani, but I do not know what lies between them." So al-Bukhari was uncertain whether the father's nisbah was "Sulami" or "Shaybani," as you see.
When he came to the section on "Mikhariq" in al-Kabir (4/1/430), he listed "Mikhariq Abu Qabus, from Ali; his son Qabus narrated from him, and he is Ibn Sulaym, as related by Ibn Tahman." Then after that he listed "Mikhariq ibn Sulaym al-Shaybani" and said: "He is counted among the Kufans." He omitted "Mikhariq ibn Sulaym al-Sulami," who is mentioned in the biography of his son "Abd Allah ibn Mikhariq ibn Sulaym al-Sulami," as having narrated from his father, and who was a Companion, as is evident. Ibn Abi Hatim likewise did this (4/1/352): he mentioned only "Mikhariq ibn Sulaym al-Shaybani," and omitted "al-Sulami," which he had mentioned in the chapter on "Abd Allah."
As for the Hafiz Ibn Hajar, in al-Tahdhib and al-Isabah, he said: "Mikhariq ibn Sulaym al-Shaybani, Abu Qabus, narrated from the Prophet ﷺ, from Ibn Mas'ud, Ammar ibn Yasir, and Ali ibn Abi Talib. Narrating from him were his two sons, Qabus and Abd Allah. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat."
This is a comprehensive statement, which indicates that this "Abd Allah ibn Mikhariq" is in fact "al-Shaybani," and that "al-Sulami" is a nisbah whose bearer is hardly known, and this would increase the ambiguity regarding his father among the Companions, which is unlikely.
"Abd Allah ibn Mikhariq ibn Sulaym al-Shaybani" is Nabigha of the Banu Shayban, the famous poet, and he is the brother of "Qabus ibn Mikhariq ibn Sulaym al-Shaybani," who is discussed in al-Tahdhib and in al-Kabir (4/1/193), without attribution to "Shayban" or "Sulaym," and in Ibn Abi Hatim (3/2/145), in my estimation. I read long ago, in a book whose location has escaped me today, that Qabus was a poet, and that his brother Abd Allah, Nabigha of the Banu Shayban, was a transmitter of hadith. Then one of them, or both, saw a dream, and Qabus gave up poetry and sought hadith, while Abd Allah gave up hadith and took to poetry, becoming Nabigha of the Banu Shayban. Abd Allah ibn Mikhariq, Nabigha of the Banu Shayban, would recite poetry at length, until when he finished he would seize his tongue and say: "By God, I will surely set upon you what will displease you: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, God is greatest." (This appears in the book al-Muntaqa min Akhbar al-Asma'i, p. 6.) This appears to corroborate the report whose location has escaped me, and I ask whoever finds it to direct me to it.
This report is very confused (mudtarib). However, al-Haythami cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id (3:54) and said: "al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Kabir, and its chain is good." Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur and attributed it to Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani, and al-Bayhaqi in "The Punishment of the Grave."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 27 (part 3 of 3):

20786 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: As for the disbeliever, the angels descend upon him when death attends him, and they stretch out their hands. He returns no answer to them, and God makes him forget the mention of that. And when it is said to him: "Who is the Messenger who was sent to you?" he is not guided to him, and he returns no answer to it. God says: ﴿And God leaves the wrongdoers astray﴾ [[In the printed edition: "He says: And God leaves the wrongdoers astray," and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]].

He says: 'I do not know.' It is said to him: 'What is this Prophet who was sent among you?' He says: 'I heard the people say that, I do not know.' They say: 'You did not know.'" See the earlier commentary on report 20780.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and God does what He wills﴾, by it He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: guidance and misguidance are in the hand of God, so do not deny, O people, His power, nor the guidance of whoever among you is astray, nor the misguidance of whoever among you is guided, for in His hand is the disposing of His creation and the turning of their hearts; He does with them what He wills.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verses 28–29:

On the interpretation (*ta'wil*) of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin, into Hell, which they will enter? And wretched is the resting place.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "Have you not considered, O Muhammad, ﴿those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief﴾?" He means: they altered what Allah had bestowed upon them of His blessings, and made it into disbelief in Him. Their exchanging the favour of Allah for disbelief concerned the Prophet of Allah Muhammad (ﷺ), whom Allah had bestowed upon the Quraysh. He brought him forth from among them and sent him to them as a messenger, a mercy to them and a blessing from Him upon them. But they disbelieved in him and denied him, so they exchanged the favour of Allah upon them for disbelief.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin﴾:

He means: they lodged their people, the polytheists of the Quraysh, in the abode of ruin, which is the abode of destruction. It is said from this: *bara al-shay'* (the thing perished), *yabur buran*, when it was destroyed and became void. From this is the saying of Ibn al-Zib'ara, although it has been said that it belongs to Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib:

*O Messenger of the King, indeed my tongue*

It has been said: those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief are the Banu Umayyah and the Banu Makhzum.

In the same sense as what we have said concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin﴾, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿the abode of ruin﴾: The Fire. He said: Allah has explained that and informed you of it, when He said ﴿into Hell, which they will enter; and wretched is the resting place﴾.

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah ﴿the abode of ruin, into Hell, which they will enter﴾: It is their abode in the Hereafter.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verses 28–29:

On the interpretation (*ta'wil*) of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin, into Hell, which they will enter? And wretched is the resting place.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "Have you not considered, O Muhammad, ﴿those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief﴾?" He means: they altered what Allah had bestowed upon them of His blessings, and made it into disbelief in Him. Their exchanging the favour of Allah for disbelief concerned the Prophet of Allah Muhammad (ﷺ), whom Allah had bestowed upon the Quraysh. He brought him forth from among them and sent him to them as a messenger, a mercy to them and a blessing from Him upon them. But they disbelieved in him and denied him, so they exchanged the favour of Allah upon them for disbelief.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin﴾:

He means: they lodged their people, the polytheists of the Quraysh, in the abode of ruin, which is the abode of destruction. It is said from this: *bara al-shay'* (the thing perished), *yabur buran*, when it was destroyed and became void. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. [and] al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us. [and] al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief﴾: He said: The disbelievers of the Quraysh.

Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: The disbelievers of the Quraysh.

Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief﴾: The disbelievers of the Quraysh.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ata, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: "They, by Allah, are ﴿those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin﴾: the Quraysh." Or he said: the people of Makkah.

Ibn Wakf and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both saying: Ghundar narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr concerning this verse (Those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin): He said: The slain of the day of Badr.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin﴾: He said: They are the disbelievers of the Quraysh.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, both said: They are the slain of Badr from among the polytheists.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas concerning ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin﴾: He said: They, by Allah, are the people of Makkah. He said: Abu Kurayb said: Sufyan said: meaning their disbelievers.

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin﴾: He said: They are the polytheists from the people of Badr.

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Ishaq, from some companions of Ali, from Ali, concerning His saying ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief﴾: He said: They are the two wicked groups of the Quraysh, from the Banu Makhzum and the Banu Umayyah. As for the Banu Makhzum, Allah cut off their remnant on the day of Badr; and as for the Banu Umayyah, they were given enjoyment for a time.

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Mu'alla ibn Asad narrated to us, saying: Khalid informed us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, concerning the word of Allah ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief﴾: He said: They are the leaders of the polytheists on the day of Badr.

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, both said: They are the disbelievers of the Quraysh who were slain at Badr.

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: They are the disbelievers of the Quraysh who were slain at Badr.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning the word (Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief) ... the verse, he said: They are the polytheists of the people of Makkah.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq informed me, from some of his companions, from Ata ibn Yasar, who said: This verse was revealed concerning those of the Quraysh who were killed ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin﴾ ... the verse.

Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin﴾: We used to narrate that they are the people of Makkah: Abu Jahl and his companions whom Allah destroyed on the day of Badr. Allah said: ﴿Into Hell, which they will enter; and wretched is the resting place﴾.

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin﴾: They are the leaders of the polytheists on the day of Badr, who caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin ﴿into Hell, which they will enter﴾.

Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin﴾: They are the polytheists of the people of Badr.

Others said about this, narrating:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin, into Hell, which they will enter﴾: He is Jabalah ibn al-Ayham, and those from the Arabs who followed him and joined the Byzantines (al-Rum).

In the same sense as what we have said concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin﴾, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak ﴿and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin﴾: He said: They caused those among their people who obeyed them to settle.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abbas ﴿the abode of ruin﴾: He said: The destruction. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said ﴿and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin﴾: He said: The companions of Badr.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿the abode of ruin﴾: The Fire. He said: Allah has explained that and informed you of it, when He said ﴿into Hell, which they will enter; and wretched is the resting place﴾.

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah ﴿the abode of ruin, into Hell, which they will enter﴾: It is their abode in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 30:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they set up rivals to God, to lead [others] astray from His way. Say: "Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire."﴾

Exalted is He, His remembrance, says: And those who have exchanged the blessing of God for disbelief toward their Lord have set up rivals (andad) to Him. Andad is the plural of nidd (rival), and I have already explained the meaning of nidd earlier, with its evidences, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. What He means is that they set up partners with God.

As [it is related]:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And they set up rivals to God﴾: "The andad are the partners."

* *

As for His saying ﴿to lead [others] astray from His way﴾:

The reciters differed regarding the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it ﴿liyudillu﴾ (to lead astray), meaning: so that they lead people astray from the way of God by what they did of that. The majority of the reciters of Basra read it "liyaḍallu" (that they may go astray), meaning: so that those who set up rivals to God may go astray from the way of God.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Say: "Enjoy yourselves"﴾:

Exalted is He, His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to them: "Enjoy yourselves in the life of this world," as a threat from God to them, not as a permission for them to enjoy it, nor as a command in the manner of worship, but as rebuke, intimidation and warning. He clarified this with His saying ﴿for your destination is the Fire﴾, meaning: enjoy the life of this world, for it is swift to leave you, and to the Fire you will return soon; there you will know the outcome of your enjoyment in the world through disobedience to God and your disbelief in Him therein.

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say to My servants who have believed: establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly, before there comes a Day in which there is no trade and no friendship﴾ (31).

He, mighty is His remembrance, says to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿to My servants who have believed﴾ in you, and affirmed that what you have brought them is from Me, ﴿establish prayer﴾. The meaning is: say to them, "Let them establish the five obligatory prayers within their prescribed limits. And let them spend from what We have provided them, bestowing upon them from Our bounty, secretly and openly; let them render what I have made obligatory upon them of the rights therein, secretly and publicly." ﴿Before there comes a Day in which there is no trade﴾ means: no ransom or compensation will be accepted on it from a soul that has become liable to God's punishment for the disobedience to its Lord it committed in the world, so that its ransom would be accepted and it would be left alone without punishment. God, mighty is His praise, called the ransom a "compensation" because it is the taking of a return from the one who gives it in exchange.

* *

As for His saying ﴿nor friendship﴾:

It means: there is no friendship of a close friend there, so that one would forgive the one deserving punishment from the punishment because of his friendship; rather, there is justice and equity there. The word khilal (friendship) is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "I befriended so-and-so, so I befriend him, friendship (mukhalah) and khilal." From it is the verse of Imru' al-Qays:

I turned my desire away from them out of fear of destruction... and I am not one who is weary of friendship, nor one who is hated by them [[The verse is by Imru' al-Qays (Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili, with commentary by Mustafa al-Saqqa, Halabi edition, p. 40). He said: "al-Radaa" here means disgrace, i.e., I did not turn away from them because I had come to dislike them, nor because they had come to dislike me, but out of fear of disgrace and shame. And "al-khilal" here is the verbal noun of khalla yakhallu khilalan and mukhalah, meaning companionship; the author cited it for this meaning. See Lisan al-'Arab, root kh-l-l. As for the saying of God, Exalted: "no trade therein and no khilal," it has been said: it is a verbal noun of khallala, and it has been said: it is the plural of khullah (with a dammah on the kha'), like jullah and jilal. In Abu 'Ubaydah's Majaz al-Qur'an: "majazah" means exchange of ransom, and "no mukhalah of a close friend." He has another place too, where he makes it the plural of khullah, like jullah, whose plural is jilal; and qullah, whose plural is qilal.]]

The verb ﴿establish﴾ (yuqimu) is in the jussive mood by way of the conditional sense, and its meaning is: the command is intended; say to them, "let them establish the prayer."

⁕ Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Say to My servants who have believed: establish prayer﴾, he meant the five prayers. ﴿And spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly﴾, he said: the zakat of their wealth.

⁕ Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿before there comes a Day in which there is no trade therein and no khilal﴾. Qatadah said: Indeed God, blessed and exalted, knows that in this world there are trades and friendships by which people befriend one another in this world. So a man looks at whom he befriends and with whom he keeps company; if it is for God, let him persist in it, and if it is for other than God, it will cease.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verses 32–33:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth, and sent down water from the sky, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you; and He has subjected for you the ships to sail through the sea by His command, and He has subjected for you the rivers﴾ (32).

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Allah is the One who brought into being the heavens and the earth from nothing, O people, and sent down from the sky rain by which He gave life to the trees and the crops, so they bore fruit as provision for you to eat. ﴿And He subjected for you the ships﴾, which are boats, ﴿to sail through the sea by His command﴾, for you to ride and to carry your goods in them from one land to another. ﴿And He subjected for you the rivers﴾, whose water is drink for you. His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: the One who deserves worship from you and sincere obedience is the One who has these attributes, not those who have no power to harm or benefit, neither themselves nor others, such as your idols and your gods, O polytheists.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us. And al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, meaning al-Za'farani, told us, saying: Shababa told us, saying: Warqa told us. And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: Abdullah told us. And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Shibl told us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And He subjected for you the rivers﴾, he said: "In every land."

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He subjected for you the sun and the moon, both constant in their courses; and He subjected for you the night and the day﴾ (33).

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth﴾, and who did the deeds He described, ﴿and subjected for you the sun and the moon﴾, which follow one another over you, O people, by night and by day, for the good of your souls and your livelihoods. ﴿Both constant﴾ in their alternation over you. It has been said that the meaning is: they are both constant in obedience to Allah.

Khalaf ibn Wasil told us, from a man, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And He subjected for you the sun and the moon, both constant﴾, he said: "Their constancy in obedience to Allah."

* *

As for His saying ﴿And He subjected for you the night and the day﴾:

They alternate over you in succession: when this one departs, that one comes, bringing your benefits and the good of your affairs. So this is for you to make your living through your activity, and that is for you to rest in, and as a mercy from Him to you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 34–36:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him. And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, mankind is must be wrongdoing and ungrateful.﴾ (34)

Allah, may He be remembered, says: And He gave you, in addition to His bounty upon you through what He bestowed upon you, by subjecting to you these things He subjected to you, and the provision He granted you from the vegetation of the earth and its plantings, of every thing you asked Him for and desired from Him. The second object has been omitted, being sufficiently indicated by the word "kull" (every) with the particle "mā" which follows it. The omission is permissible because "min" (of) here signifies partitive, so it stands in for the object by indicating partiality. This is why the omission is permitted. A similar example is His words: ﴿and she was given of all things﴾, meaning: she was given some of everything that existed in her time. It has also been said that this is said for emphasis, like the saying of one who says: "So-and-so knows everything," and "All the people came to him," meaning some of them. Likewise His words: ﴿We opened for them the gates of every thing﴾. It has also been said: there is nothing except that some people have asked for it, so He says: ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him﴾, meaning some of you were given some of what they asked for, and another was given something of what he asked for. This is the view of some grammarians of Basra.

Some grammarians of Kufa said: its meaning is: "And He gave you of all that you asked of Him, had you asked it," as if it were said: "And He gave you of all your asking." He said: Do you not see that you say to a man who has not asked you for anything: "By God, I will give you your request, whatever you ask," even if he has not asked.

As for the people of interpretation, they differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: "And He gave you of all that you desired of Him."

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us; and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: Shababa told us, saying: Warqa told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿of all that you asked of Him﴾: and you desired of Him.

- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Shabl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid; and al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abdullah told us, from Warqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid; and al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him﴾, he said: of all that you asked of Him.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "And He gave you of all that you asked of Him and that you did not ask."

Those who said this:

- Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Khalaf, meaning Ibn Hisham, told us, saying: Mahbub told us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Rukana ibn Hashim, regarding ﴿of all that you asked of Him﴾, and he said: what you asked for and what you did not ask for.

Others read it "wa-ātākum min kullin mā saʾaltumūhu" with tanwin on kull and without its being annexed to "mā", meaning: "And He gave you of every thing you did not ask Him for and did not seek from Him," because the servants did not ask Him for the sun, the moon, the night and the day; He created these for them without their asking Him.

Those who said this:

- Abu Husayn, Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus, related to me, saying: Bazi told us, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding this verse: "And He gave you of all that you asked of Him", he said: what you did not ask for.

- Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih told us, saying: Ubayd told us, from al-Dahhak that he used to read: "min kulla mā saʾaltumūhu" and explain it: He gave you things you did not ask for and did not seek, but I gave you by My mercy and My vastness. Al-Dahhak said: how many a thing has Allah given us that we did not ask for or seek.

- I was told from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: "And He gave you of all that you asked of Him": he says: He gave you things you did not seek nor ask for; Allah has spoken truly, how many a thing Allah has given us that we did not ask Him for and did not occur to us.

- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: "And He gave you of all that you asked of Him", he said: you did not ask Him for of all that He gave you.

The correct view in this matter, in our judgment, is the reading upon which the reciters of the major cities agree, namely the annexation of "kull" to "mā", meaning: "And He gave you some of what you asked for," as we have explained before, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it and their rejection of the other reading.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, mankind is must be wrongdoing and ungrateful.﴾ (34)

Allah, may He be remembered, says: And if you, O people, should count the favor of Allah that He has bestowed upon you, you would not be able to enumerate its number or perform its thanks except by Allah's help to you in it. ﴿Indeed, mankind is must be wrongdoing and ungrateful﴾: he says: indeed, man who exchanges the favor of Allah for disbelief is a wrongdoer, meaning: he is thankful to other than the One who bestowed upon him; thus by his own act he places thanks in other than its place, because Allah is the One who bestowed upon him what He bestowed, and deserved from him sincere worship to Him, yet he worshipped other than Him and set up rivals to lead astray from His way; that is his wrongdoing. His words ﴿ungrateful﴾ mean: he denies the favor of Allah that He bestowed upon him, by diverting worship to other than the One who bestowed upon him, and abandoning obedience to the One who bestowed upon him.

- Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun told us, saying: Mis'ar told us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from Talq ibn Habib, who said: Indeed the right of Allah is too heavy for the servants to fulfill, and the favors of Allah are too many for the servants to count; but rise in the morning repenting and go to sleep repenting.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And when Abraham said: "My Lord, make this city secure, and keep me and my sons far from worshipping idols. My Lord, they have led many people astray. So whoever follows me, he is of me; and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful."﴾ (35–36)

Allah, may He be remembered, says: ﴿And﴾ mention, O Muhammad, ﴿when Abraham said: "My Lord, make this city secure"﴾, meaning the Haram, a secure city for its people and inhabitants, ﴿and keep me and my sons far from worshipping idols﴾. It is said of it: "janabtuhu al-sharr, fa-ana ajnubuhu janban, and jannabtuhu al-sharr, fa-ana ujannibuhu tajnīban, and ajnabtuhu dhalika, fa-ana ujnibuhu ijnaban," and from "janabtu" is the saying of the poet:

And she shakes its cradle out of compassion for it... and keeps away from it our difficult she-camels.

[The verse is cited in Majaz al-Quran of Abu Ubayda (1:342), who said: "I kept the man away from the matter, and he keeps his brother away from evil; and jannabtuhu (with doubled nun) is the same," and he recited the verse, and Dhu al-Rumma doubled it, saying: "And a hair I have lulled at night... I keep away from it the supports and the ropes." He means that the woman is compassionate to her child, so she shakes out its bedding out of fear for it from what would harm it, and does not ride with it on young she-camels, which are the qalāʾis, because their vigor in travel would harm it. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 34–36:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him. And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, mankind is must be wrongdoing and ungrateful.﴾ (34)

Allah, may He be remembered, says: And He gave you, in addition to His bounty upon you through what He bestowed upon you, by subjecting to you these things He subjected to you, and the provision He granted you from the vegetation of the earth and its plantings, of every thing you asked Him for and desired from Him. The second object has been omitted, being sufficiently indicated by the word "kull" (every) with the particle "mā" which follows it. The omission is permissible because "min" (of) here signifies partitive, so it stands in for the object by indicating partiality. This is why the omission is permitted. A similar example is His words: ﴿and she was given of all things﴾, meaning: she was given some of everything that existed in her time. It has also been said that this is said for emphasis, like the saying of one who says: "So-and-so knows everything," and "All the people came to him," meaning some of them. Likewise His words: ﴿We opened for them the gates of every thing﴾. It has also been said: there is nothing except that some people have asked for it, so He says: ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him﴾, meaning some of you were given some of what they asked for, and another was given something of what he asked for. This is the view of some grammarians of Basra.

Some grammarians of Kufa said: its meaning is: "And He gave you of all that you asked of Him, had you asked it," as if it were said: "And He gave you of all your asking." He said: Do you not see that you say to a man who has not asked you for anything: "By God, I will give you your request, whatever you ask," even if he has not asked.

As for the people of interpretation, they differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: "And He gave you of all that you desired of Him."

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us; and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: Shababa told us, saying: Warqa told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿of all that you asked of Him﴾: and you desired of Him.

- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Shabl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid; and al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abdullah told us, from Warqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid; and al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him﴾, he said: of all that you asked of Him.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "And He gave you of all that you asked of Him and that you did not ask."

Those who said this:

- Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Khalaf, meaning Ibn Hisham, told us, saying: Mahbub told us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Rukana ibn Hashim, regarding ﴿of all that you asked of Him﴾, and he said: what you asked for and what you did not ask for.

Others read it "wa-ātākum min kullin mā saʾaltumūhu" with tanwin on kull and without its being annexed to "mā", meaning: "And He gave you of every thing you did not ask Him for and did not seek from Him," because the servants did not ask Him for the sun, the moon, the night and the day; He created these for them without their asking Him.

Those who said this:

- Abu Husayn, Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus, related to me, saying: Bazi told us, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding this verse: "And He gave you of all that you asked of Him", he said: what you did not ask for.

- Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih told us, saying: Ubayd told us, from al-Dahhak that he used to read: "min kulla mā saʾaltumūhu" and explain it: He gave you things you did not ask for and did not seek, but I gave you by My mercy and My vastness. Al-Dahhak said: how many a thing has Allah given us that we did not ask for or seek.
