* *

As for His words: ﴿My Lord, they have led many people astray﴾

He says: O my Lord, indeed the idols have led astray: he says: they have diverted many people from the path of guidance and the way of truth, until they worshipped them and disbelieved in You.

- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿they have led many people astray﴾, meaning the idols.

- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: Hisham told us, from Amr, from Sa'id, from Qatada ﴿they have led many people astray﴾, he said: the idols.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So whoever follows me, he is of me﴾

He says: whoever follows me in what I am upon of believing in You, sincerely worshipping You, and abandoning the worship of idols, then he is of me: he says: he is following my example and acting like my deeds. ﴿And whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾: he says: whoever opposes my command, does not accept from me what I have called him to, and associates others with You, indeed You are Forgiving of the sins of sinners and the erring, by Your bounty, and Merciful to Your servants, pardoning whom You will of them.

As for:

- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿So whoever follows me, he is of me, and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾: Listen to the words of the friend of Allah, Abraham. By Allah, they were not slanderers nor cursers. It was said: indeed among the worst of Allah's servants is every slanderer and curser. The Prophet of Allah, Ibn Maryam, peace be upon him, said: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾

- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Asbagh ibn al-Faraj told us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed me, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith told us, that Bakr ibn Sawada narrated to him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited the words of Abraham ﴿My Lord, they have led many people astray; so whoever follows me, he is of me; and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾, and Jesus said ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾. Then he raised his hands and said: "O Allah, my ummah! O Allah, my ummah!" and wept. Allah, the Exalted, said: "O Jibril, go to Muhammad, and your Lord knows best; ask him what makes him weep." Jibril came to him and asked him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told him what he had said. He said: Allah said: "O Jibril, go to Muhammad and tell him: We shall indeed please you regarding your ummah, and We shall not grieve you."

**The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation, by Your Sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among people incline toward them, and provide them with fruits, that they may be grateful﴾ [14:37]**

Abraham, the Friend of the Merciful, said this statement when he settled Ishmael and his mother Hagar, according to what has been reported, in Mecca.

As follows:

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to me, both saying: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Ayyub, who said: I was informed about Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The first person to run between al-Safa and al-Marwa was the mother of Isma'il, and the first thing the women of the Arabs did in trailing their garments was done by the mother of Isma'il. When she fled from Sarah, she let down her garment so as to conceal her tracks. Abraham brought her, with Isma'il, until he reached with them the site of the House, and he placed them and then returned. She followed him and said: 'To what do you entrust us? To food? To drink?' He did not answer her at all. So she said: 'Has Allah commanded you to do this?' He said: 'Yes.' She said: 'Then He will not neglect us.' He said: She returned, and he went on until, when he reached the ridge of Kada', he turned toward the valley and supplicated, saying: ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation, by Your Sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among people incline toward them, and provide them with fruits, that they may be grateful﴾." He said: The woman had a water-skin with water in it. The water ran out, she became thirsty, and her milk dried up, so the child became thirsty. She looked at which of the mountains was nearest to the ground, and she climbed up al-Safa. She listened carefully, to see whether she could hear a sound or see a person, but she heard nothing. So she came down, and when she reached the valley she ran, though she was not trying to run, like a person exhausted who runs but does not intend to. Then she looked at which of the mountains was nearest to the ground, and she climbed al-Marwa, listened carefully to see whether she could hear a sound or see a person, and she heard a sound. She said, like a person who doubts his own hearing: "Hush," until she was certain. Then she said: "You have made me hear your voice, so help me, for I and those with me are dying." So the angel came and brought her to the place of Zamzam. He struck the ground with his foot, and a spring gushed forth. The woman hastened and gathered it into her water-skin. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on the mother of Isma'il. Had she not hastened, Zamzam would have been a flowing spring (ʿaynan maʿīnan) [Ma'in: a flowing stream upon the face of the earth]." The angel said to her: "Do not fear thirst for the people of this land, for this is only a spring for the drinking of Allah's guests." He also said: "Verily the father of this boy will come, and they will build a house for Allah on this spot." He said: A caravan of Jurhum passing by, heading toward Syria, saw birds over the mountain. They said: "These birds are hovering over water. Do you know of any water in this valley?" They said: "No." So they looked out and found the woman, and they came to her and asked her to let them stay with her. She permitted them. He said: What befalls these people of death came upon her, and she died. Isma'il married a woman from among them. Abraham came and asked about Isma'il's dwelling until he was directed to it, but he did not find him. He found his wife, who was harsh and rude, and he said to her: "When your husband comes, tell him: 'An old man of such and such description came here, and he says to you: I am not pleased with the threshold of your door, so change it,' and then he left." When Isma'il came, she informed him, and he said: "That was my father, and you are the threshold; I am your father's son." So he divorced her and married another woman from among them. Abraham came and reached the dwelling of Isma'il, but did not find him. He found his wife, who was gentle and pleasant, and he said to her: "Where has your husband gone?" She said: "He has gone hunting." He said: "What is your food?" She said: "Meat and water." He said: "O Allah, bless them in their meat and their water, O Allah, bless them in their meat and their water," three times. He said to her: "When your husband comes, inform him: 'An old man of such and such description came here, and he says to you: I am pleased with the threshold of your door, so keep it.'" When Isma'il came, she informed him. He said: Then he came a third time, and the two of them raised the foundations of the House."

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Abbad narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Prophet of Allah Ibrahim came with Isma'il and Hagar, and he placed them in Mecca, at the place of Zamzam. When he departed, Hagar called out to him: "O Ibrahim, I ask you three times: Who commanded you to leave us in a land with no pasture, no crops, no companion, no provision and no water?" He said: "My Lord commanded me." She said: "Then He will not neglect us." He said: When Ibrahim turned away, he said: ﴿Our Lord, You know what we conceal and what we disclose﴾, meaning from grief, ﴿and nothing is hidden from Allah on earth or in heaven﴾. When Isma'il became thirsty, he began to scrape the ground with his heel. Hagar went up to al-Safa, and the valley at that time was deep (lākh), meaning deep. She climbed al-Safa, looked out to see whether she could see anything, but she saw nothing. She came down and reached the valley, ran through it until she came out of it, and came to al-Marwa. She climbed it and looked out to see whether she could see anything, but she saw nothing. She did this seven times. Then she came from al-Marwa to Isma'il, and he was scraping the ground with his heel, and the spring had gushed forth, and it was Zamzam. She began to search the ground with her hand for water, and whenever water gathered, she took it with her cup and poured it into her water-skin. He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on her. If she had left it alone, it would have been a flowing spring running until the Day of Resurrection." He said: The Jurhum were at that time in a valley near Mecca. He said: The birds stayed in the valley when they saw the water. When the Jurhum saw the birds staying in the valley, they said: "They would not stay there unless there were water in it." So they came to Hagar and said: "If you wish, we will be with you and keep you company, and the water will be yours." She said: "Yes." So they stayed with her until Isma'il grew up. Hagar died, and Isma'il married a woman from among them. He said: Then Abraham asked Sarah's permission to visit Hagar, and she permitted him, but stipulated that he should not dismount. Abraham came after Hagar had died. He went to the house of Isma'il and said to his wife: "Where is your husband?" She said: "He is not here. He has gone hunting." Isma'il used to go out of the Sacred Precinct to hunt and then return. Abraham said: "Do you have any hospitality? Do you have food or drink?" She said: "I do not have any, and no one is with me." Abraham said: "When your husband comes, convey my greetings to him and say to him: Let him change the threshold of his door!" Abraham departed, and Isma'il came and found his father's scent. He said to his wife: "Has anyone come to you?" She said: "An old man of such and such description came to me," as if she belittled his matter. He said: "What did he say to you?" She said: "He said to me: Convey my greetings to your husband and say to him: Let him change the threshold of his door." So he divorced her and married another. Abraham remained as long as Allah willed him to remain, then he asked Sarah's permission to visit Isma'il, and she permitted him, but stipulated that he should not dismount. Abraham came until he reached the door of Isma'il, and he said to his wife: "Where is your husband?" She said: "He has gone hunting, and he will come now, God willing. So dismount, may Allah have mercy on you." He said to her: "Do you have any hospitality?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Do you have bread, wheat, dates or barley?" She said: "No." So she brought milk and meat, and he supplicated for them for blessing. Had she brought bread, wheat, barley or dates that day, the land of Allah would have had the most wheat, barley and dates. She said to him: "Dismount until I wash your head." But he did not dismount. So she brought the maqam (standing stone) and placed it under his right side, and he placed his foot upon it, and the mark of his foot remained on it. She washed the right side of his head, then she moved the maqam to his left side and washed his left side. He said to her: "When your husband comes, convey my greetings to him and say to him: Your door's threshold has become right." When Isma'il came and found his father's scent, he said to his wife: "Has anyone come to you?" She said: "Yes, an old man, the most handsome of people in face and the most fragrant in scent. He said to me such and such, and I said to him such and such, and I washed his head, and this is the place of his foot on the maqam." He said: "What did he say to you?" She said: "He said to me: When your husband comes, convey my greetings to him and say to him: Your door's threshold has become right." He said: "That was Abraham." He remained as long as Allah willed him to remain. Then Allah commanded him to build the House, and he and Isma'il built it. When they had built it, it was said: "Proclaim to the people the pilgrimage." So he did not pass by any people without saying: "O people, a house has been built for you, so make pilgrimage to it." No one heard him, no stone, no tree, nor anything else, but it answered: "At Your service, O Allah, at Your service." He said: Between His words ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation, by Your Sacred House﴾ and His words ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has granted me, in old age, Isma'il and Isaac﴾, there were such and such years. 'Ata' did not remember exactly.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation, by Your Sacred House﴾: It is a house that Allah purified from evil, made a qiblah, and made a sanctuary (ḥaram), which the Prophet of Allah Ibrahim chose for his son.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿without cultivation﴾: Mecca had no cultivation at that time.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Kathir informed me. Al-Qasim, in his narration, said: "'Amr ibn Kathir informed me." [Abu Ja'far said]: I altered it and made it: "Ibn Kathir informed me," and I dropped "'Amr," because I do not know of any person called 'Amr ibn Kathir from whom Ibn Jurayj narrated. This narration was related by Ma'mar from Kathir ibn Kathir ibn al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada'ah, and I fear that the narration of Ibn Jurayj is also from Kathir ibn Kathir. He said: I, 'Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, and some people were with Sa'id ibn Jubayr at night, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said to the people: "Ask me before you cannot ask me." The people asked him and asked much. Among what he was asked was: "Is what we have heard about the maqam true?" Sa'id said: "What have you heard?" They said: "We have heard that Abraham, the Messenger of Allah, when he came from Syria, had sworn to his wife that he would not dismount in Mecca until he returned, so the maqam was brought near to him, and he dismounted upon it." Sa'id said: "It is not like that. Ibn 'Abbas related to us, but when there was a matter between the mother of Isma'il and Sarah, what happened was that he brought Isma'il," and then he mentioned a narration like that of Ayyub, except that he added in his narration: The Prophet Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ) said: "They asked to stay with her, and the mother of Isma'il loved company, so they stayed and sent to their families, who came; their food was game. They went out of the Sacred Precinct, and Isma'il went out with them hunting. When he reached [puberty], they married him to a woman, and his mother had died before that." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When he supplicated for them that He bless them in meat and water, he said to her: Is there any grain or other food? She said: No. Had he found grain for her that day, he would have supplicated for her with blessing in it." Ibn 'Abbas said: Then he remained as long as Allah willed him to remain. Then he came and found Isma'il sitting under a large tree near the well, trimming an arrow of his. He greeted him and dismounted to him, sat with him, and said: "O Isma'il, Allah has commanded me with a command." Isma'il said: "Then obey your Lord in what He has commanded you." Abraham said: "He commanded me to build Him a house." Isma'il said: "Build." Ibn 'Abbas said: Abraham pointed to him a mound before him, raised above what was around it, to which the flood reached from its sides, and which was not climbed. He said: They both began to dig out the foundations, raising them, and saying: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us; You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾, ﴿Our Lord, accept from us; You are the Hearer of supplication﴾. Isma'il carried the stones on his neck while the old man Abraham built. When the structure rose high and the old man found it difficult to reach, Isma'il brought this stone near to him, and he stood upon it and built, turning it around the sides of the House until he finished. Ibn 'Abbas said: That is the Station of Abraham and his standing upon it.

⁕ Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Shurayk, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation﴾: He settled Isma'il and his mother in Mecca.

⁕ Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning ﴿I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation﴾: when Isma'il was placed.

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the statement, then, is: "Our Lord, I have settled some of my children in a valley without cultivation." In His words, He indicates that there was no water there at that time, for if there had been water there, He would not have described it as without cultivation, by Your House, which You have made sacred and forbidden to all Your creatures to violate.

It was reported that its sanctity was as follows:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said in his sermon: "This House was first governed by people of Tasm. They disobeyed their Lord, violated its sanctity, and disregarded its rights, so Allah destroyed them. Then people of Jurhum governed it, and they disobeyed their Lord, violated its sanctity, and disregarded its rights, so Allah destroyed them. Then you, O assembly of Quraysh, have governed it, so do not disobey its Lord, do not violate its sanctity, and do not disregard its rights. By Allah, a prayer in it is dearer to me than a hundred prayers elsewhere, and know that sins committed in it are of a similar kind." And He said: ﴿I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation﴾, and He did not mention what the verb applied to. That is because the proper form of the speech would be: "I have settled some of my offspring, a group, or a man, or a people," and that is not permissible with "min" (some of), since it indicates the intended meaning of the speech. The Arabs do this often with it, saying: "We killed some of the Banu Fulan (min Banī Fulān), we ate some of the pasture (min al-Kala'), and we drank some of the water (min al-Ma')." And from this is the saying of Allah, may He be exalted: ﴿Pour upon us some of the water, or some of what Allah has provided you﴾.

If someone says: How did Abraham say, when he settled his son in Mecca, ﴿I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation by Your Sacred House﴾, when it has been reported in the narrations I have mentioned that Abraham built the House a long time afterward? It is said: Several sayings have been given on this, which I have mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah. Among them: its meaning is "by Your Sacred House, which was there before You raised it from the earth, when You raised it in the days of the Flood." And among them: "by Your Sacred House, sacred from the violation of Allah's sanctities in it and the disregard of its rights."

* *

And His words: ﴿Our Lord, that they may establish prayer﴾.

He says: I did this, O our Lord, so that Your obligatory prayers, which You have made obligatory upon them in Your Sacred House, may be performed.

* *

And His words: ﴿So make hearts among people incline toward them﴾.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, informs about His friend Abraham, that he asked in his supplication that He make the hearts of some of His creatures yearn toward the dwellings of his descendants whom he settled in a valley without cultivation by His Sacred House. This was a supplication from him that they be given the pilgrimage to His Sacred House.

As follows:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Abi Qays, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning ﴿hearts from among people incline toward them﴾: "If He had said 'the hearts of people incline toward them,' the Jews, Christians and Magians would have made pilgrimage, but He said 'hearts from among people incline toward them,' and they are the Muslims."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿So make hearts from among people incline toward them﴾: He said: "If it had been the hearts of people, Persia and Rome would have crowded upon it, but it is hearts from among people."

⁕ Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakic narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿So make hearts from among people incline toward them﴾: He said: "If He had said 'the hearts of people incline toward them,' Persia and Rome would have crowded upon them."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 37 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: ʿAli, that is Ibn al-Jaʿd, narrated to us, saying: Jarir informed us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the like of it.
⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from al-Hakam, who said: I asked ʿIkrima about this verse, "So make hearts from among the people incline towards them" (﴿فَاجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً مِنَ النَّاسِ تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِمْ﴾), and he said: "Their hearts incline towards the House (al-Bayt)."
⁕ Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from al-Hakam, from ʿIkrima, ʿAta' and Tawus, "So make hearts from among the people incline towards them" (﴿فَاجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً مِنَ النَّاسِ تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِمْ﴾): "The House; hearts incline towards it, they come to it."
⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn ʿAbbad narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from al-Hakam, who said: I asked ʿAta', Tawus and ʿIkrima about His saying, "So make hearts from among the people incline towards them" (﴿فَاجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً مِنَ النَّاسِ تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِمْ﴾), and they said: "The Hajj."
⁕ Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Shababa and ʿAli ibn al-Jaʿd narrated to us, both saying: Saʿid informed us, from al-Hakam, from ʿAta', Tawus and ʿIkrima, regarding His saying, "So make hearts from among the people incline towards them" (﴿فَاجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً مِنَ النَّاسِ تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِمْ﴾), he said: "Their desire towards Makkah, that they perform Hajj."
⁕ Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from al-Hakam, who said: I asked Tawus, ʿIkrima and ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah about His saying, "So make hearts from among the people incline towards them" (﴿فَاجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً مِنَ النَّاسِ تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِمْ﴾), and they said: "Make their desire the Hajj."
⁕ Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn ʿAbbad narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from ʿAta' ibn al-Saʾib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Had Ibrahim said, 'So make the hearts of the people incline towards them,' it would have longed for it, the Jews, the Christians and all people. But he said, 'Hearts from among the people incline towards them'" (﴿أَفْئِدَةً مِنَ النَّاسِ تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِمْ﴾).
⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying, "So make hearts from among the people incline towards them" (﴿فَاجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً مِنَ النَّاسِ تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِمْ﴾), he said: "They yearn towards them."
⁕ Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn ʿAta' narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Qatada, the like of it.
⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, both saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, the like of it.

Others said: He only prayed that they would long to dwell in Makkah.

Mention of those who said that:
⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying, "So make hearts from among the people incline towards them" (﴿فَاجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً مِنَ النَّاسِ تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِمْ﴾), he said: "Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful, asked God to make some people among the people long to dwell (sukna) or to be residents (sakan) of Makkah."

And His saying, "And provide for them with fruits" (﴿وَارْزُقْهُمْ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ﴾).
He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Provide for them with the fruits of plants and trees, the same as You provided for the inhabitants of the rural areas and the towns which have waters and rivers, even though You made them dwell in a valley without crops or water. So He, mighty is His praise, provided them with that.

As:
⁕ Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, saying: I read to Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Ta'ifi that when Ibrahim prayed for the Sanctuary, "And provide its people with fruits" (﴿وَارْزُقْ أَهْلَهُ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ﴾), God transferred al-Ta'if from Palestine.

And His saying, "That perhaps they may give thanks" (﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْكُرُونَ﴾).
He says: That they may thank You for what You provided them with and the blessing You bestowed upon them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 14, verses 38–40:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Our Lord, You indeed know what we conceal and what we disclose, and nothing is hidden from Allah on the earth or in the heaven﴾ (38)

This is a report from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, about His intimate friend Ibrahim calling Him as a witness to what he intended and aimed at in his supplication and his words: ﴿My Lord, make this city secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols﴾ ... the verse, and that he only intended by that the pleasure of Allah, may He be pleased with him, in his love that his offspring be among those who obey Allah and devote worship to Him in the same manner as he himself did. So he said: "Our Lord, You indeed know what our hearts conceal when we ask You, what we ask of You, and other than that of our states, and what we disclose of our supplication, so we proclaim it aloud, and other than that of our deeds. And nothing that will exist on the earth or in the heaven is hidden from You, O our Lord, for all of that is manifest to You, clear and evident, because You are its Manager and Creator. How could it be hidden from You?"

* *

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has given me, in old age, Ismail and Ishaq. Indeed my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾ (39)

He says: Praise be to Allah, who provided me, in my old age, with the two sons Ismail and Ishaq. ﴿Indeed my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾: he says, indeed my Lord hears my supplication with which I call upon Him, and my words ﴿make this city secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols﴾, and other than that of my supplication and the supplication of others, and everything that any speaker utters, nothing of it is hidden from Him.

⁕ Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Darar ibn Murrah, he said: I heard a shaykh narrating to Sa'id ibn Jubayr, he said: Ibrahim was given good news after one hundred and seventeen years.

* *

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿My Lord, make me one who establishes prayer, and from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication﴾ (40)

He says: My Lord, make me one who performs what You have obligated me to of Your obligation that You have enjoined upon me, which is prayer. ﴿And from my descendants﴾: he says, and also make from my descendants those who establish prayer for You. ﴿Our Lord, and accept my supplication﴾: he says, our Lord, and accept my deed that I perform for You and my worship of You. This is similar to the report transmitted from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed supplication is worship," then he recited: ﴿And your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humiliated﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 41:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the day the reckoning is established.﴾

This is a supplication from Ibrahim, may Allah's blessings be upon him, for his parents, asking forgiveness for them. Allah, mighty is His mention, has informed us that the istighfar of Ibrahim for his father was only ﴿due to a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Ibrahim was tender-hearted and forbearing.﴾

We have already explained the time of his disavowal of him in what preceded, which suffices so that it need not be repeated.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and the believers﴾:

It means: and for the believers among those who follow me in the religion I am upon, who obey you in your command and your prohibition.

* *

As for His saying ﴿on the day the reckoning is established﴾:

It means: the people will stand up for the reckoning. He suffices with mentioning the reckoning instead of mentioning the people, since its meaning is understood.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 14, verses 42–43:**

On the exegesis (ta'wil, interpretation) of His words, ﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only defers them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾ (42)

﴿hastening forward, heads raised, their glance not returning to them, and their hearts empty﴾ (43)

He, may His mention be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And do not think that Allah﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿is unaware﴾, heedless, ﴿of what﴾ these polytheists of your people ﴿do﴾. Rather, He knows them and their deeds, recording them against them, so that He may recompense them with their recompense at the time that has already been decreed in His knowledge for their recompense.

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Thabit narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Maymun ibn Mihran, regarding His words (﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do﴾), he said: "It is a warning to the wrongdoer and a consolation to the wronged."

* *

On the interpretation of His words, ﴿He only defers them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly. Hastening forward, heads raised, their glance not returning to them, and their hearts empty﴾ (43)

He, may His mention be exalted, says: Your Lord only defers these wrongdoers, O Muhammad, who deny you and reject your prophethood, ﴿to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾. That is to say: He only postpones their punishment and the sending down of the torment upon them until a Day when the eyes of creation stare fixedly, and that is the Day of Resurrection.

As related:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾: "By Allah, their eyes will stare fixedly, and they will not return to them."

As for His words ﴿hastening forward﴾, the people of ta'wil differed over its meaning. Some of them said: its meaning is "hurrying."

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id al-Mu'addib, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿hastening forward﴾, he said: "al-Naslan, which is the khabb (a loping gait), or less than the khabb," Abu Sa'id was uncertain, "they will run while looking ahead."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿hastening forward﴾, he said: "Hurrying."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿hastening forward﴾, he said: "Going forth, intent on the caller."

Others said: the meaning of that is: "those who keep their gaze fixed."

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿hastening forward﴾, he said: "By ihtaa' (hastening) he means: looking without blinking."

⁕ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Abu al-Duha, regarding ﴿hastening forward﴾: "It was said: ihtaa' is a constant staring that does not blink."

⁕ Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Mughirah, from Abu al-Khayr ibn Tamim ibn Haddalam, from his father, regarding His words ﴿hastening forward﴾, he said: "Ihtaa' is intense staring (al-tahmij)."

⁕ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿hastening forward﴾, he said: "The intensity of gaze that does not blink."

⁕ Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr informed us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words ﴿hastening forward﴾, he said: "The intensity of gaze without blinking."

⁕ It was reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿hastening forward﴾: "Ihtaa' is intensity of gaze without blinking."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿hastening forward﴾, he said: "Those who keep their gaze fixed."

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the same.

Others said: the meaning of that is: "not raising his head."

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿hastening forward﴾: "The muhti' is the one who does not raise his head."

The usage of ihtaa' in the speech of the Arabs in the sense of "hastening" is more well-known than in the sense of "keeping the gaze fixed." As for ihtaa' in the sense of hastening, the poet's words are:

*"And with a hastening, swift one, as if its halter were on the top of a trunk from the Awal, trimmed (of its branches)."* [[The verse was recited by Ibn Bari in (al-Lisan: awal), and he attributed it to Unayf ibn Jabalah. Its version there is: "When you face him, it is as though he is for the eye a trunk from Awal, trimmed." In Mu'jam ma Ista'jam by al-Bakri: Awal is the first village in Bahrain, and it was said it is an island; if it is a village, it is one of the villages of al-Sayf (with a kasra on the sin). Ibn Muqbil's words support this: "And they are like ships at al-Sayf Awal." Al-Muhti' (as in al-Lisan) is one who keeps his gaze fixed with his eyes open. It was said: one who faces a thing with his sight, and does not lift it from it. Al-Muhti' also means: the hastening, frightened one, which occurs only with fear. His words ﴿hastening forward to the caller﴾ have been explained with both meanings together. End. In (Sarah) he said: "a swift horse (khayl sarh), a swift she-camel in her travel," i.e., quick. The author and Abu Ubaydah cited it in Majaz al-Qur'an (1/342) as evidence that muhti' means hastening.]]

And the other's words:

*"With a hastening, slow-paced one, as if its jadil (halter) were on the qaydum of a cliff-nose of Sawwam, long."* [[The verse was cited by the author of Asas al-Balaghah (h-t-a'): he said it is in the description of a bull; mumna' with a ta': i.e., tall, from al-matu'. In it is "radam" in place of "sawwam." In (al-Lisan: qadam) he said: qaydum of a mountain is a nose that projects from it. He cited the verse and said: Sawwam (like sahab) is the name of a mountain. Qaydum of everything is its front and its chest. Al-mutahti' is like al-muhti', which means hastening. Rasl: easy, in which there is softness. Al-jadil: a braided rope of leather or hair, worn on the neck of a camel or she-camel; its plural is judal. Al-jadil also: a halter braided from leather. Al-ran: the nose of a mountain. Sawwam (like sahab): a mountain, so said al-Bakri and the author of al-Lisan. Mumna': with an nun: the high one that cannot be climbed. In Majaz al-Qur'an: "al-rasl: one who does not burden you with anything." Bi-qaydum: in front. Ran al-jabal: its nose. Sa'um (with a damma on the sad and a hamza on the waw) I have not found thus; rather it is sawwam, with a fatha on the sad and a waw, on the pattern of sahab.]]

* *

On His words ﴿heads raised﴾

That is to say: raising their heads. Iqna' al-ra's is lifting it, and from it is the words of al-Shammakh:

*"They come at dawn to the thorny trees with raised (muqna'at) mouths, their molars like sharpened axes."* [[The verse is by al-Shammakh ibn Dirar (Diwan, p. 56). In it the version is "yubaadirna" in place of "yubakirna," and both have the same meaning. Its commentator said: "yubadirna" from al-mubadarah (hastening). Al-'idah: plural of 'idhah, the greatest of trees. Al-muqna'at: plural of muqni', he means the mouths of camels. Al-nawajidh: the farthest molars. Al-hada': plural of hadaah, which is an axe with two heads. Abu Ubaydah said in Majaz al-Qur'an (1/343), in explaining "muqni'i ru'usihim," its meaning is: raising their heads. He cited al-Shammakh's verse, then said: that is, with heads raised toward the 'idah, so that they may take from it. The 'idah is every tree with thorns. Nawajidhuhunna: their molars. Al-hada': the axe; he meant the one that has no second, and its plural is hada'. Al-waqi': the sharpened, thinned one; it is said: "waqa'a hadidataka" (sharpen your iron). And the hammer is called miq'ah. In (al-Lisan: hada'): al-hada' is like an axe with which stones are pecked, and its edge is sharp. Al-hadaah: a double-headed axe, and its plural is hada', like qasabah and qasab. He said: he likened their teeth to axes that have been sharpened.]]

That is: they come to the thorny trees with their heads raised toward them, so that they may take from them. Also from it is the words of the rajaz-poet:

*"He shook his head toward me and raised it, as if he saw something that gave him hope."* [[Anghada ra'sahu: a movement like one who is tired. Aqna'ahu: raised it. He says: he shook his head toward me, and raised it, looking at me as one looks at a thing in which there is hope for him. Like the previous verse, it is evidence that iqna' means raising.]]

Those who engage in ta'wil have spoken in accordance with what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "Iqna' is raising their heads."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Hasan said: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "Those who raise them."

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the same.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, from Abu Sa'd, who said: al-Hasan said: "The faces of people on the Day of Resurrection will be toward the sky, and no one will look at anyone."

⁕ Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, that he heard Mujahid say, regarding His words ﴿hastening forward, heads raised﴾, he said: "One who raises his head like this," ﴿their glance not returning to them﴾.

⁕ Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "Raising their heads."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "Iqna' is raising their heads."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "The muqni' is the one who raises his head, his gaze fixed, not blinking."

⁕ It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "Raising them."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "The muqni' is the one who raises his head."

⁕ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "Raising their heads."

⁕ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id, from Salim, from Sa'id, regarding ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "Raising their heads."

* *

On His words ﴿their glance not returning to them﴾

He says: their eyes do not return to them because of the intensity of their gaze.

As related:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿their glance not returning to them, and their hearts empty﴾, he said: "Their eyes are staring fixedly."

* *

On His words ﴿and their hearts empty﴾

The people of ta'wil differed over its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is "ruptured, not understanding anything of good."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, regarding His words ﴿and their hearts empty﴾, he said: "Ruptured, not understanding anything."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, the same.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, the same.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Umarah narrated to us, saying: Sahl ibn Amir narrated to us, saying: Malik and Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, the same.

⁕ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, regarding ﴿and their hearts empty﴾, he said: "Ruptured, not understanding anything of good."

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abbad narrated to us, saying: Malik, meaning Ibn Mighwal, narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, except that he said: "Not understanding anything." He did not say "of good."

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, the same.

⁕ Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Mighwal and Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, regarding ﴿and their hearts empty﴾: one of them said: "Hollowed out," and the other said: "Ruptured, not understanding anything."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿and their hearts empty﴾, he said: "There is nothing of good in them, so they are like a ruined house."

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, who said: "There is nothing of good in their hearts, like your saying of a house that has nothing in it, it is only empty air."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and their hearts empty﴾: "The af'idah (hearts): the hearts are empty air, as Allah said, having no intellect and no benefit."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasah, from Abu Bakrah, from Abu Salih, regarding ﴿and their hearts empty﴾, he said: "There is nothing of good in them."

Others said: it means that they do not settle in a place; they move about in their bodies.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn WakI' and Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, both saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Salim, from Sa'id, regarding ﴿and their hearts empty﴾, he said: "They churn in their bodies, having no place in which to settle."

⁕ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id, from Salim, from Sa'id, similarly.

Others said: the meaning of that is: they have come out of their places and become lodged in their throats.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn WakI' and Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, both saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Sa'id, from Masruq, from Abu al-Duha, regarding ﴿and their hearts empty﴾, he said: "They have reached their gullets."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and their hearts empty﴾, he said: "Empty air, nothing in them. They came out of their chests and became lodged in their throats."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and their hearts empty﴾: "They are torn out until they are in their gullets, not coming out of their mouths and not returning to their places."

The most correct of these views in my opinion, regarding the interpretation of this, is the view of the one who said: its meaning is that they are hollow, containing nothing of good, and not understanding anything. This is because the Arabs call every hollow, empty thing "hawa'" (air). From it is the words of Hassan ibn Thabit:

*"Let me convey to Abu Sufyan from me: 'You are hollow, cowardly, and empty air.'"* [[The verse is by Hassan, as in his Diwan, p. 7. Abu Sufyan is al-Mughirah ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the cousin of the Prophet (ﷺ), who used to satirize the Prophet before he embraced Islam. Al-mujawwaf: the hollow-bellied one, meaning the coward; likewise al-nakhib and al-hawa'. In (al-Lisan) he said: al-nakhib: the coward, as if his heart had been torn out, i.e., he has no heart. In (hawa) he said: al-hawa' and al-khawa' are the same. He cited the verse as in the author's version.]]

From it is also the words of another:

*"And do not be among the companions of every cowardly, empty one, hollow, whose bones break."* [[The verse is in (al-Lisan: yara'), as in the author's version. Ibn Bari attributed it to Ka'b al-Amthal(?), and said before it: al-bura'ah and al-bara': the coward who has no intellect or judgment, derived from cane, i.e., by way of comparison to the hollow cane. Al-hawa': the coward whose heart is torn out. Al-ban: a tree that rises and grows tall in straightness, but its wood is not firm. Al-saqab: the pillar of a tent; when it is made of ban wood, it cannot bear weight because of its slight firmness. Juwf: plural of ajwaf (hollow). Al-makasir: the places of breaking, meaning that when ban breaks, it is found to be hollow and weak in bearing.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 14, verses 42–43:**

On the exegesis (ta'wil, interpretation) of His words, ﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only defers them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾ (42)

﴿hastening forward, heads raised, their glance not returning to them, and their hearts empty﴾ (43)

He, may His mention be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And do not think that Allah﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿is unaware﴾, heedless, ﴿of what﴾ these polytheists of your people ﴿do﴾. Rather, He knows them and their deeds, recording them against them, so that He may recompense them with their recompense at the time that has already been decreed in His knowledge for their recompense.

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Thabit narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Maymun ibn Mihran, regarding His words (﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do﴾), he said: "It is a warning to the wrongdoer and a consolation to the wronged."

* *

On the interpretation of His words, ﴿He only defers them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly. Hastening forward, heads raised, their glance not returning to them, and their hearts empty﴾ (43)

He, may His mention be exalted, says: Your Lord only defers these wrongdoers, O Muhammad, who deny you and reject your prophethood, ﴿to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾. That is to say: He only postpones their punishment and the sending down of the torment upon them until a Day when the eyes of creation stare fixedly, and that is the Day of Resurrection.

As related:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾: "By Allah, their eyes will stare fixedly, and they will not return to them."

As for His words ﴿hastening forward﴾, the people of ta'wil differed over its meaning. Some of them said: its meaning is "hurrying."

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id al-Mu'addib, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿hastening forward﴾, he said: "al-Naslan, which is the khabb (a loping gait), or less than the khabb," Abu Sa'id was uncertain, "they will run while looking ahead."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿hastening forward﴾, he said: "Hurrying."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿hastening forward﴾, he said: "Going forth, intent on the caller."

Others said: the meaning of that is: "those who keep their gaze fixed."

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿hastening forward﴾, he said: "By ihtaa' (hastening) he means: looking without blinking."

⁕ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Abu al-Duha, regarding ﴿hastening forward﴾: "It was said: ihtaa' is a constant staring that does not blink."

⁕ Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Mughirah, from Abu al-Khayr ibn Tamim ibn Haddalam, from his father, regarding His words ﴿hastening forward﴾, he said: "Ihtaa' is intense staring (al-tahmij)."

⁕ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿hastening forward﴾, he said: "The intensity of gaze that does not blink."

⁕ Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr informed us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words ﴿hastening forward﴾, he said: "The intensity of gaze without blinking."

⁕ It was reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿hastening forward﴾: "Ihtaa' is intensity of gaze without blinking."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿hastening forward﴾, he said: "Those who keep their gaze fixed."

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the same.

Others said: the meaning of that is: "not raising his head."

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿hastening forward﴾: "The muhti' is the one who does not raise his head."

The usage of ihtaa' in the speech of the Arabs in the sense of "hastening" is more well-known than in the sense of "keeping the gaze fixed." As for ihtaa' in the sense of hastening, the poet's words are:

*"And with a hastening, swift one, as if its halter were on the top of a trunk from the Awal, trimmed (of its branches)."* [[The verse was recited by Ibn Bari in (al-Lisan: awal), and he attributed it to Unayf ibn Jabalah. Its version there is: "When you face him, it is as though he is for the eye a trunk from Awal, trimmed." In Mu'jam ma Ista'jam by al-Bakri: Awal is the first village in Bahrain, and it was said it is an island; if it is a village, it is one of the villages of al-Sayf (with a kasra on the sin). Ibn Muqbil's words support this: "And they are like ships at al-Sayf Awal." Al-Muhti' (as in al-Lisan) is one who keeps his gaze fixed with his eyes open. It was said: one who faces a thing with his sight, and does not lift it from it. Al-Muhti' also means: the hastening, frightened one, which occurs only with fear. His words ﴿hastening forward to the caller﴾ have been explained with both meanings together. End. In (Sarah) he said: "a swift horse (khayl sarh), a swift she-camel in her travel," i.e., quick. The author and Abu Ubaydah cited it in Majaz al-Qur'an (1/342) as evidence that muhti' means hastening.]]

And the other's words:

*"With a hastening, slow-paced one, as if its jadil (halter) were on the qaydum of a cliff-nose of Sawwam, long."* [[The verse was cited by the author of Asas al-Balaghah (h-t-a'): he said it is in the description of a bull; mumna' with a ta': i.e., tall, from al-matu'. In it is "radam" in place of "sawwam." In (al-Lisan: qadam) he said: qaydum of a mountain is a nose that projects from it. He cited the verse and said: Sawwam (like sahab) is the name of a mountain. Qaydum of everything is its front and its chest. Al-mutahti' is like al-muhti', which means hastening. Rasl: easy, in which there is softness. Al-jadil: a braided rope of leather or hair, worn on the neck of a camel or she-camel; its plural is judal. Al-jadil also: a halter braided from leather. Al-ran: the nose of a mountain. Sawwam (like sahab): a mountain, so said al-Bakri and the author of al-Lisan. Mumna': with an nun: the high one that cannot be climbed. In Majaz al-Qur'an: "al-rasl: one who does not burden you with anything." Bi-qaydum: in front. Ran al-jabal: its nose. Sa'um (with a damma on the sad and a hamza on the waw) I have not found thus; rather it is sawwam, with a fatha on the sad and a waw, on the pattern of sahab.]]

* *

On His words ﴿heads raised﴾

That is to say: raising their heads. Iqna' al-ra's is lifting it, and from it is the words of al-Shammakh:

*"They come at dawn to the thorny trees with raised (muqna'at) mouths, their molars like sharpened axes."* [[The verse is by al-Shammakh ibn Dirar (Diwan, p. 56). In it the version is "yubaadirna" in place of "yubakirna," and both have the same meaning. Its commentator said: "yubadirna" from al-mubadarah (hastening). Al-'idah: plural of 'idhah, the greatest of trees. Al-muqna'at: plural of muqni', he means the mouths of camels. Al-nawajidh: the farthest molars. Al-hada': plural of hadaah, which is an axe with two heads. Abu Ubaydah said in Majaz al-Qur'an (1/343), in explaining "muqni'i ru'usihim," its meaning is: raising their heads. He cited al-Shammakh's verse, then said: that is, with heads raised toward the 'idah, so that they may take from it. The 'idah is every tree with thorns. Nawajidhuhunna: their molars. Al-hada': the axe; he meant the one that has no second, and its plural is hada'. Al-waqi': the sharpened, thinned one; it is said: "waqa'a hadidataka" (sharpen your iron). And the hammer is called miq'ah. In (al-Lisan: hada'): al-hada' is like an axe with which stones are pecked, and its edge is sharp. Al-hadaah: a double-headed axe, and its plural is hada', like qasabah and qasab. He said: he likened their teeth to axes that have been sharpened.]]

That is: they come to the thorny trees with their heads raised toward them, so that they may take from them. Also from it is the words of the rajaz-poet:

*"He shook his head toward me and raised it, as if he saw something that gave him hope."* [[Anghada ra'sahu: a movement like one who is tired. Aqna'ahu: raised it. He says: he shook his head toward me, and raised it, looking at me as one looks at a thing in which there is hope for him. Like the previous verse, it is evidence that iqna' means raising.]]

Those who engage in ta'wil have spoken in accordance with what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "Iqna' is raising their heads."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Hasan said: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "Those who raise them."

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the same.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, from Abu Sa'd, who said: al-Hasan said: "The faces of people on the Day of Resurrection will be toward the sky, and no one will look at anyone."

⁕ Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, that he heard Mujahid say, regarding His words ﴿hastening forward, heads raised﴾, he said: "One who raises his head like this," ﴿their glance not returning to them﴾.

⁕ Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "Raising their heads."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "Iqna' is raising their heads."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "The muqni' is the one who raises his head, his gaze fixed, not blinking."

⁕ It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "Raising them."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "The muqni' is the one who raises his head."

⁕ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "Raising their heads."

⁕ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id, from Salim, from Sa'id, regarding ﴿heads raised﴾, he said: "Raising their heads."

* *

On His words ﴿their glance not returning to them﴾

He says: their eyes do not return to them because of the intensity of their gaze.

As related:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿their glance not returning to them, and their hearts empty﴾, he said: "Their eyes are staring fixedly."

* *

On His words ﴿and their hearts empty﴾

The people of ta'wil differed over its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is "ruptured, not understanding anything of good."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, regarding His words ﴿and their hearts empty﴾, he said: "Ruptured, not understanding anything."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, the same.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, the same.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Umarah narrated to us, saying: Sahl ibn Amir narrated to us, saying: Malik and Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, the same.

⁕ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, regarding ﴿and their hearts empty﴾, he said: "Ruptured, not understanding anything of good."

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abbad narrated to us, saying: Malik, meaning Ibn Mighwal, narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, except that he said: "Not understanding anything." He did not say "of good."

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, the same.

⁕ Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Mighwal and Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, regarding ﴿and their hearts empty﴾: one of them said: "Hollowed out," and the other said: "Ruptured, not understanding anything."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿and their hearts empty﴾, he said: "There is nothing of good in them, so they are like a ruined house."

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, who said: "There is nothing of good in their hearts, like your saying of a house that has nothing in it, it is only empty air."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and their hearts empty﴾: "The af'idah (hearts): the hearts are empty air, as Allah said, having no intellect and no benefit."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasah, from Abu Bakrah, from Abu Salih, regarding ﴿and their hearts empty﴾, he said: "There is nothing of good in them."

Others said: it means that they do not settle in a place; they move about in their bodies.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn WakI' and Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, both saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Salim, from Sa'id, regarding ﴿and their hearts empty﴾, he said: "They churn in their bodies, having no place in which to settle."

⁕ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id, from Salim, from Sa'id, similarly.

Others said: the meaning of that is: they have come out of their places and become lodged in their throats.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn WakI' and Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, both saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Sa'id, from Masruq, from Abu al-Duha, regarding ﴿and their hearts empty﴾, he said: "They have reached their gullets."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and their hearts empty﴾, he said: "Empty air, nothing in them. They came out of their chests and became lodged in their throats."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and their hearts empty﴾: "They are torn out until they are in their gullets, not coming out of their mouths and not returning to their places."

The most correct of these views in my opinion, regarding the interpretation of this, is the view of the one who said: its meaning is that they are hollow, containing nothing of good, and not understanding anything. This is because the Arabs call every hollow, empty thing "hawa'" (air). From it is the words of Hassan ibn Thabit:

*"Let me convey to Abu Sufyan from me: 'You are hollow, cowardly, and empty air.'"* [[The verse is by Hassan, as in his Diwan, p. 7. Abu Sufyan is al-Mughirah ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the cousin of the Prophet (ﷺ), who used to satirize the Prophet before he embraced Islam. Al-mujawwaf: the hollow-bellied one, meaning the coward; likewise al-nakhib and al-hawa'. In (al-Lisan) he said: al-nakhib: the coward, as if his heart had been torn out, i.e., he has no heart. In (hawa) he said: al-hawa' and al-khawa' are the same. He cited the verse as in the author's version.]]

From it is also the words of another:

*"And do not be among the companions of every cowardly, empty one, hollow, whose bones break."* [[The verse is in (al-Lisan: yara'), as in the author's version. Ibn Bari attributed it to Ka'b al-Amthal(?), and said before it: al-bura'ah and al-bara': the coward who has no intellect or judgment, derived from cane, i.e., by way of comparison to the hollow cane. Al-hawa': the coward whose heart is torn out. Al-ban: a tree that rises and grows tall in straightness, but its wood is not firm. Al-saqab: the pillar of a tent; when it is made of ban wood, it cannot bear weight because of its slight firmness. Juwf: plural of ajwaf (hollow). Al-makasir: the places of breaking, meaning that when ban breaks, it is found to be hollow and weak in bearing.]]

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And warn mankind of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who did wrong will say: "Our Lord, grant us respite for a short term; we will respond to Your call and follow the messengers."﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: "And warn, O Muhammad, the people to whom I have sent you as one calling to Islam, of what is about to befall them on the Day when the punishment of God comes to them on the Day of Resurrection." ﴿Then those who did wrong will say﴾ means: those who disbelieved in their Lord, and thereby wronged themselves, will say ﴿"Our Lord, grant us respite"﴾, i.e., postpone Your punishment from us and give us time, ﴿"for a short term; we will respond to Your call"﴾ to the truth, "and believe in You, and not associate anything with You," ﴿"and follow the messengers"﴾: they say, "and we will affirm Your messengers and follow them in what they have called us to of obedience to You and submission to Your command."

And in accordance with what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said that:

* Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And warn mankind of the Day when the punishment will come to them﴾, he said: "The Day of Resurrection." ﴿Then those who did wrong will say: "Our Lord, grant us respite for a short term"﴾, he said: "A period in which they may act in the world."

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And warn mankind of the Day when the punishment will come to them﴾, he said: "Warn them in this world before the punishment comes to them."

* * *

As for His words ﴿Then those who did wrong will say﴾:

It is in the nominative (marfu') as a conjunction (ʿatf) upon His words ﴿will come to them﴾ in ﴿the punishment will come to them﴾, and it is not a response (jawab) to the imperative. Had it been a response to His words ﴿And warn mankind﴾, both the nominative and the accusative would have been permissible. As for the accusative, it is as the poet said:

*Yā nāqu sīrī ʿanaqan fasīḥā ... ilā Sulaymāna fanastarīḥā*
(O she-camel, walk with a long, wide stride, to Sulayman, that we may rest.)

[This verse is among the evidences cited by the grammarians; it is by Abu al-Najm al-ʿIjli, addressing his she-camel on her journey to Sulayman ibn ʿAbd al-Malik. "Nāq" is a vocative diminutive, meaning "O she-camel"; "ʿanaqan" is in the accusative as a substitute for the infinitive, i.e., an adjective of an omitted infinitive, meaning a kind of gait of riding beasts and camels, a sustained pace. The poet said... and recited the verse. "Fasīḥ" means wide, an adjective. The evidence lies in "fanastarīḥā," which is in the accusative because it is the response to the imperative introduced by "fa" (the particle of consequence). This is without disagreement, except what is reported from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Sayyāba, that he did not permit this, and he is refuted by it. (See Fara'id al-Qala'id by al-ʿAynī, chapter on the i'rab of the verb.)] And al-Farra' said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 164): His words "The punishment will come to them, then he will say" are in the nominative, following "will come to them," and are not a response to the imperative. Had it been a response, the accusative and the nominative would both be permitted, as the poet said: "O she-camel..." the verse. The nominative is by way of resumption (isti'naf), and the accusative after "fa" as a response to the imperative is also good. There was a shaykh of ours called al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Sayyāba, who taught Muʿadh al-Harra' and his companions, and he used to say: "I do not put the verb in the accusative after the imperative."

The nominative is by way of resumption (isti'naf). It is reported from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Sayyāba that he rejected the accusative in response to the imperative with "fa." Al-Farra' said: al-ʿAlāʾ was the one who taught Muʿadh and his companions.

* * *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Had you not sworn before that there would be for you no cessation?﴾

This is a rebuke from God, exalted is His mention, to the polytheists of Quraysh, after they have entered the Fire because of their denial in the world of resurrection after death. He says to them, when they asked Him to lift the punishment from them and to postpone them so that they might turn back and repent: ﴿"Had you not been"﴾ in the world ﴿"sworn before that there would be for you no cessation"﴾, i.e., no transfer from this world to the Hereafter; and that you would only die and then not be resurrected.

As:

* Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said regarding ﴿Had you not sworn before﴾, like His words (And they swore by God their most solemn oaths that God would not raise up one who dies. Yes indeed) [Q. 16:38]. Then He said ﴿there would be for you no cessation﴾; he said: "The transfer from this world to the Hereafter."

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us; and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Shababa related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us; and al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Salama related to us; and al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allah related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿there would be for you no cessation﴾, he said: "You will not die, O Quraysh."

* Al-Qasim related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from al-Hakam, from ʿAmr ibn Abi Layla, one of the Banu ʿAmir, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi say: "It has reached me, or it was mentioned to me, that the people of the Fire call out: ﴿'Our Lord, grant us respite for a short term; we will respond to Your call and follow the messengers'﴾, and He replies to them: ﴿'Had you not sworn before that there would be for you no cessation, and you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves'﴾ ... to His words ﴿'by which the mountains would be moved'﴾."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 45:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We set forth for you the parables﴾ (14:45).

He, exalted is His mention, says: And you dwelt in this world in the dwellings of those who disbelieved in Allah, and by that they wronged themselves, from the nations that were before you. ﴿And it became clear to you how We dealt with them﴾ means: and you knew how We destroyed them when they became arrogant toward their Lord and persisted in their rebellion and disbelief. ﴿And We set forth for you the parables﴾ means: and We made clear to you, through the examples you observed, the likenesses of what you were upon of associating others with Allah, yet you did not turn back or repent from your disbelief. So now you ask for a delay for repentance, when the punishment that has already come upon you has descended, but that is not going to happen.

And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves﴾, he said: People dwelt in the dwellings of the people of Noah, 'Ad and Thamud, and many generations between them of the nations that were destroyed. ﴿And it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We set forth for you the parables﴾. By Allah, He has sent His messengers and revealed His books, and set forth the parables for you. None is deaf to them except the deaf, and none is deprived of them except the deprived, so understand from Allah His command.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying, ﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves and it became clear to you how We dealt with them﴾, he said: They dwelt in their villages, Madyan, al-Hijr, and the towns whose people Allah punished, and it became clear to you how Allah dealt with them, and He set forth the parables for them.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿the parables﴾, he said: the likenesses.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 46:

The explanation of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they have certainly plotted their plot, and with Allah is [recompense for] their plot, though their plot was [enough] to move mountains.﴾

Allah, the Exalted, says: "Those who wronged themselves have certainly plotted their plot, [those] who then dwelt in their dwellings after them." And their plot which they plotted was [what]:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Aban [[It will come (p. 345) that his name is Abd al-Rahman ibn Daniel, and al-Qurtubi transmitted this name in his tafsir (9: 380), but I have not found it among the names of narrators. Perhaps the two words "Aban" and "Wasil" here are a corruption of "Daniel".]], who said: I heard Ali reciting: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it." He said: There was a tyrant, an arrogant and insolent one, who took the young of vultures and fed them meat until they grew, became strong and thick. Then he and his companion sat in a chest, and they tied the chest to the feet of the vultures, and they hung meat above the chest. Whenever the vultures looked at the meat, they rose and rose. He said to his companion: "What do you see?" He said: "I see the mountains like smoke." They said: "What do you see?" He said: "I see nothing." He said: "Woe to you, lower it, lower it!" So that is His saying: ﴿and their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it﴾.

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Wasil [[Reference to him was already made (p. 244).]], from Ali ibn Abi Talib, the same as the hadith of Yahya ibn Sa'id, and he added in it: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud used to recite it: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it."

* al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Wasil narrated to us [[Reference to him was already made (p. 244).]] that Ali said regarding this verse: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it." He said: That man who disputed with Abraham about his Lord took two young vultures and raised them, then they became thick, strong and grown. He said: A man tied each one of them with a stake to a chest, and starved them, and he and another man sat in the chest. He said: A staff with meat on its head was raised in the chest. He said: They flew, and he kept saying to his companion: "Look, what do you see?" He said: "I see such and such," until he said: "I see the world as if it were a fly." He said: "Lower the staff," so they lowered it and descended. He said: So that is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it." Abu Ishaq said: Likewise it is in the reading of Abdullah: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it."

* Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it." He said: It was the plot of Persia. He claimed that Bukhtanasr went out with vultures, and made for himself a chest to enter, and placed spears at its ends with meat above them. I think he said: The vultures went toward the meat until his sight was cut off from the earth and its people. Then he was called: "O tyrant, where do you intend to go?" He was startled. Then he heard the voice above him, so he lowered the spears, and the vultures lowered themselves.
