The mountains were terrified by their thunder, and the mountains nearly moved from it because of the sensation of that. So that is His saying: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it."

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: "And they have certainly plotted their plot, and with Allah is their plot, though their plot was [enough] to..." He read it thus: "kāda makruhum latazulu minhu al-jibal" (though their plot almost [kāda] moved the mountains from it). He said: Some of those who had passed starved vultures, then placed a chest over them and entered it, then placed spears at their ends with meat on them. They kept seeing the meat and going off, until his sight ended. He was called: "O tyrant, where do you intend to go?" So he lowered the spears, and the vultures lowered themselves. The mountains were terrified and thought the Hour had come, and they nearly moved, so that is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it."

Ibn Jurayj said: Amr ibn Dinar informed me, from Ikrimah, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, that he used to recite: "Wa in kāda makruhum latazulu minhu al-jibal."

* Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated this hadith to me, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, that he used to recite in a manner like: "latazulu," with a fatha on the first lam and a damma on the second.

* Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Daniel [[Reference to him was already made (p. 244).]], who said: I heard Ali say: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it."

* Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Daniel [[Reference to him was already made (p. 244).]], who said: I heard Ali say: "Wa in kāda makruhum latazulu minhu al-jibal." He said: Then Ali began to narrate, saying: It was revealed concerning a tyrant among the tyrants. He said: "I will not stop until I know what is in the heaven." Then he took vultures and began feeding them meat until they became thick, strong and grown, and he mentioned a similar hadith to the hadith of Shu'bah.

* Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud al-Hadrami narrated to us, from Yaqub, from Hafs ibn Humayd or Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it." He said: Namrud, the owner of the vultures, ordered a chest to be made and made a man go with him. Then he ordered the vultures, and they carried it. When it ascended, he said to his companion: "What do you see?" He said: "I see the water and an island," meaning the world. Then he ascended and said to his companion: "What do you see?" He said: "We do not increase in distance from the sky except by distance." He said: "Descend" — and another said: "He was called" — "O tyrant, where do you intend to go?" He said: The mountains heard the rustling of the vultures, and they thought it was a command from the sky, so they nearly moved. That is His saying: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it."

* Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, that Anas used to recite: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it."

Others said: Their plot was their associating partners with Allah and their fabrication against Him.

Mention of those who said that:

* Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it," meaning: their shirk, like His saying: ﴿The heavens are almost torn apart from it﴾.

* Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: al-Maharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it." He said: It is like His saying: ﴿And they say: "The Most Merciful has taken a son." You have certainly produced a monstrous thing. The heavens are about to burst from it, and the earth split open, and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾.

* Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: ﴿And if their plot was﴾, then he mentioned the like of it.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, that al-Hasan used to say: "It was too insignificant and too small before Allah for the mountains to be moved by it," describing them with that. Qatadah said: In the codex of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "Wa in kāda makruhum latazulu minhu al-jibal." Qatadah would say at that point: ﴿The heavens are almost torn apart from it, and the earth is split open, and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾, meaning: because of their saying that.

* Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it." He said: That was when they ascribed a son to Allah. And in another verse he said: ﴿The heavens are almost torn apart from it, and the earth is split open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they ascribe to the Most Merciful a son﴾.

It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿And if their plot was﴾, in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "Wa in kāda makruhum latazulu minhu al-jibal," it is like His saying: ﴿The heavens are almost torn apart from it, and the earth is split open, and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾.

The reciters differed regarding the reading of His saying: ﴿latazula minhu al-jibal﴾. The majority of reciters of Hijaz, Madinah and Iraq, except al-Kisa'i, read: ﴿And if their plot was [such that] the mountains would be moved by it﴾ with a kasra on the first lam and a fatha on the second, meaning: "And their plot was not such that the mountains would be moved by it." Al-Kisa'i read: "Wa in kāna makruhum latazulu minhu al-jibal" with a fatha on the first lam and a damma on the second, according to the interpretation of the reading of those who read: "Wa in kāda makruhum latazulu minhu al-jibal" from the earlier ones whose sayings I have mentioned, meaning: their plot was so intense that the mountains were moved by it, or nearly moved by it. Al-Kisa'i used to narrate from Hamzah, from Shibl, from Mujahid, that he used to read it in the manner of his reading: "Wa in kāna makruhum latazulu minhu al-jibal" with the damma on "tazulu."

* Al-Harith narrated to me this from al-Qasim, from him.

The correct reading in our view is the reading of the one who reads: ﴿And if their plot was [such that] the mountains would be moved by it﴾ with a kasra on the first lam and a fatha on the second, meaning: "And their plot was not such that the mountains would be moved by it."

We said that this is the correct one because if the first lam is read with a fatha, the meaning of the speech becomes: "Their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it," and if they had moved, they would not have remained firm; and their remaining in their state indicates that they did not move. Also, there is the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon this, and that suffices as evidence for its soundness and the corruption of other readings without other proof.

If someone supposes that this is not a consensus of the authorities, since among the Companions and Successors some read it thus, the matter is contrary to what he supposes. Those who read it with a fatha on the first lam and a damma on the second read: "Wa in kāda makruhum" with the dal, and when it is recited thus, the sound reading with "Wa in kāda" is a fatha on the first lam and a damma on the second as they read. But it is not permissible in our view to recite it that way, because our codices differ from that; our codices are written with the nun, not the dal. Since that is so, it is not permissible for anyone to alter the orthography of the codices of the Muslims. And if that is not permissible, the sound reading is only what the readers of the regions hold, not those who deviated in their reading from them.

In agreement with what we have said regarding the meaning of ﴿And if their plot was﴾, a group of the people of interpretation said so.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿And they have certainly plotted their plot, and with Allah is their plot, though their plot was [such that] the mountains would be moved by it﴾, means: "Their plot was not such that the mountains would be moved by it."

* Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: al-Hasan said, regarding His saying: ﴿And if their plot was [such that] the mountains would be moved by it﴾: their plot was not such that the mountains would be moved by it.

* Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, who said: Their plot was not such that the mountains would be moved by it.

* Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, from Yunus and Amr, from al-Hasan, ﴿And if their plot was [such that] the mountains would be moved by it﴾. They both said: al-Hasan used to say: "And if their plot was [such that] the mountains would be moved by it" means: it was too weak and too feeble for the mountains to be moved by it.

He said: Harun said: Yunus informed me, from al-Hasan, who said: Four [verses] in the Qur'an: ﴿And if their plot was [such that] the mountains would be moved by it﴾, meaning: their plot was not such that the mountains would be moved by it; and His saying: ﴿We would have taken it from Us, if We were doers﴾, meaning: "We were not doers"; and His saying: ﴿If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers﴾, meaning: "The Most Merciful had no son"; and His saying: ﴿And We had established them in that in which We have not established you﴾, meaning: "We did not establish you in it."

Harun said: Amr ibn Asbat narrated these to me from al-Hasan, and he added one more: ﴿So if you are in doubt﴾, meaning: "You were not in doubt" about ﴿what We have sent down to you﴾.

So the more appropriate of what is said as the correct interpretation of the verse, since the reading that I mentioned is the correct one, for the proof we have shown in His saying: ﴿And they have certainly plotted their plot, and with Allah is their plot, and though their plot was [such that] the mountains would be moved by it﴾. Those who wronged themselves associated partners with their Lord and fabricated against Him their fabrication. With Allah is the knowledge of their shirk and their fabrication against Him, and He is the one who will punish them for that with the punishment they deserve. Their shirk and their fabrication against Allah were not such that the mountains would be moved by it; rather, they harmed only themselves, and the evil of their scheme returned only upon them.

* al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Waki' ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shamir, from Ali, who said: Treachery is deceit, and deceit is disbelief.

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So do not think that Allah would break His promise to His messengers. Indeed, Allah is Mighty, Able of retribution.﴾ (14:47)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿So do not think that Allah would break His promise﴾ which He promised to those who denied them, and rejected what they brought them from Him. He, exalted is His remembrance, said this to His Prophet as a confirmation and a strengthening of his resolve, and to inform him that He will send down His wrath upon those who denied him and rejected his prophethood, and rejected what he brought from Allah, in the same manner as what He sent down upon those who followed their way among the nations before them, who were upon the same path of denying their messengers, rejecting their prophethood, and rejecting what they brought them from Allah.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is Mighty, Able of retribution﴾

By His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is Mighty﴾ He means that nothing can prevent Him from punishing whom He wills; He is able over everyone who seeks Him, and no one can escape Him by fleeing from Him. ﴿Able of retribution﴾ against those who disbelieved in His messengers, denied them, rejected their prophethood, associated others with Him, and took another god alongside Him.

The word ﴿mukhlif﴾ is annexed to the promise (wa'd), which is a verbal noun (masdar), because it stands in the position of a noun. The word ﴿rusulahu﴾ is in the accusative according to the meaning, since the meaning is: "So do not think that Allah would break His messengers' promise." Although "al-wa'd" is in the genitive by the annexation of "mukhlif" to it, it is in the sense of the accusative. This is because the verb "ikhlaf" (breaking) takes two different objects, as in the saying of a speaker: "I clothed Abdullah with a garment, and I made him enter a house." When the verb is of this kind, taking two different objects, it is permissible to place either of them first, and to put in the genitive the one that follows the verbal form which has the appearance of a noun, while putting the second in the accusative. So one says: "Ana mudkhilu Abdillah al-dar" and "Ana mudkhilu al-dara Abdallah." If you place "al-dar" next to "mudkhil" and postpone "Abdallah," you put "al-dar" in the genitive, since "mudkhil" is annexed to it, and "Abdallah" in the accusative. If "Abdallah" is placed next to it and "al-dar" postponed, "Abdallah" is in the genitive by the annexation of "mudkhil" to it, and "al-dar" is in the accusative. This is done in this way because the verb, that is "mudkhil," governs each of the two in the accusative in the same way as it governs the other. From this is the saying of the poet:

*You see the bull in it, his head making entry into the shade,*
*while the rest of him is exposed to the sun, entirely.*

Here he annexed "mudkhil" to "al-zill" (the shade), and put "al-ra's" (the head) in the accusative, and the meaning of the statement is: "entering his head the shade."

From this is another's saying:

*Sprinkle me with good, so that neither I nor my praise*
*be like one who chisels a rock one day with a feather (?)*

The "'asil" is a feather with which perfume is gathered. The meaning of the statement is: "like one who chisels a rock one day with an 'asil."

Likewise another's saying:

*Many a paternal cousin of Sulaymá, quick and hasty,*
*a cook of the hours of sleep, whose laziness is increased.*

The meaning of the statement is: "a cook whose laziness has increased the hours of sleep."

As for one who reads it ﴿So do not think that Allah would break the promise of His messengers, they being His messengers﴾, we have already explained the weakness of this reading in the Arabic language in the commentary on Surah al-An'am, at His saying ﴿And so their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children﴾, with what suffices instead of repeating it here.

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿On the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens [too]; and they will come forth before God, the One, the Subduer﴾ (14:48)**

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Indeed God is Lord of retribution ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens﴾ against the polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, from Quraysh, and all who disbelieved in God and denied your prophethood and the prophethood of the messengers before you. Here "yawma" (on the day) is connected to "al-intiqam" (retribution).

There is disagreement about the meaning of His words ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾. Some of them said: The meaning is: on the day the earth on which people are today, in the abode of this world, is changed to another earth, and it becomes a white earth like silver.

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard 'Amr ibn Maymun narrating, from 'Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud), that he said regarding this verse ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens﴾: "[It is] an earth like pure silver, in which no blood has been shed and no sin has been committed. The caller makes them hear, and the sight penetrates them, barefoot, naked, standing, I think he said: as they were created, until the sweat bridles them, standing alone."

Shu'bah said: Then I heard him say: I heard 'Amr ibn Maymun, but he did not mention 'Abdullah. Then I went back to him about it, and he said: Hubayrah narrated it to me, from 'Abdullah.

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Abbad narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah informed us, saying: Abu Ishaq informed us, saying: I heard 'Amr ibn Maymun, and perhaps he would say: "'Abdullah said," and perhaps he would not say it. So I said to him: "From 'Abdullah?" He said: I heard 'Amr ibn Maymun say ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾: "[It is] an earth like white, pure silver, in which no blood has been shed and no sin has been committed; the sight penetrates them, and the caller makes them hear, barefoot, naked as they were created." He said: I think he said: "standing, until the sweat bridles them."

⁕ Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His words ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens﴾, he said: "It will be changed into a white, pure earth, as if it were silver, in which no forbidden blood has been spilled and no sin has been committed."

⁕ Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abdullah, regarding His words ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾, he said: "The earth of Paradise is white and pure, no sin has been committed in it, the caller makes them hear, the sight penetrates it, barefoot, naked, standing, the sweat bridles them."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾, he said: "An earth white like silver, in which no forbidden blood has been spilled and no sin has been committed."

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Abbad narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, saying: 'Asim ibn Bahdalah informed us, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, that he recited this verse ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens, and they will come forth before God, the One, the Subduer﴾, and he said: "An earth white as if it were an ingot of silver will be brought, in which no blood has been shed and no sin has been committed upon it." He said: "The first thing judged among people in it will be concerning blood."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Sinan, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Abu Jubayrah, from Zayd, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent for the Jews and said: "Do you know why I have sent for them?" They said: "God and His Messenger know best." He said: "I have sent for them to ask them about the saying of God ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾: that on that day it will be white like silver." When they came, he asked them, and they said: "It will be white like the naqiy (white bread)."[[In Lisan al-'Arab: "And in the hadith: 'People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection upon a white earth, like a loaf of naqiy (bread).' Abu 'Ubayd said: al-naqiy is leavened bread (al-hawwari)."]]

⁕ Abu Isma'il al-Tirmidhi narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Sinan ibn Sa'd, from Anas ibn Malik, that he recited this verse ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾, and said: "God will change it on the Day of Resurrection into an earth of silver, on which no sins have been committed, and the Almighty, blessed and exalted is He, will descend upon it."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾, he said: "An earth like silver." Al-Hasan added in his narration from Shababah: "And the heavens likewise, also like silver."

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾, he said: "An earth like silver, and the heavens likewise."

⁕ Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, saying: Abu Hazim narrated to me, saying: I heard Sahl ibn Sa'd say: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection upon a white, pure earth, like a loaf of naqiy (bread)." Sahl, or someone else, said: "There is no landmark in it other than it."

Others said: It will be changed into fire.

Those who said this:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Qays ibn al-Sakan, who said: 'Abdullah said: "The whole earth will be fire on the Day of Resurrection, and Paradise beyond it, you see its cups and its maidens. By the One in whose hand is the soul of 'Abdullah, a man will sweat so much that his foot sinks into the earth, then it rises until it reaches his nose, and he has not yet been touched by the reckoning." They said: "Why is that, O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman?" He said: "Because of what people see and what they encounter."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Khaythamah, who said: 'Abdullah said: "The whole earth on the Day of Resurrection is fire, and Paradise beyond it, you see its maidens and its cups, and the sweat bridles people, or the sweat reaches them, and they have not reached the reckoning."

Others said: Rather, the earth will be changed into another earth of silver.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Mughirah ibn Malik narrating from al-Mujashi' or al-Mujashi'i, Abu Musa doubted it, from one who heard 'Ali say regarding this verse ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾: "The earth will be of silver, and Paradise of gold."

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Shu'bah, from al-Mughirah ibn Malik, who said: A man from Banu Mujashi' called 'Abd al-Karim, or the son of 'Abd al-Karim, narrated to me, said: This man narrated to me, I think in Samarqand, that he heard 'Ali ibn Abi Talib recite this verse ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾, and say: "The earth is of silver, and Paradise of gold."

⁕ Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Mughirah ibn Malik, from a man from Banu Mujashi' called 'Abd al-Karim, or known as Abu 'Abd al-Karim, who said: He had me stand before a man in Khurasan, and he said: "This one narrated to me that he heard 'Ali ibn Abi Talib," and he mentioned something similar.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾ ... the verse, and he claimed that it will be silver.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Sinan ibn Sa'd, from Anas ibn Malik who said: "God will change it on the Day of Resurrection into an earth of silver."

Others said: He will change it into a loaf of bread.

Those who said this:

⁕ Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Sa'd Sa'id ibn Dall of Saghaniyan narrated to us, saying: al-Jarud ibn Mu'adh al-Tirmidhi narrated to us, saying: Waki' ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, from 'Umar ibn Bashir al-Hamdani, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾, he said: "It will be changed into a white loaf of bread from which the believer eats from beneath his feet."

⁕ Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, or from Muhammad ibn Qays, ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾, he said: "A loaf from which the believers eat beneath their feet."

Others said: The earth will be changed into other than the earth.

Those who said this:

⁕ 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Ka'b, regarding His saying ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens﴾, he said: "The heavens will become gardens, and the place of the sea will become fire." He said: "And the earth will be changed into other than it."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rafi' al-Madani, from Yazid, from a man of the Ansar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "On the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens, He will spread it out, level it, and stretch it like a stretched leather hide of 'Ukaz; you will not see in it any crookedness or unevenness. Then God will drive the creation with a single driving, and they will be on this changed earth in the same positions they were in the first earth: what was in its belly remains in its belly, and what was on its back remains on its back. That is when He will roll up the heavens like the rolling of a scroll for the writing, then He will spread them out, then the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Qays narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, who said: People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in a white earth, in which no sin has been committed, for the length of forty years; the sweat will bridle them.

'Ā'ishah said about this:

⁕ Ibn Abi al-Shawarib, Humayd ibn Mas'adah and Ibn Bazi' narrated to us, they said: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, from Dawud, from 'Amir, from 'Ā'ishah, who said: I said: "O Messenger of God, when the earth is changed to other than the earth, and they come forth before God, the One, the Subduer, where will people be on that day?" He said: "On the Sirat (Path)."

⁕ Humayd ibn Mas'adah and Ibn Bazi' narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Amir, from 'Ā'ishah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly.

⁕ Ishaq ibn Shahin narrated to me, saying: Khalid narrated to us, from Dawud, from 'Amir, from Masruq, who said: I said to 'Ā'ishah: "O Mother of the Believers, have you seen the saying of God ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens, and they come forth before God, the One, the Subduer﴾: where will people be on that day?" She said: "I asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about that, and he said: 'On the Sirat.'"

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Anbasah al-Warraq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahim, meaning Ibn Sulayman al-Razi, narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Amir, from Masruq, from 'Ā'ishah, who said: "I asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the saying of God ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾. I said: 'O Messenger of God, when the earth is changed to other than the earth, where will people be?' He said: 'On the Sirat.'"

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: 'Asim ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Zakariyya narrated to us, from Dawud, from 'Amir, from Masruq, from 'Ā'ishah, similarly.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Amir, from 'Ā'ishah, Mother of the Believers, who said: "I am the first of people to ask the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about this verse," then he mentioned something similar.

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Rab'i ibn Ibrahim al-Asadi, brother of Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Amir, who said: 'Ā'ishah said: "O Messenger of God, have you seen when the earth is changed to other than the earth, where will people be on that day?" He said: "On the Sirat."

⁕ Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Jund narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim informed me, saying: I heard al-Hasan say: 'Ā'ishah said: "O Messenger of God, ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾, so where will people be on that day?" He said: "Indeed, no one has asked me about this matter other than you. [They will be] on the Sirat, O 'Ā'ishah."

⁕ Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: al-Walid narrated to me, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Hassan ibn Bilal al-Muzani, from 'Ā'ishah: that she asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the saying of God ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens﴾. She said: "O Messenger of God, then where will people be on that day?" He said: "You have asked me about a matter that no one of my community has asked me about. That is when people will be on the bridge (jisr) of Hell."[[In Taj al-'Arus: "al-jisr, with a fatha, is that which one crosses over, like a causeway or similar; it is also pronounced with a kasra; both are dialects."]]

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens﴾: It was mentioned to us that 'Ā'ishah said: "O Messenger of God, then where will people be on that day?" He said: "You have asked about a matter that no one of my community has asked me about before you." He said: "They will be on that day on the bridge of Hell."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, that 'Ā'ishah asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: "On the Sirat."

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Asma', from Thawban, who said: "A Jewish rabbi asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ), saying: 'Where will people be on the day the earth is changed to other than the earth?' He said: 'They will be in darkness, below the bridge.'"

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Awn narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Thawban al-Kala'i narrated to us, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, who said: A rabbi of the Jews came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Have you seen, when God says in His Book ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens﴾, where will the creation be at that time?" He said: "They are the guests of God, and what is with Him will not fail them."

The most correct of these sayings in interpretation is the saying of the one who said: Its meaning is: on the day the earth on which we are today is changed on the Day of Resurrection to other than it, and likewise the heavens, which are today, will be changed to other than them, as His majestic praise said. It is permissible that the changed earth is another earth of silver, and it is permissible that it is fire, and it is permissible that it is bread, and it is permissible that it is other than that. There is no report on this from us, in a manner that must be accepted, as to which of these it will be. So there is no saying on this that is correct except what the apparent meaning of the revelation (tanzil) indicates.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of His words ﴿and the heavens﴾.

Those who said this:

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid ﴿on the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾, he said: "An earth like silver, ﴿and the heavens﴾ likewise."

* *

As for His words ﴿and they will come forth before God, the One, the Subduer﴾:

He says: And they will appear before God, the One alone in lordship, who overpowers every thing, defeating it and directing it as He wills, however He wills, so He gives life to His creation when He wills and causes them to die when He wills; nothing overcomes Him, and nothing subdues Him; and they will come out of their graves alive for the standing place of the Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 49–51:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And you will see the criminals that Day bound together in shackles (49), their garments of pitch, and the Fire covering their faces (50), so that Allah may recompense every soul for what it has earned. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning (51).﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: You will see those who disbelieved in Allah, who committed shirk in the world, on that Day, meaning the Day when the earth will be changed into other than the earth, and the heavens [too]. ﴿Bound together in shackles﴾ means: their hands and feet bound to their necks with shackles, which are restraints of iron collars and chains. Its singular is ṣafad (شد/fetter), and one says of it: "I fettered him in the ṣafad, ṣafdan and ṣifādan." Al-ṣifād is the fetter, and from it comes the verse of ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm:

"They returned with plunder and captives, and we returned with kings bound in fetters (muṣaffadīn)." [The line is by ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm from his Muʿallaqa. Ābū means "they returned." Al-nihāb is the plural of nahb (plunder). Al-muṣaffadūn are those shackled with fetters; the singular is ṣafd, which is the shackle. He means: we conquered them, and did not turn to their spoils or their wealth, but aimed at their kings and fettered them in iron. In the Lisan (ṣafh): al-ṣifād is a rope with which one is bound, or a shackle; it is also al-ṣafd (with the fāʾ sukun or with a vowel). Its plural is al-aṣfād. Ibn Sīdah said: we do not know it to be broken in any other way. In the revelation: "bound together in shackles." It was said: they are the chains. It was also said: the fetters. Its singular is ṣafd. See the Sharḥ al-Muʿallaqāt al-Sabʿ of al-Zawzanī and the Sharḥ al-Qaṣāʾid al-ʿAshr of al-Tibrīzī.]

Whoever makes the singular of this ṣifād, its plural is ṣufud and not aṣfād. As for the meaning of giving, one says from it: aṣfadtuhu iṣfādan, as al-Aʿshā said:

"I hosted him one day, and he honoured my seat, and gave me a guide when I was old and infirm." [The line is by al-Aʿshā (Lisan: ṣfd; Diwan of al-Aʿshā, Cairo ed., p. 65) from a qasida in praise of Hawdhah ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥanafī, and satirising al-Ḥārith ibn Waʿlah ibn Mujālid al-Raqqāshī. Tadayyaftuhu: I stayed with him as a guest; aṣfadanī: gave me, here from ṣafd meaning gift. He means: when I visited Hawdhah in Jaw, he honoured my reception and brought me close to his assembly, and gave me a guide to lead me, seeing the signs of weakness, fatigue and poor sight. The Diwan version has ʿalā in place of ʿinda.]

It has also been said of giving: ṣafadanī ṣafdan, as al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī said:

"This is praise; if you hear its speaker, I did not refuse, may you avoid blame, with the ṣafad." [This line is by al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī (Mukhtār al-Shiʿr al-Jāhilī with the commentary of Muṣṭafā al-Saqqā, Ḥalabī edition, p. 155). Al-ṣafd here means gift, like the previous. In its second hemistich: "fa-lam aʿrid" in place of "famā ʿaraḍt".]

Concerning the meaning of His words ﴿bound together in shackles﴾, the people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

- Al-Muthannā told me, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiyah told me, on the authority of ʿAlī, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words ﴿bound together in shackles﴾: he said: in bondage.
- Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Dāmaghānī told me, he said: Ibn al-Mubārak told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Ḍaḥḥāk, he said: al-aṣfād are the chains.
- Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Maʿmar, on the authority of Qatādah, ﴿bound together in shackles﴾, he said: bound together in fetters and iron collars.
- al-Qāsim told us, he said: al-Ḥusayn told us, he said: ʿAlī ibn Hāshim ibn al-Barīd told us, he said: I heard al-Aʿmash say: al-ṣafd is the fetter.
- Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿bound together in shackles﴾: their hands, feet and necks were fettered in it, and al-aṣfād are the shackles.

* *

And His words ﴿their garments of pitch﴾

He means: their shirts that they wear; its singular is sirbāl, as Imruʾ al-Qays said:

"A playful one who makes me forget my garment when I stand." [This is the second half of a line by Imruʾ al-Qays ibn Ḥujr from his lengthy lamiyya (54 verses), whose first half is "wa-mithlaki bayḍāʾ al-ʿawāriḍ ṭifla" (Mukhtār al-Shiʿr al-Jāhilī, with the commentary of Muṣṭafā al-Saqqā, Ḥalabī edition, p. 37). This line is omitted from the Diwan copy with the commentary of the vizier Abū Bakr ʿĀṣim ibn Ayyūb al-Baṭalyawsī, but is present in the copy of al-Aʿlam al-Shantamarī, and in what al-Baghdādī quoted in Khizānat al-Adab al-Kubrā from the verses of the qasida (vol. 1: 197), where he cited it after Imruʾ al-Qays's words: "wa-amnaʿu ʿirsī an yazinna bihā al-khālī". The "wāw" in the line is the wāw of rubba (many a). The address is to Basbāsa. Al-ʿāriḍ and al-ʿāriḍah are the cheek's surface and the side of the neck, the side of the face, and what faces you of a thing; and from the face is what appears in laughter. Al-ṭifla (with fatḥa) is one soft in body. Al-laʿūb is one graceful in coquetry. Al-sirbāl is the shirt; he means: she takes my heart away until I forget my shirt. The evidence in it, according to al-Ṭabarī, is that sirbāl is the shirt in the Arab usage.]

- Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿their garments﴾: he said: al-sarābīl are the shirts.

* *

And His words ﴿of pitch﴾

He means: of the pitch with which camels are treated for mange. It has three dialectal forms: one says qiṭrān and qaṭrān (with fatḥa on the qāf and sukūn on the ṭāʾ). It was also said that ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar used to read "min qiṭrin" with kasra on the qāf and sukūn on the ṭāʾ, and from it is the verse of Abū al-Najm:

"A dark-coloured one, as if the sweat, fully exuded, clothed him in pitch and coarse hair-cloth." [The line is in (Lisan al-ʿArab: nataḥ). He said: al-natḥ is the emergence of sweat from the skin, and of grease from the ... and the dew from the soil. The Jawharī said: al-natḥ is perspiration; manātiḥ al-ʿaraq are its exits from the skin, and he recited: "jawn..." etc. Al-qiṭrān (with fatḥa, with kasra, and like ẓarbān) is the resin of the pine, which is boiled and then camels are treated with it; and their garments were made of it because it greatly intensifies the fire in the skins (from Tāj al-ʿArūs). Al-masūḥ is the plural of misḥ, with kasra on the mīm, which is a garment of hair; its plurals are amsāḥ and masūḥ.]

with kasra on the qāf, and he also said:

"As if qiṭrān, when they follow it, the wind throws it toward its course." [This evidence is like the previous one, showing that qiṭrān has kasra on the qāf.]

with kasra.

Those who read it thus have said what we have said regarding it.

Those who said that:

- al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb told us, on the authority of Saʿīd, on the authority of Qatādah, on the authority of al-Ḥasan, ﴿of pitch﴾, meaning: al-khaṣkhāṣ, the mange-treatment of camels.
- Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Maʿmar, on the authority of al-Ḥasan, ﴿of pitch﴾, he said: the pitch of camels.

Some of them said: al-qiṭrān is copper.

Those who said that:

- al-Qāsim told us, he said: al-Ḥusayn told us, he said: Ḥajjāj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujāhid, he said: qiṭrān: copper. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn ʿAbbās said ﴿of pitch﴾: copper.

al-Qāsim told us, he said: al-Ḥusayn told us, he said: Abū Sufyān told us, on the authority of Maʿmar, on the authority of Qatādah, ﴿of pitch﴾, he said: it is copper. By this reading, I mean with fatḥa on the qāf and kasra on the ṭāʾ, and making all of that one word, all the readers of the amṣār read it so, and by it we read, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

It has been narrated from some earlier scholars that they used to read it: "min qaṭrin ānin", with fatḥa on the qāf, sukūn on the ṭāʾ, tanwīn on the rāʾ, and making ān an adjective of it, and directing the meaning of qaṭr to mean copper, and the meaning of ān to mean that whose heat has reached its intensity.

Among those who read it thus, as was mentioned to us, was ʿIkrimah, mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās; Aḥmad ibn Yūsuf narrated this to me, he said: al-Qāsim told us, he said: Hushaym told us, he said: Ḥuṣayn informed us, on his authority.

Those who interpreted it on this reading in the way I mentioned: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Yaʿqūb told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿīd, regarding His words "sarābīluhum min qaṭrin ānin", he said: qaṭr, and ān: that whose heat has reached its intensity.

- al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad told us, he said: Dāwūd ibn Mihrān told us, on the authority of Yaʿqūb, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, similarly.
- al-Muthannā told me, he said: Isḥāq told us, he said: Hishām told us, he said: Yaʿqūb al-Qummī told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿīd, similarly.
- al-Muthannā told me, he said: Isḥāq told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Ḥammād told us, he said: Yaʿqūb al-Qummī told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, that he used to read "sarābīluhum min qaṭrin ānin".
- al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad told us, he said: ʿAffān told us, he said: al-Mubārak ibn Faḍālah told us, he said: I heard al-Ḥasan say: The Arabs used to say of a thing when its heat had reached its intensity: "qad āna ḥarr hādhā" (the heat of this has reached its limit). "Jahannam has been kindled over it since it was created, so its heat has reached its limit."

The Jawharī said: al-natḥ is perspiration; manātiḥ al-ʿaraq are its exits from the skin, and he recited: "jawn..." etc. Al-qiṭrān (with fatḥa, with kasra, and like ẓarbān) is the resin of the pine, which is boiled and then camels are treated with it; and their garments were made of it because it greatly intensifies the fire in the skins (from Tāj al-ʿArūs). Al-masūḥ is the plural of misḥ, with kasra on the mīm, which is a garment of hair; its plurals are amsāḥ and masūḥ.]

with kasra on the qāf, and he also said:

"As if qiṭrān, when they follow it, the wind throws it toward its course." [This evidence is like the previous one, showing that qiṭrān has kasra on the qāf.]

with kasra.

Those who read it thus have said what we have said regarding it.

Those who said that:

- al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb told us, on the authority of Saʿīd, on the authority of Qatādah, on the authority of al-Ḥasan, ﴿of pitch﴾, meaning: al-khaṣkhāṣ, the mange-treatment of camels.
- Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Maʿmar, on the authority of al-Ḥasan, ﴿of pitch﴾, he said: the pitch of camels.

Some of them said: al-qiṭrān is copper.

Those who said that:

- al-Qāsim told us, he said: al-Ḥusayn told us, he said: Ḥajjāj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujāhid, he said: qiṭrān: copper. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn ʿAbbās said ﴿of pitch﴾: copper.

al-Qāsim told us, he said: al-Ḥusayn told us, he said: Abū Sufyān told us, on the authority of Maʿmar, on the authority of Qatādah, ﴿of pitch﴾, he said: it is copper. By this reading, I mean with fatḥa on the qāf and kasra on the ṭāʾ, and making all of that one word, all the readers of the amṣār read it so, and by it we read, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

It has been narrated from some earlier scholars that they used to read it: "min qaṭrin ānin", with fatḥa on the qāf, sukūn on the ṭāʾ, tanwīn on the rāʾ, and making ān an adjective of it, and directing the meaning of qaṭr to mean copper, and the meaning of ān to mean that whose heat has reached its intensity.

Among those who read it thus, as was mentioned to us, was ʿIkrimah, mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās; Aḥmad ibn Yūsuf narrated this to me, he said: al-Qāsim told us, he said: Hushaym told us, he said: Ḥuṣayn informed us, on his authority.

Those who interpreted it on this reading in the way I mentioned: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Yaʿqūb told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿīd, regarding His words "sarābīluhum min qaṭrin ānin", he said: qaṭr, and ān: that whose heat has reached its intensity.

- al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad told us, he said: Dāwūd ibn Mihrān told us, on the authority of Yaʿqūb, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, similarly.
- al-Muthannā told me, he said: Isḥāq told us, he said: Hishām told us, he said: Yaʿqūb al-Qummī told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿīd, similarly.
- al-Muthannā told me, he said: Isḥāq told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Ḥammād told us, he said: Yaʿqūb al-Qummī told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, that he used to read "sarābīluhum min qaṭrin ānin".
- al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad told us, he said: ʿAffān told us, he said: al-Mubārak ibn Faḍālah told us, he said: I heard al-Ḥasan say: The Arabs used to say of a thing when its heat had reached its intensity: "qad āna ḥarr hādhā" (the heat of this has reached its limit). "Jahannam has been kindled over it since it was created, so its heat has reached its limit."
- al-Muthannā told me, he said: Isḥāq told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿīd told us, he said: Abū Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, regarding His words "sarābīluhum min qaṭrin ānin", he said: al-qaṭr is copper, and ān: he says: its heat has reached its limit, for he says: "ḥamīmun ān" (boiling water that has reached its limit).
- al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad told us, he said: ʿAffān ibn Muslim told us, he said: Thābit ibn Yazīd told us, he said: Hilāl ibn Khabbāb told us, on the authority of ʿIkrimah, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding this verse "sarābīluhum min qaṭrin ānin", he said: of copper; ān: "it has come to them, that they should be punished with it."
- al-Muthannā told me, he said: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn told us, he said: Hushaym informed us, on the authority of Ḥuṣayn, on the authority of ʿIkrimah, regarding His words "min qaṭrin ānin", he said: the ānī is that whose heat has reached its limit.
- al-Muthannā told me, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiyah told me, on the authority of ʿAlī, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, His words: "min qaṭrin ānin", he said: it is molten copper.
- al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn ʿAṭāʾ told us, on the authority of Saʿīd, on the authority of Qatādah: "min qaṭrin ānin", meaning: molten ṣifr (brass).
- Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Qatādah: "sarābīluhum min qaṭrin ānin", he said: of copper.
- al-Muthannā told me, he said: Isḥāq told us, he said: Hishām told us, he said: Abū Ḥafṣ told us, on the authority of Hārūn, on the authority of Qatādah, that he used to read "min qaṭrin ānin", he said: of ṣafr (brass) whose heat has reached its limit.

And al-Ḥasan used to read it "min qaṭrin ānin".

* *

And His words ﴿and the Fire covers their faces﴾

He means: the Fire scorches their faces and burns them. ﴿So that Allah may recompense every soul for what it has earned﴾: He means: Allah did that to them as recompense for what they earned of sins in the world, so that He may reward every soul according to what it has earned of good and evil, rewarding the doer of good for his goodness and the evildoer for his evil. ﴿Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾: He means: Allah is knowing of the deed of every doer, so He has no need, in counting their deeds, for folding of the palm or effort; and He is swift in reckoning their deeds, having encompassed them in knowledge, nothing of them escaping Him, and He will recompense them for all of that, small and great.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 52:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿This is a message for mankind, that they may be warned thereby, and that they may know that He is but one God, and that those of understanding may take heed.﴾ (52)

He, dhikruhu (exalted is He), says: This Qur'an is a message for mankind, which Allah has conveyed to them as proof against them, and by which He has left them without excuse, through what He has sent down in it of admonitions and lessons. ﴿And that they may be warned thereby﴾ means: that they may be warned of the punishment of Allah and be cautious of His vengeance, which He sent down to His Prophet ﷺ. ﴿And that they may know that He is but one God﴾ means: and that they may know, through the proofs He has put forth against them in it, that He is one God, not many gods, as the polytheists who associate others with Allah say, and that there is no god but Him, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, who subjected to them the sun, the moon, the night and the day, sent down water from the sky and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for them, subjected to them the ship to run upon the sea by His command, and subjected to them the rivers. ﴿And that those of understanding may take heed﴾ means: and that those who possess intelligence and reason may be admonished and reflect upon the proofs Allah has set forth against them in this Qur'an, so that they desist from taking alongside Him another god and from associating with Him in worship anything else. For they are the people of reflection and remembrance, unlike those who have no intellect or understanding, who are like cattle, rather they are further astray in the way.

Similar to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿This is a message for mankind﴾, he said: the Qur'an. ﴿And that they may be warned thereby﴾, he said: by the Qur'an. ﴿And that they may know that He is but one God, and that those of understanding may take heed﴾.

End of the commentary on Surah Ibrahim, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
